cards.name: Jerusalem
cards.line: Jerusalem is the city David captured and made his capital, where the temple stood, where Jesus was welcomed as King, and where the Holy Spirit came upon the believers.

moments.title: David Takes the Fortress
moments.text: David marched against the Jebusites, who said he could never get in. He captured the fortress of Zion and called it the City of David, and he became greater because the LORD was with him.

moments.title: The Ark Comes to the Temple
moments.text: Solomon gathered Israel's leaders in Jerusalem to bring the ark of the covenant to the temple. The priests placed it in the Most Holy Place, and the glory of the LORD filled the house in a cloud.

moments.title: Babylon Destroys the City
moments.text: Nebuchadnezzar surrounded Jerusalem with his army and a siege wall. Later his captain burned the house of the LORD, the palace, and the houses, and the army broke down the city walls.

moments.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem
moments.text: Jesus rode toward Jerusalem on a donkey while crowds spread cloaks and branches and shouted, "Hosanna to the Son of David!" When He entered, the whole city was stirred and asked, "Who is this?"

moments.title: Peter Speaks at Pentecost
moments.text: God-fearing Jews from every nation were living in Jerusalem when the Holy Spirit filled the believers. Each person heard them in his own language, and Peter stood up and spoke to the crowd.

cards.name: Egypt
cards.line: Egypt is the land of the Nile, where Joseph rose to power, Jacob's family grew into a nation, and God later brought Israel out.

moments.title: Joseph Sold to Potiphar
moments.text: Joseph's brothers sold him to traders who took him to Egypt. There the Midianites sold him to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh.

moments.title: Joseph Placed Over Egypt
moments.text: Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of all the land of Egypt. Joseph then stored up food in the cities during the seven years of plenty.

moments.title: Jacob's Family Goes to Egypt
moments.text: God told Jacob not to be afraid to go down to Egypt, and promised to make his family a great nation there. Jacob and all his descendants then went to Egypt.

moments.title: The Midwives Fear God
moments.text: A new king who did not know Joseph came to power. He ordered the Hebrew midwives to kill baby boys, but they feared God and let the boys live.

moments.title: The Exodus
moments.text: At midnight the LORD struck down every firstborn male in the land of Egypt, from Pharaoh's firstborn to the prisoner's, and the firstborn of the livestock too. The Egyptians urged the Israelites to leave, and after 430 years the LORD's divisions went out of Egypt.

cards.name: Mount Sinai
cards.line: Mount Sinai, also called Horeb, is the mountain of God where Moses met God in a burning bush and where God gave Israel the tablets of the Testimony.

moments.title: The burning bush
moments.text: Moses led his flock to Horeb, the mountain of God. There God spoke to him from a bush that blazed but did not burn up, and He sent Moses to bring His people out of Egypt.

moments.title: God comes down in fire
moments.text: The LORD came down on Mount Sinai in fire and smoke, and the whole mountain shook. He called Moses up to the top, and the people stood at the foot of the mountain.

moments.title: The tablets of stone
moments.text: When the LORD finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him the two tablets of the Testimony. They were stone tablets written by the finger of God.

moments.title: The golden calf
moments.text: The psalm says that at Horeb the people made a calf and worshiped it, and they forgot God their Savior. God said He would destroy them, but Moses stood before Him and turned His wrath away.

moments.title: Moses' shining face
moments.text: Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets, and his face was radiant from speaking with the LORD. The people were afraid, and then Moses told them everything the LORD had said to him.

cards.name: Bethlehem
cards.line: Bethlehem is a town in Judah, also called Ephrath, near where Rachel was buried, where David's story began, and where a ruler for Israel was to come from.

moments.title: Rachel is buried
moments.text: Rachel died on the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and was buried there on the way. Jacob set up a pillar on her grave.

moments.title: Naomi and Ruth arrive
moments.text: Naomi came back from Moab with her daughter-in-law Ruth. They arrived in Bethlehem at the start of the barley harvest.

moments.title: Samuel visits Jesse
moments.text: Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. The elders trembled and asked if he came in peace, and he said he came to sacrifice to the LORD.

moments.title: Water from the well
moments.text: David longed for water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem. Three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp to get it, but David poured it out to the LORD.

moments.title: Jesus is born in Bethlehem
moments.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, during the time of King Herod. The prophet had written that a ruler who would shepherd God's people Israel would come out of Bethlehem.

cards.name: Golgotha
cards.line: Golgotha, meaning The Place of the Skull, was the well-known spot near Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified between two robbers.

moments.title: Jesus arrives at Golgotha
moments.text: Soldiers took Jesus away, and He went out carrying His own cross to Golgotha. Along the way, they forced Simon of Cyrene to carry the cross of Jesus.

moments.title: Wine offered and garments divided
moments.text: They offered Jesus wine mixed with gall, but after tasting it He refused to drink. The soldiers divided His garments by casting lots and sat down to keep watch over Him.

moments.title: Jesus is crucified
moments.text: At Golgotha they crucified Jesus, and with Him two robbers, one on His right and one on His left. A sign over His head called Him the King of the Jews.

cards.name: Skull
cards.line: The Skull is the place outside Jerusalem's walls where Jesus was crucified between two criminals, as told in Luke's account of His death.

moments.title: Jesus is crucified
moments.text: At the place called The Skull, they crucified Jesus with two criminals, one on His right and one on His left. Jesus said, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing."

cards.name: Jordan
cards.line: The Jordan is the main river of the land of Israel, where God opened the water for His people and where Jesus was baptized.

moments.title: Israel Crosses on Dry Ground
moments.text: When the priests carrying the ark touched the Jordan, the flowing water stood still. All Israel crossed on dry ground near Jericho.

moments.title: Twelve Stones from the River
moments.text: The LORD told Joshua to have twelve men, one from each tribe, take stones from the middle of the Jordan. The stones were a memorial of how the waters were cut off.

moments.title: Elisha Takes Up the Cloak
moments.text: After Elijah went up into heaven, Elisha picked up Elijah's cloak and struck the Jordan. The waters parted and he crossed over.

moments.title: Naaman Washes and Is Healed
moments.text: Elisha told Naaman to wash seven times in the Jordan. Naaman did it, and his flesh was restored like that of a little child.

moments.title: Jesus Is Baptized
moments.text: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John. The Spirit of God came down like a dove, and a voice from heaven called Him God's beloved Son.

cards.name: Babylon
cards.line: Babylon was a great city on the Euphrates and the capital of Nebuchadnezzar's empire, where many people of Judah were taken into exile.

moments.title: Jehoiachin Taken to Babylon
moments.text: Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem, and King Jehoiachin surrendered. Nebuchadnezzar carried Jehoiachin, the king's family, officials, and leading men into exile in Babylon.

moments.title: Zedekiah Taken to Babylon
moments.text: After the Chaldeans seized King Zedekiah, they killed his sons before his eyes. Then they put out his eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.

moments.title: A Letter to the Exiles
moments.text: Jeremiah sent a letter to the exiles Nebuchadnezzar had carried from Jerusalem to Babylon. In it the LORD said that when Babylon's seventy years were complete, He would restore them to their home.

moments.title: Daniel Pleads for the Wise Men
moments.text: The king was so angry that he ordered all the wise men of Babylon destroyed. Daniel answered with tact, asked his friends to plead for God's mercy, and then asked Arioch not to execute the wise men.

cards.name: Canaan
cards.line: Canaan is the land west of the Jordan that God promised to Abraham's family as an eternal possession, and it is where much of Israel's story takes place.

moments.title: Abram Arrives in Canaan
moments.text: Abram takes Sarai, Lot, and all their people and goods and sets out for Canaan. There the LORD appears and says He will give this land to Abram's offspring, and Abram builds an altar.

moments.title: God Promises the Land
moments.text: God makes His covenant with Abraham. He promises to give Abraham and his descendants all the land of Canaan as an eternal possession, and to be their God.

moments.title: Sarah Dies in Canaan
moments.text: Sarah dies in Hebron in the land of Canaan, and Abraham mourns and weeps for her. He then asks the Hittites for a burial site.

moments.title: Spies Explore Canaan
moments.text: Moses sends one leader from each tribe to spy out Canaan. They travel through the Negev and the hill country, and at the Valley of Eshcol they cut a huge cluster of grapes.

moments.title: Manna Stops
moments.text: At Gilgal, the Israelites keep the Passover and eat from the produce of the land. The day after, the manna stops, and that year they eat the crops of Canaan.

cards.name: Jericho
cards.line: Jericho was a strong, walled city in the Jordan valley, the first city Israel faced in Canaan, and later a place where Elisha and Jesus were found.

moments.title: Spies Hidden by Rahab
moments.text: Joshua sent two spies to look over Jericho. The king of Jericho heard about them, but Rahab hid them on her roof and sent the king's men the wrong way.

moments.title: The Commander of the LORD's Army
moments.text: Near Jericho, Joshua saw a man with a drawn sword. He said He was Commander of the LORD's army and told Joshua to take off his sandals, because the place was holy.

moments.title: Marching Around the City
moments.text: Jericho was tightly shut up because of Israel. The LORD told Joshua He had delivered the city into his hand, and the people marched around it with the ark and seven priests blowing rams' horns.

moments.title: Elisha Stays with Elijah
moments.text: Elijah told Elisha to stay behind, but Elisha would not leave him. At Jericho the sons of the prophets told Elisha that the LORD would take his master that day, and later they bowed to him when they saw that Elijah's spirit rested on him.

moments.title: Jesus Meets Zacchaeus
moments.text: Jesus passed through Jericho and called Zacchaeus, a wealthy chief tax collector, down from a sycamore tree to stay at his house. Jesus said the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

cards.name: Rome
cards.line: Rome was the great capital of the empire in New Testament times, and the city where Paul came as a prisoner to preach the gospel.

moments.title: Jews Ordered Out of Rome
moments.text: Claudius ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Aquila and his wife Priscilla were among those who left Italy, and Paul later met them in Corinth.

moments.title: Paul Told to Go to Rome
moments.text: The Lord stood near Paul at night and told him to take courage. As Paul had testified about the Lord in Jerusalem, so he must testify in Rome.

moments.title: Welcomed by Brothers
moments.text: Believers heard Paul was coming and met him on the road. Paul was encouraged and thanked God, and then he came into Rome.

moments.title: Paul Stays Under Guard
moments.text: In Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him. After three days he called the Jewish leaders together and told them he was bound with a chain because of the hope of Israel.

cards.name: Nazareth
cards.line: Nazareth was a town in Galilee where Mary lived and Jesus grew up, and where the people drove Him out after He spoke in the synagogue.

moments.title: Gabriel Visits Mary
moments.text: God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary, a virgin pledged to Joseph. He told her she would bear a Son named Jesus, and Mary answered, "I am the Lord's servant."

moments.title: Joseph Settles Here
moments.text: After an angel told Joseph in a dream to leave Egypt, he feared Archelaus. Warned in a dream, he took the Child and His mother to live in Nazareth.

moments.title: Jesus Grows Up
moments.text: Jesus' parents returned to their own town of Nazareth, and the Child grew strong and wise. After He was found in the temple at twelve, He went down to Nazareth and was obedient to them.

moments.title: Jesus Reads Isaiah
moments.text: On the Sabbath Jesus stood in the synagogue, read from Isaiah, and said, "Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing." The people grew enraged and drove Him out of town to throw Him off a cliff.

cards.name: Sodom
cards.line: Sodom was a wicked city on the well-watered plain of the Jordan, where Lot made his home and which God destroyed with sulfur and fire.

moments.title: Lot Settles Near Sodom
moments.text: Lot looked over the well-watered plain and chose it for himself. He pitched his tent toward Sodom, though its men were wicked and sinned greatly against the LORD.

moments.title: Lot Is Carried Off
moments.text: Four kings seized the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah. They also carried off Lot and his possessions, since he was living in Sodom.

moments.title: Angels Visit Lot
moments.text: Two angels came to Sodom, and Lot welcomed them into his house. That night the men of the city surrounded the house, and the angels struck them with blindness.

moments.title: Sodom Destroyed
moments.text: The LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah from the heavens. Abraham saw smoke rising like smoke from a furnace, and God remembered him and brought Lot out.

cards.name: Red Sea
cards.line: The Red Sea is the sea where the LORD defeated Pharaoh's army and set Israel free, leading to a song of praise.

moments.title: Led Toward the Red Sea
moments.text: God led the people around by the way of the wilderness toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt arrayed for battle.

moments.title: Pharaoh's Army Drowns
moments.text: Moses and the Israelites sang that the LORD had thrown Pharaoh's chariots and army into the sea. His finest officers were drowned in the Red Sea.

moments.title: Leaving the Sea for the Desert
moments.text: Moses led Israel away from the Red Sea into the Desert of Shur. They walked three days without finding water.

cards.name: Nineveh
cards.line: Nineveh was the great city of Assyria, where God sent Jonah to preach, and its people turned from their evil and God spared them.

moments.title: Jonah preaches in the city
moments.text: Jonah obeys the second time. He walks into Nineveh and announces that in forty more days the city will be overturned.

moments.title: Nineveh turns to God
moments.text: The Ninevites believe God and fast, and the king sits in ashes and calls everyone to turn from evil. When God sees this, He decides not to bring the disaster He threatened.

cards.name: Sea of Galilee
cards.line: The Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Tiberias, is a lake where Jesus called fishermen to follow Him, healed many people, and met His disciples.

moments.title: Fishers of Men
moments.text: Jesus walked beside the sea and saw fishermen casting nets and mending them. He called Peter, Andrew, James, and John, and they left their nets and boat and followed Him.

moments.title: Healing Along the Shore
moments.text: Jesus went along the Sea of Galilee and up on a mountain. Large crowds laid the lame, blind, crippled, and mute at His feet, and He healed them.

moments.title: Crowd Near the Sea
moments.text: Jesus crossed the Sea of Galilee, and a large crowd followed Him because of the signs He did for the sick. He asked Philip where to buy bread for them.

moments.title: Jesus Appears at Dawn
moments.text: After a night of catching nothing, the disciples saw Jesus standing on the shore, though they did not know Him. At His word they cast the net on the right side and caught so many fish they could not haul it in.

cards.name: Gethsemane
cards.line: Gethsemane is a place near Jerusalem where Jesus went with His disciples to pray, and where He faced deep sorrow before His death.

moments.title: Jesus prays in sorrow
moments.text: Jesus tells His disciples to sit while He prays. He takes Peter, James, and John with Him, and says His soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death.

moments.title: Not My will, but Yours
moments.text: Jesus falls facedown and asks His Father to take the cup from Him. Then He says, "Yet not as I will, but as You will."

moments.title: The disciples fall asleep
moments.text: Jesus returns and finds His disciples sleeping. He asks them to watch and pray, because the spirit is willing but the body is weak.

cards.name: Mount Zion
cards.line: Mount Zion is the hill in Jerusalem that David captured from the Jebusites and made his city, and later the name is used for God's people and the heavenly city.

moments.title: David captures the fortress
moments.text: The Jebusites said David could never get in, but David captured the fortress of Zion. He lived there and called it the City of David.

moments.title: The ark is brought up
moments.text: Solomon gathered Israel's leaders to bring the ark of the covenant up from Zion, the City of David. The priests set it in the temple, and the glory of the LORD filled the house.

moments.title: The Lamb on Mount Zion
moments.text: John saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion. With Him were 144,000 who had His name and His Father's name written on their foreheads.

cards.name: Assyria
cards.line: Assyria was a strong empire north of Babylonia along the Tigris River, whose kings attacked Israel and Judah and carried the Israelites away from their land.

moments.title: Israelites Taken to Assyria
moments.text: The king of Assyria surrounded Samaria for three years and then captured it. He carried the Israelites away to Assyria and settled them in Halah, Gozan, and the cities of the Medes.

cards.name: Galilee
cards.line: Galilee is the northern region of Israel where Jesus grew up, taught, and healed, and where He later met His disciples and sent them to all nations.

moments.title: Gabriel comes to Nazareth
moments.text: God sent the angel Gabriel to Mary, a virgin in the Galilean town of Nazareth. He told her she would give birth to Jesus, the Son of the Most High, and Mary answered, "I am the Lord's servant."

moments.title: The first sign at Cana
moments.text: At a wedding in Cana in Galilee, the wine ran out. Jesus turned water in stone jars into wine, and His disciples believed in Him.

moments.title: Teaching and healing across Galilee
moments.text: Jesus went throughout Galilee teaching in the synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness. Large crowds followed Him, including people from Galilee.

moments.title: Authority at Capernaum
moments.text: In Capernaum, a town in Galilee, Jesus taught on the Sabbath and people were astonished. He commanded an unclean spirit to come out of a man, and the news spread through the region.

moments.title: The mountain in Galilee
moments.text: The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had chosen. There they worshiped Him, and He told them to make disciples of all nations and promised to be with them always.

cards.name: Corinth
cards.line: Corinth was a wealthy Greek city where Paul stayed to teach about Jesus and started a church, and he later wrote two letters to the believers there.

moments.title: Paul Arrives in Corinth
moments.text: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth. There he met Aquila and Priscilla, who were tentmakers like him, and he stayed and worked with them.

moments.title: Paul Turns to the Gentiles
moments.text: Every Sabbath Paul reasoned in the synagogue, and after Silas and Timothy came he testified that Jesus is the Christ. When people opposed and insulted him, he left and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

moments.title: Apollos in Corinth
moments.text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples who had not heard of the Holy Spirit, and they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

cards.name: Bethel
cards.line: Bethel, once called Luz, was a city in Canaan where Jacob met God in a dream and named the place "house of God."

moments.title: Jacob's dream
moments.text: On his way to Haran, Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, and the LORD promised him land and descendants. Jacob named the place Bethel, which had been called Luz.

moments.title: Jacob returns to Bethel
moments.text: God told Jacob to go up to Bethel and build an altar. Jacob had his household put away foreign gods, then built the altar there and called the place El-bethel.

moments.title: Israel weeps and asks God
moments.text: In the war against Benjamin, the Israelites went up to Bethel to ask God who should fight first. After a hard defeat, they wept, fasted, and offered sacrifices there, and the LORD told them to fight.

moments.title: Jeroboam's golden calf
moments.text: King Jeroboam made two golden calves and set one up in Bethel. He also ordained a feast, made offerings on an altar there, and appointed priests for the high places.

moments.title: A man of God speaks against the altar
moments.text: A man of God from Judah came to Bethel by the LORD's word and cried out against Jeroboam's altar. When the king stretched out his hand and ordered, "Seize him!", his hand withered, and the altar split apart.

cards.name: Damascus
cards.line: Damascus is an ancient, important city of Syria, north of Jerusalem, where Elisha spoke to Hazael, Assyria conquered it, and Saul began to preach about Jesus.

moments.title: Elisha and Hazael
moments.text: Elisha came to Damascus while King Ben-hadad was sick. Hazael brought a gift and asked if the king would recover, and Elisha said the LORD had shown him that Hazael would be king over Aram.

moments.title: Assyria captures Damascus
moments.text: King Ahaz of Judah asked Assyria for help. The king of Assyria marched up to Damascus and captured it, took its people to Kir, and put Rezin to death.

moments.title: Ahaz copies an altar
moments.text: Ahaz went to Damascus to meet the king of Assyria and saw an altar there. He sent plans for it to Uriah the priest, who built one, and Ahaz made offerings on it.

moments.title: Saul meets Jesus
moments.text: As Saul drew near to Damascus to arrest followers of the Way, a light from heaven flashed around him and Jesus spoke to him. Saul was left blind and was led by the hand into Damascus.

moments.title: Ananias helps Saul
moments.text: The Lord sent a disciple named Ananias to Saul in Damascus. Ananias placed his hands on him, Saul could see again and was baptized, and he stayed several days with the disciples.

cards.name: Mount Carmel
cards.line: Mount Carmel is a mountain ridge by the Mediterranean Sea, best known as the place where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal and the LORD answered by fire.

moments.title: Elijah and the prophets of Baal
moments.text: Elijah asked Ahab to gather all Israel and the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. He told the people to follow the LORD if He is God, and the God who answers by fire is God.

moments.title: Elijah and the small cloud
moments.text: Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel and bent down with his face between his knees. His servant looked toward the sea, and on the seventh time saw a small cloud, and then heavy rain came.

moments.title: The Shunammite woman seeks Elisha
moments.text: The Shunammite woman went to the man of God at Mount Carmel, and Elisha sent Gehazi to meet her when he saw her coming. She clung to Elisha's feet.

cards.name: Ephesus
cards.line: Ephesus was a major city of the province of Asia, home to the temple of Artemis, where Paul taught for about two years and the gospel spread widely.

moments.title: Paul's short first visit
moments.text: Paul stopped at Ephesus and reasoned with the Jews in the synagogue. When they asked him to stay longer, he declined, promising to return if God was willing.

moments.title: Apollos is taught more fully
moments.text: Apollos, a skilled speaker who knew the Scriptures, came to Ephesus and spoke boldly. Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God more accurately.

moments.title: The Holy Spirit comes on disciples
moments.text: Paul found about twelve disciples who knew only John's baptism. They were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them.

moments.title: The riot over Artemis
moments.text: Demetrius the silversmith stirred up the craftsmen, who feared Paul's teaching would hurt their business and the temple of Artemis. The crowd rushed into the theatre shouting until the city clerk quieted them.

moments.title: Paul sends for the elders
moments.text: Paul decided to sail past Ephesus because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem. From nearby Miletus he sent for the elders of the Ephesian church, and they came to him.

cards.name: Beersheba
cards.line: Beersheba is a city in the south of the land where Abraham and Isaac each made an oath with Abimelech, and where God spoke to Isaac and Jacob.

moments.title: Abraham and Abimelech swear an oath
moments.text: Abraham and Abimelech made a covenant over a well, and the place was named Beersheba because they swore an oath there. Abraham planted a tamarisk tree and called on the LORD, the Eternal God.

moments.title: The LORD appears to Isaac
moments.text: Isaac went up to Beersheba, and that night the LORD told him not to be afraid because He was with him. Isaac built an altar there and his servants dug a well.

moments.title: Isaac's oath and the well
moments.text: Abimelech came to Isaac and they swore an oath of peace. That same day Isaac's servants found water, and the city's name stayed Beersheba.

moments.title: Jacob stops on the way to Egypt
moments.text: Israel offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac at Beersheba. God told him not to fear going down to Egypt, and then Jacob left Beersheba.

moments.title: Elijah runs away
moments.text: Elijah was afraid of Jezebel and ran for his life. At Beersheba in Judah he left his servant there and went on into the wilderness.

cards.name: Mount of Olives
cards.line: The Mount of Olives is a ridge east of Jerusalem where David wept, Jesus prayed and rode toward the city, and the LORD will one day stand.

moments.title: David weeps and climbs
moments.text: David climbed the Mount of Olives weeping, with his head covered and his feet bare. All the people with him covered their heads and wept too.

moments.title: The LORD will stand here
moments.text: Zechariah says that on that day the LORD's feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The mountain will split in two, forming a great valley.

moments.title: Jesus sends for a donkey
moments.text: Near Jerusalem, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples to bring a colt. As He rode, the crowd praised God for the miracles they had seen, and called Him the King who comes in the Lord's name.

moments.title: A hymn, then the mountain
moments.text: After the Last Supper, Jesus and His disciples sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives. There Jesus said they would all fall away, and Peter said he never would.

moments.title: Jesus prays on the mountain
moments.text: Jesus went to the Mount of Olives as usual. He knelt and prayed, "Not My will, but Yours be done," and an angel strengthened Him.

cards.name: Gomorrah
cards.line: Gomorrah was a city of the plain near Sodom, and God destroyed it with fire for its great sin, so the Bible uses it as a warning.

moments.title: Goods Taken from Gomorrah
moments.text: As the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some men fell into tar pits. The four enemy kings took all the goods and food of Sodom and Gomorrah and went on their way.

moments.title: Fire from Heaven
moments.text: The LORD rained sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. He destroyed the cities, the whole plain, and everyone and everything in them.

cards.name: Nile
cards.line: The Nile is the great river of Egypt, where Pharaoh dreamed, Hebrew baby boys were threatened, and God showed His power through plagues.

moments.title: Pharaoh's dream by the river
moments.text: Pharaoh dreamed he stood beside the Nile. Seven healthy cows came up from the river, followed by seven thin, sickly cows that ate them.

moments.title: Pharaoh's cruel order
moments.text: Pharaoh commanded his people to throw every Hebrew baby boy into the Nile. Every daughter was allowed to live.

moments.title: The Nile turns to blood
moments.text: God told Moses to meet Pharaoh on the bank of the Nile. Aaron struck the water with the staff, and the river turned to blood, so the fish died and the Egyptians could not drink.

moments.title: Frogs from the Nile
moments.text: God said the Nile would teem with frogs that would come into Pharaoh's palace and homes. When Moses prayed, the frogs in the houses, courtyards, and fields died, and frogs stayed only in the Nile.

cards.name: Capernaum
cards.line: Capernaum was a city by the Sea of Galilee where Jesus made His home after leaving Nazareth, and where He taught and healed.

moments.title: Jesus makes His home here
moments.text: After leaving Nazareth, Jesus went to live in Capernaum by the sea. Matthew says this fulfilled Isaiah's words about a great light dawning for people in darkness.

moments.title: The centurion's great faith
moments.text: A centurion asked Jesus to heal his paralyzed servant and said Jesus only needed to say the word. Jesus marveled at his faith, and the servant was healed at that very hour.

moments.title: Teaching with authority
moments.text: On the Sabbath Jesus taught in the synagogue, and the people were astonished. He told an unclean spirit to come out of a man, and it obeyed.

moments.title: Who is the greatest?
moments.text: In a house in Capernaum, Jesus asked the disciples what they had argued about on the way. He taught that whoever wants to be first must be the servant of all, and He held a little child in His arms.

moments.title: The bread of life teaching
moments.text: Jesus taught in the synagogue about the bread that came down from heaven. Many disciples turned back, but Peter said Jesus has the words of eternal life.

cards.name: Bethany
cards.line: Bethany was a village about two miles east of Jerusalem, the home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, where Jesus often visited in His last days.

moments.title: Lazarus is sick
moments.text: Lazarus lived in Bethany with his sisters Mary and Martha. The sisters sent word to Jesus that the one He loved was sick, and Jesus said the sickness was for the glory of God.

moments.title: A night away from the city
moments.text: After the children praised Him in Jerusalem, Jesus left the city and went out to Bethany, where He spent the night.

moments.title: Dinner at Bethany
moments.text: Six days before the Passover, a dinner was held for Jesus. Mary anointed His feet with expensive perfume, and Jesus said she had kept it for the day of His burial.

moments.title: A woman anoints Jesus
moments.text: At Simon the Leper's home, a woman poured perfume on Jesus' head. Some scolded her, but Jesus called it a beautiful deed done to anoint His body for burial.

moments.title: Jesus blesses His followers
moments.text: Jesus led His followers out as far as Bethany and lifted up His hands to bless them. While He was blessing them, He was carried up into heaven.

cards.name: Athens
cards.line: Athens was a famous Greek city full of idols, where Paul reasoned with philosophers and told the Athenians about the God who made the world.

moments.title: Paul sees the idols
moments.text: Paul waits in Athens for Silas and Timothy. He is deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city is full of idols.

moments.title: Paul speaks at the Areopagus
moments.text: Philosophers bring Paul to the Areopagus to explain his new teaching. He tells them about an altar TO AN UNKNOWN GOD and proclaims the God who made the world and gives everyone life and breath. Some believe.

moments.title: Paul sends Timothy to Thessalonica
moments.text: Paul writes that when they could bear it no longer, they were willing to be left on their own in Athens. They sent Timothy to strengthen and encourage the believers in their faith.

moments.title: Paul leaves for Corinth
moments.text: After this, Paul leaves Athens and goes to Corinth.

cards.name: Patmos
cards.line: Patmos is a small, rocky island in the Aegean Sea where John was living when he received the vision written down in the book of Revelation.

moments.title: John on Patmos
moments.text: John calls himself a brother and partner in the troubles, the kingdom, and the patient endurance found in Jesus. He says he was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and his testimony about Jesus.

moments.title: A voice like a trumpet
moments.text: On the Lord's day, John was in the Spirit and heard a loud voice behind him like a trumpet. It told him to write what he saw and send it to seven churches.

moments.title: One like the Son of Man
moments.text: After John heard the voice on Patmos, he turned and saw seven golden lampstands. Among them stood One like the Son of Man, with white hair, eyes like blazing fire, and a voice like the roar of many waters.

cards.name: Babel
cards.line: Babel was a city in the land of Shinar where the LORD confused the language of the whole world and scattered people across the earth.

moments.title: Nimrod's kingdom begins
moments.text: Nimrod, a mighty hunter before the LORD, had a kingdom that began in Babylon and other cities in the land of Shinar.

moments.title: The LORD scatters the people
moments.text: The LORD scattered the people over all the earth, and they stopped building the city. He confused the language of the whole world there, which is why it is called Babel.

cards.name: Emmaus
cards.line: Emmaus was a village about seven miles from Jerusalem, where two disciples were headed when the risen Jesus joined them on the road on the day of His resurrection.

moments.title: Two disciples bound for Emmaus
moments.text: On the day Jesus rose, two of His followers were going to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem. They talked with each other about everything that had happened.

cards.name: Armageddon
cards.line: Armageddon is the Hebrew name of a place where kings are gathered in Revelation, linked to the great day of God's judgment.

moments.title: Kings gather
moments.text: The kings are assembled in the place called Armageddon in Hebrew.

cards.name: Moab
cards.line: Moab is a region east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, where Israel made its last camp before Canaan and where Moses died.

moments.title: Balak Fears Israel
moments.text: Israel camped in the plains of Moab, and Moab was terrified because the people were so many. King Balak sent for Balaam to curse Israel, but God told Balaam not to go, because Israel was blessed.

moments.title: Sin at Shittim
moments.text: While Israel stayed in Shittim, the men joined the daughters of Moab in sin and bowed down to their gods. The LORD's anger burned, and a plague killed 24,000 people.

moments.title: Moses Explains the Law
moments.text: On the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, the LORD's commandments were given to Israel through Moses. In the land of Moab, east of the Jordan, Moses began to explain this law to the people.

moments.title: Moses Dies
moments.text: Moses climbed from the plains of Moab up Mount Nebo, where the LORD showed him the promised land. He died there in Moab, and the Israelites mourned him for thirty days.

cards.name: Samaria
cards.line: Samaria was a region in the heart of Israel, named for the hill Omri bought and built into his capital city, and it fell to Assyria.

moments.title: Omri builds Samaria
moments.text: Omri paid Shemer two talents of silver for the hill of Samaria and built a city on it. He named the city after Shemer, who had owned the hill.

moments.title: Ahab's temple of Baal
moments.text: Ahab became king and reigned in Samaria twenty-two years. He married Jezebel and built a temple for Baal in Samaria, where he set up an altar for Baal.

moments.title: Blind soldiers led to Samaria
moments.text: Elisha prayed and the LORD struck the Aramean soldiers with blindness. Elisha led them into Samaria, where the LORD opened their eyes, and the king fed them and sent them home.

moments.title: Famine under siege
moments.text: Ben-hadad of Aram marched up with his whole army and besieged Samaria, and a great famine followed. Food became so costly that a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver.

moments.title: Assyria captures Samaria
moments.text: Assyria's king besieged Samaria for three years and then captured it. He carried the Israelites away to Assyria because they had sinned against the LORD.

cards.name: Judea
cards.line: Judea was the southernmost region of Palestine in Jesus' day, where Jesus was born, John preached in the wilderness, and the church was first scattered.

moments.title: Jesus born in Judea
moments.text: Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea during the time of King Herod. Wise men from the east, called Magi, came to Jerusalem asking where the newborn King of the Jews was.

moments.title: John preaches in the wilderness
moments.text: John the Baptist preached in the wilderness of Judea, telling people to turn away from their sins because God's kingdom was near. People from Jerusalem and all Judea went out to him, confessed their sins, and were baptized in the Jordan River.

moments.title: Time in the Judean countryside
moments.text: Jesus and His disciples went into the Judean countryside, where He spent some time with them and baptized. John's disciples heard that people were going to Jesus.

moments.title: Jesus warns people in Judea to flee
moments.text: Jesus said that when Jerusalem was surrounded by armies, those in Judea should flee to the mountains.

moments.title: The church is scattered
moments.text: After Stephen's death, a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem. All except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria, and they preached the word wherever they went.

cards.name: Lebanon
cards.line: Lebanon is a mountain region north of Israel, famous for its cedar trees, which Solomon and later the returning exiles used to build God's temple.

moments.title: Solomon asks for cedars
moments.text: Solomon asks King Hiram of Tyre to have cedars of Lebanon cut for the Lord's house. Hiram says his servants will haul the logs from Lebanon to the sea, and he provides the timber Solomon wants.

moments.title: Israelite workers sent to Lebanon
moments.text: Solomon sends 10,000 men at a time to Lebanon in monthly shifts. They spend one month there and two months at home.

moments.title: Cedar for the second temple
moments.text: The returned exiles pay people of Sidon and Tyre to bring cedar logs from Lebanon to Joppa by sea. Cyrus king of Persia had authorized this.

cards.name: Tyre
cards.line: Tyre was a rich port city on the Mediterranean coast whose king Hiram was a friend to David and Solomon, and Paul's ship stopped there.

moments.title: Hiram sends help to David
moments.text: Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons. They built a palace for David.

moments.title: Hiram hears about Solomon
moments.text: When Hiram king of Tyre heard that Solomon was king, he sent messengers to him, for Hiram had always been a friend of David. Hiram later agreed to send cedar for the house of the LORD.

moments.title: Tyre cheers at Jerusalem's fall
moments.text: Tyre said 'Aha!' about Jerusalem lying in ruins. The Lord GOD said He was against Tyre and would bring Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon and many nations against its walls and towers.

moments.title: Jesus names Tyre
moments.text: Jesus said that if the miracles done in Chorazin and Bethsaida had been done in Tyre and Sidon, their people would have turned from their sins long ago. He said it would be easier for Tyre on the day of judgment.

moments.title: Paul visits the disciples
moments.text: Paul's ship landed at Tyre to unload its cargo. Paul and his companions stayed seven days with the disciples, who prayed with them on the beach before they sailed on.

cards.name: Euphrates
cards.line: The Euphrates is the great river of western Asia, where Jacob crossed, armies fought, and a prophet's scroll was sunk to show Babylon's fall.

moments.title: Jacob Flees Laban
moments.text: Jacob left Laban in secret with his family and all his possessions. He crossed the Euphrates and headed for the hill country of Gilead.

moments.title: Josiah Goes Out to Meet Neco
moments.text: Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah went out to meet him. Neco said God had told him to hurry, but Josiah did not listen.

moments.title: The Ruined Loincloth
moments.text: The LORD told Jeremiah to hide a linen loincloth in a crevice of the rocks at Perath, which some sources say is the Euphrates. Many days later he dug it up, and it was ruined and of no use at all.

moments.title: Egypt Defeated at Carchemish
moments.text: The LORD spoke about Pharaoh Neco's army, which Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates. The warriors stumbled and fell by the river in the north.

moments.title: A Scroll Sunk in the River
moments.text: Jeremiah told Seraiah to read a scroll about Babylon's coming disaster aloud in Babylon. Then he was to tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates, showing that Babylon will sink and never rise again.

cards.name: Hebron
cards.line: Hebron is an ancient city in Judah's hill country where Abraham lived and buried Sarah, which became Caleb's inheritance, and where David first became king.

moments.title: Abram Settles at Hebron
moments.text: Abram moved his tent to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron. There he built an altar to the LORD.

moments.title: Sarah Dies at Hebron
moments.text: Sarah died in Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron. Abraham mourned for her and then asked the Hittites for a burial site.

moments.title: Hebron Given to Caleb
moments.text: Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him Hebron as his inheritance. It still belonged to Caleb's family because he wholly followed the LORD.

moments.title: David Made King of Judah
moments.text: David asked the LORD where to go, and the LORD said, "To Hebron." The men of Judah came there and anointed him king over Judah.

moments.title: David Made King of Israel
moments.text: All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron. The elders made a covenant with him before the LORD and anointed him king over Israel.

cards.name: Persia
cards.line: Persia was a vast empire, from a homeland by the Persian Gulf, whose kings ruled Babylon and Jerusalem and let God's people go home to rebuild the temple.

moments.title: Cyrus sends the people home
moments.text: The LORD stirred the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia. He sent a message through his kingdom, written down, that God's people could go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the LORD.

moments.title: Temple work stops
moments.text: The building of God's house in Jerusalem stopped. It stayed stopped until the second year of Darius king of Persia.

moments.title: The temple is finished
moments.text: The Jewish elders built and did well as the prophets Haggai and Zechariah spoke God's word. They finished the house by God's command and the orders of the Persian kings.

moments.title: Ezra goes up to Jerusalem
moments.text: During the reign of Artaxerxes king of Persia, Ezra, a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, went up from Babylon to Jerusalem. The hand of his God was upon him.

moments.title: A message for Daniel
moments.text: In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, Daniel received a true message in a vision. A heavenly messenger said the prince of Persia opposed him for twenty-one days until Michael came to help.

cards.name: Gath
cards.line: Gath was one of the five royal Philistine cities and the home of the giant Goliath, where the ark brought trouble and David hid from Saul.

moments.title: The ark sent to Gath
moments.text: The Philistines of Ashdod moved the ark of the God of Israel to Gath. The LORD's hand was against that city, and its people, young and old, were struck with tumors.

moments.title: David pretends to be mad
moments.text: David ran from Saul to Achish, king of Gath. Afraid when Achish's servants spoke of his victories, David acted insane, and Achish wanted nothing to do with him.

moments.title: David lives in Gath
moments.text: David went to Achish with his six hundred men and their families, and they settled in Gath. When Saul heard David was there, he stopped searching for him.

moments.title: A giant killed at Gath
moments.text: In a battle at Gath, a huge man with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot taunted Israel. Jonathan, David's nephew, killed him.

moments.title: Shimei goes to Gath
moments.text: Shimei had been told by Solomon never to leave Jerusalem. When his slaves ran away to Gath, he went there to bring them back, and so broke the king's command.

cards.name: Gibeon
cards.line: Gibeon was a great hill city of the Hivites that tricked Israel into a peace treaty, and later saw a famous battle and Solomon's dream.

moments.title: The Gibeonites' trick
moments.text: Having heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai, the people of Gibeon put on worn clothes, packed moldy bread, and said they came from far away. Israel made a treaty with them without asking the LORD for guidance.

moments.title: Five kings attack Gibeon
moments.text: Gibeon was a great city, and five Amorite kings camped against it because it had made peace with Israel. The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua to come quickly and save them.

moments.title: The sun stands still
moments.text: The LORD threw the enemy into confusion, and Israel won at Gibeon. When Joshua spoke, the sun stood still over Gibeon for about a full day.

moments.title: Battle by the pool
moments.text: Abner's men and Joab's men met on opposite sides of the pool of Gibeon. Twelve men from each side fought and fell together, so the place was called Helkath-hazzurim.

moments.title: Solomon's dream
moments.text: Solomon went to Gibeon, the great high place, and offered a thousand burnt offerings. One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to him in a dream and said, "Ask, and I will give it to you!"

cards.name: Shechem
cards.line: Shechem was a city in Canaan where Jacob camped, where Joshua called Israel to serve the LORD, and where Abimelech was made king and Israel gathered to make Rehoboam king.

moments.title: Jacob camps at Shechem
moments.text: Jacob came safely from Paddan-aram and camped outside the city of Shechem. He bought the plot of ground where he pitched his tent and set up an altar there.

moments.title: Foreign gods buried
moments.text: Jacob told his household to get rid of their foreign gods. They gave him the gods and earrings, and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.

moments.title: Joshua gathers Israel
moments.text: Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem, and they presented themselves before God. He reminded them of what God had done and told them to fear the LORD and serve Him.

moments.title: Abimelech made king
moments.text: Abimelech asked his mother's family to speak to the leaders of Shechem, and their hearts turned to follow him. The leaders gathered by the oak at the pillar and made him their king.

moments.title: Rehoboam goes to Shechem
moments.text: All Israel went to Shechem to make Rehoboam king. The people asked him to lighten the heavy yoke Solomon had put on them, and he went to ask the elders for advice.

cards.name: Gaza
cards.line: Gaza was a Philistine city near the Mediterranean coast, and it is where Samson was carried as a blind prisoner and also where he carried off the city gates.

moments.title: Samson carries off the gates
moments.text: Samson went to Gaza, and the men of the city waited at the gate to kill him at dawn. At midnight he pulled up the city gate doors, posts, and bar, and carried them to a mountaintop near Hebron.

moments.title: Samson in prison
moments.text: After the Philistines seized Samson and gouged out his eyes, they brought him down to Gaza. He was bound with bronze shackles and forced to grind grain in the prison.

cards.name: Shiloh
cards.line: Shiloh was a city in Ephraim where Israel set up the Tent of Meeting, divided the land, and where God spoke to young Samuel.

moments.title: Land divided at Shiloh
moments.text: Israel gathered at Shiloh and set up the Tent of Meeting. Joshua sent men to map the land, then cast lots there in the presence of the LORD to give seven tribes their shares.

moments.title: Hannah prays for a son
moments.text: Hannah wept and prayed at Shiloh, promising to dedicate a son to the LORD. Eli blessed her, and God later gave her Samuel.

moments.title: Samuel given to the LORD
moments.text: After Samuel was weaned, Hannah brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh with a bull, flour, and wine. She dedicated him to the LORD for life.

moments.title: The LORD speaks to Samuel
moments.text: The LORD called the boy Samuel at night, and Samuel answered, "Speak, for Your servant is listening." The LORD kept appearing at Shiloh and revealed Himself to Samuel by His word.

moments.title: The ark taken from Shiloh
moments.text: After Israel lost to the Philistines, the elders had the ark of the covenant brought from Shiloh. The ark was captured, and a runner brought the news to Shiloh, where the whole city cried out.

cards.name: Mount Nebo
cards.line: Mount Nebo is a mountain in Moab, across from Jericho, where Moses saw the Promised Land from a distance and died.

moments.title: God Calls Moses Up
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to go up Mount Nebo and view Canaan, the land He was giving to Israel. He said Moses would die there, and would not enter the land because he and Aaron broke faith at Meribah-kadesh.

moments.title: Moses Sees the Land and Dies
moments.text: The LORD showed Moses the whole land from the top of Pisgah, but said he would not cross into it. Then Moses died there in Moab, as the LORD had said.

cards.name: River
cards.line: In these verses, "the River" is the Euphrates, a great river that flows all year and marks the land beyond which Abraham's family once lived.

moments.title: Balak calls for Balaam
moments.text: Balak, king of Moab, sent messengers to Balaam at Pethor, by the Euphrates. He asked Balaam to curse the people of Israel, who had come out of Egypt.

moments.title: Abraham called from beyond the river
moments.text: Joshua reminded Israel that their fathers lived beyond the Euphrates and worshiped other gods. The LORD took Abraham from there and led him through the land of Canaan.

moments.title: Questions from the governor
moments.text: Tattenai, governor of the region west of the Euphrates, asked the Jews who authorized them to rebuild the temple. He then sent a letter to King Darius, and the work was not stopped.

moments.title: Nehemiah's letters for safe passage
moments.text: Nehemiah asked the king for letters to the governors west of the Euphrates. He gave them the letters, and the king also sent army officers and cavalry with him.

cards.name: Caesarea
cards.line: Caesarea was a Roman port city on the Mediterranean coast, where Peter met the Gentile Cornelius and where Paul was held as a prisoner.

moments.title: Peter visits Cornelius
moments.text: Peter arrives in Caesarea at the home of Cornelius, a Roman army officer called a centurion, who feared God. Peter tells the gathered people that God does not show favoritism and welcomes people from every nation.

moments.title: Agabus warns Paul
moments.text: Paul stays at the home of Philip, a man who spread the good news about Jesus. The prophet Agabus says Paul will be bound in Jerusalem, and Paul answers that he is ready even to die for the name of the Lord Jesus.

moments.title: Paul brought to Felix
moments.text: Because of a plot against Paul, Roman soldiers take him toward Caesarea, and horsemen bring him the rest of the way. There they hand the commander's letter to Governor Felix, who orders Paul kept under guard.

moments.title: Paul appeals to Caesar
moments.text: Festus returns to Caesarea and sits on the judgment seat, and Paul's accusers bring charges they cannot prove. Paul says he should be tried by Caesar and appeals to him, and Festus agrees.

cards.name: Philippi
cards.line: Philippi was a leading Roman colony in Macedonia, where the gospel first took root in Europe and where Paul planted a church that stayed close to him.

moments.title: Lydia believes
moments.text: On the Sabbath, Paul and his friends spoke to women gathered by the river outside the city gate. The Lord opened the heart of Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth, and she and her household were baptized.

moments.title: A spirit leaves a slave girl
moments.text: While Paul stayed in Philippi, a slave girl who made money by telling fortunes followed him for many days. Paul commanded the spirit in her, in the name of Jesus Christ, to come out, and it left at that moment.

moments.title: Suffering in Philippi
moments.text: Paul later reminded the believers in Thessalonica that he and his team had suffered and been shamefully treated in Philippi. Even so, they boldly spoke the gospel of God to the Thessalonians.

moments.title: Paul sails from Philippi
moments.text: After the Feast of Unleavened Bread, Paul and his companions sailed from Philippi. Five days later they reached Troas and stayed seven days.

cards.name: Antioch
cards.line: Antioch in Syria was a major city about 300 miles north of Jerusalem, where the good news reached Greeks and where missionaries were sent out.

moments.title: Good News to the Greeks
moments.text: Believers scattered by persecution came to Antioch. Some men from Cyprus and Cyrene began speaking to the Greeks about the Lord Jesus, and a great number believed.

moments.title: First Called Christians
moments.text: The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to Antioch, and he brought Saul there. They taught large numbers of people for a year, and the disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.

moments.title: Prophets and a Coming Famine
moments.text: Prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch. Agabus said through the Spirit that a great famine would come, so the disciples decided to send relief to the brothers in Judea.

moments.title: Barnabas and Saul Sent Out
moments.text: The church at Antioch had prophets and teachers. While they worshiped and fasted, the Holy Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul, and the church prayed and sent them off.

moments.title: A Letter from Jerusalem
moments.text: The apostles and elders sent Judas and Silas with a letter to the Gentile believers in Antioch. The people rejoiced at its encouraging message.

cards.name: Mount Gilboa
cards.line: Mount Gilboa is a mountain range east of the plain of Jezreel, where Saul and his sons died in battle against the Philistines.

moments.title: Saul camps at Gilboa
moments.text: The Philistines camped at Shunem, and Saul gathered all Israel and camped at Gilboa. When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.

moments.title: Saul and his sons die
moments.text: The men of Israel fled, and many fell on Mount Gilboa. The Philistines killed Saul's sons, and Saul fell on his own sword, dying with his three sons that day.

moments.title: The Philistines find Saul
moments.text: The next day the Philistines came to strip the dead and found Saul and his three sons fallen on Mount Gilboa. They cut off Saul's head and took his armor.

moments.title: The Amalekite's story
moments.text: A young man told David that he had been on Mount Gilboa and saw Saul leaning on his spear. He said he killed Saul at Saul's request and brought Saul's crown to David.

moments.title: David's song of sorrow
moments.text: David sang a sad song for Saul and Jonathan. He spoke to the mountains of Gilboa, where Saul's shield was dirtied, and said, "How the mighty have fallen!"

cards.name: Goshen
cards.line: Goshen was a region in Egypt where Jacob's family settled under Joseph's care, and where God spared His people from the flies and the hail.

moments.title: Joseph offers Goshen
moments.text: Joseph tells his brothers to bring their father and settle in the land of Goshen, near him. He says he will provide for them during the five more years of famine.

moments.title: Jacob and Joseph reunite
moments.text: Jacob sends Judah ahead to get directions to Goshen. When the family arrives, Joseph goes to meet his father, embraces him, and weeps.

moments.title: Pharaoh allows Goshen
moments.text: Joseph tells Pharaoh his family is now in Goshen. His brothers ask to settle there, and Pharaoh says they may live in Goshen, in the best part of the land.

moments.title: No flies in Goshen
moments.text: God says He will give special treatment to Goshen, where His people live. No swarms of flies will be found there, so Pharaoh will know the LORD is in the land.

moments.title: No hail in Goshen
moments.text: Hail strikes everything in the fields across Egypt. The only place it does not hail is Goshen, where the Israelites live.

cards.name: Thessalonica
cards.line: Thessalonica was a large Macedonian city with a Jewish synagogue, where Paul preached about Jesus, a church began, and trouble from opponents soon followed.

moments.title: Paul teaches in the synagogue
moments.text: On three Sabbaths Paul talked with the Jews from the Scriptures and showed that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead. Some Jews, many Greeks who worshiped God, and quite a few leading women joined Paul and Silas.

moments.title: Gifts for Paul's needs
moments.text: Paul told the Philippians that while he was in Thessalonica, they gave him what he needed again and again.

moments.title: Aristarchus sails with Paul
moments.text: When Paul was taken by ship toward Italy as a prisoner, Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with him.

moments.title: Demas goes to Thessalonica
moments.text: Near the end of his life, Paul wrote that Demas, in his love of this world, had left him and gone to Thessalonica.

cards.name: Joppa
cards.line: Joppa was a seaport city on the Mediterranean coast, where Jonah boarded a ship to flee from God and where Peter raised Tabitha and later received a vision.

moments.title: Jonah Flees by Ship
moments.text: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh, but Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish. He went down to Joppa, paid the fare, and boarded a ship, away from the presence of the LORD.

moments.title: Tabitha Raised to Life
moments.text: Tabitha, a disciple known for kindness and charity, became sick and died in Joppa. Peter prayed and said, "Tabitha, get up!" and she opened her eyes and sat up.

moments.title: Many Believe in Joppa
moments.text: News of Tabitha being alive spread all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord. Peter then stayed several days with Simon, a tanner.

moments.title: Peter's Vision
moments.text: While praying in Joppa, Peter saw a large sheet come down from heaven filled with animals. A voice told him, "Do not call anything impure that God has made clean."

cards.name: Kingdom of Judah
cards.line: The Kingdom of Judah was the southern kingdom that stayed loyal to David's family after Israel split, with Jerusalem as its capital.

moments.title: Rehoboam keeps Judah
moments.text: After Israel rebelled, Rehoboam still ruled the people in the cities of Judah. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.

moments.title: The LORD stops a war
moments.text: Rehoboam gathered 180,000 warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel. The LORD told them not to fight their brothers, and they listened and went home.

moments.title: Rehoboam builds up Judah
moments.text: Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem and built up cities in Judah to protect them. He made their defenses stronger and stocked them with food, oil, and wine.

moments.title: Assyria attacks Judah
moments.text: Sennacherib king of Assyria captured all the strong, protected cities of Judah. Hezekiah paid him silver and gold, but Assyria still sent an army to Jerusalem.

moments.title: Josiah cleans up Judah
moments.text: King Josiah removed the priests who burned incense to false gods, along with the fortune-tellers, household gods, and idols from Judah and Jerusalem. He did this to carry out the words of the law book found in the temple.

cards.name: Ararat
cards.line: Ararat is a mountain region where Noah's ark came to rest after the Flood, and later a land named when God called nations against Babylon.

moments.title: The ark comes to rest
moments.text: The waters went down for 150 days. On the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

cards.name: Babylonia
cards.line: Babylonia was the land where Israel's exiles lived and where the temple treasures were kept, and from it God's people returned to Jerusalem.

moments.title: Temple articles go home
moments.text: Sheshbazzar brought 5,400 gold and silver articles along when the exiles went up from Babylon to Jerusalem.

moments.title: Darius orders a search
moments.text: King Darius ordered a search of the archives in the treasury of Babylon. A scroll was found with Cyrus's decree to rebuild God's house.

moments.title: Ezra leaves Babylon
moments.text: Ezra, a scribe skilled in the Law of Moses, began the journey from Babylon on the first day of the first month. He reached Jerusalem in the fifth month, for the gracious hand of his God was upon him.

moments.title: Gifts from Babylon
moments.text: King Artaxerxes told Ezra to take the silver and gold he might find in all the province of Babylon, with the freewill offerings, to the house of God in Jerusalem.

moments.title: Family heads return
moments.text: Ezra listed the family heads and records of those who returned with him from Babylon during the reign of King Artaxerxes.

cards.name: Laodicea
cards.line: Laodicea was a rich city in Asia Minor with a church that Paul struggled for and that Jesus later rebuked and invited to open the door to Him.

moments.title: Paul struggles for Laodicea
moments.text: Paul says he is struggling for the believers at Laodicea, even those who have never met him. He wants them encouraged in heart and knit together in love.

moments.title: Epaphras works for Laodicea
moments.text: Paul says Epaphras goes to great pains for the believers at Laodicea, as well as Colossae and Hierapolis. Paul also tells them to greet the brothers in Laodicea.

moments.title: A letter to share
moments.text: Paul tells the Colossians to make sure his letter is also read in the church of the Laodiceans. They are to read the letter from Laodicea too.

moments.title: Laodicea named among seven churches
moments.text: Jesus tells John to write what he sees and send it to seven churches. Laodicea is the last one on the list.

moments.title: Jesus' message to Laodicea
moments.text: Jesus calls the church lukewarm and says it thinks it is rich but is really poor and blind. He rebukes those He loves, then says He stands at the door and knocks.

cards.name: Machpelah
cards.line: Machpelah is a cave and field near Mamre, in Hebron, that Abraham bought as a burial place for his family, and it became the resting place of Israel's fathers.

moments.title: Sarah is buried
moments.text: After Abraham pays four hundred shekels of silver for the field and cave, they become his property as a burial site. He buries his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre.

moments.title: Abraham is buried
moments.text: When Abraham dies, his sons Isaac and Ishmael bury him in the cave of Machpelah. He is laid there with his wife Sarah.

moments.title: Jacob is buried
moments.text: Jacob's sons carry him from Egypt to Canaan and bury him in the cave at Machpelah, as he asked.

cards.name: Cana
cards.line: Cana was a town in Galilee where Jesus did His first sign, turning water into wine, and where He later spoke healing for an official's son.

moments.title: Water Into Wine
moments.text: At a wedding in Cana, the wine ran out, and Jesus had servants fill stone jars with water. It became fine wine, the first of His signs, and His disciples believed in Him.

moments.title: A Royal Official's Son Healed
moments.text: A royal official came to Jesus at Cana and begged Him to heal his son, who was about to die at Capernaum. Jesus said, "Your son will live," and the boy was healed.

cards.name: Ur of the Chaldees
cards.line: Ur of the Chaldeans was an ancient city and the home of Abram's family, the place God brought him out of to give him the promised land.

moments.title: Haran dies in Ur
moments.text: Terah's son Haran died in his native land, in Ur of the Chaldeans, while his father was still alive. Haran was the father of Lot.

moments.title: Terah leaves Ur
moments.text: Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai and set out from Ur for the land of Canaan. When they came to Haran, they settled there.

cards.name: Mount Moriah
cards.line: Mount Moriah is the mountain in Jerusalem where Solomon built the LORD's house, and it is linked to the land where Abraham was to offer Isaac.

moments.title: God names the land of Moriah
moments.text: God tests Abraham and tells him to take his son Isaac to the land of Moriah. He is to offer Isaac there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that God will show him.

moments.title: Solomon builds the temple
moments.text: Solomon begins to build the house of the LORD on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem. This is where the LORD had appeared to David, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

cards.name: Valley of Elah
cards.line: The Valley of Elah is a valley in Judah where Israel camped to face the Philistines, the place where David killed the giant Goliath.

moments.title: Israel camps for battle
moments.text: Saul and the men of Israel gathered in the Valley of Elah to get ready to fight the Philistines. The two armies stood on hills with the valley between them.

moments.title: David kills Goliath
moments.text: The priest Ahimelech later said that David had killed Goliath the Philistine in the Valley of Elah. This is the valley where the giant fell.

cards.name: Beautiful Gate
cards.line: The Beautiful Gate was a temple gate in Jerusalem where a lame beggar sat, and where Peter and John healed him in Jesus' name.

moments.title: A beggar at the gate
moments.text: A man who had been lame from birth was carried to the temple gate called Beautiful every day. He begged from people going into the temple courts, and he asked Peter and John for money.

moments.title: Healed in Jesus' name
moments.text: Peter told the man to get up and walk in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. His feet and ankles were made strong at once, and he went into the temple walking, leaping, and praising God.

moments.title: Known as the gate beggar
moments.text: The people recognized the man as the one who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate. They were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.

cards.name: Edom
cards.line: Edom was a rugged, mountainous land south of the Dead Sea, home to Israel's "brother" nation, and a place of refusal, war, and rebellion against Israel and Judah.

moments.title: Edom Says No to Israel
moments.text: Moses sent messengers asking the king of Edom to let Israel pass along the King's Highway. Edom refused and came out with a large army, so Israel turned away.

moments.title: David Rules Edom
moments.text: David struck down eighteen thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He put soldiers throughout Edom, and all the Edomites came under his rule.

moments.title: Joab Strikes Edom
moments.text: When David was in Edom, his army commander Joab stayed six months and killed every male there. Years later, the LORD raised up Hadad the Edomite, a young boy who had escaped to Egypt, as an enemy against Solomon.

moments.title: Water Flows from Edom
moments.text: Three kings took a route by way of the Desert of Edom and ran out of water. After Elisha spoke the LORD's word, water flowed from the direction of Edom the next morning and filled the land.

moments.title: Edom Rebels Against Judah
moments.text: In the days of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against Judah and chose its own king. The writer says Edom has been in rebellion to this day.

cards.name: Gilead
cards.line: Gilead is a hilly, grassy region east of the Jordan River, good for herds, where Jacob met Laban, tribes settled, and Jephthah and Elijah lived.

moments.title: Laban catches Jacob
moments.text: Jacob ran away toward the hill country of Gilead, and Laban chased him for seven days and caught him there. That night God warned Laban in a dream not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.

moments.title: Tribes eye Gilead
moments.text: The Reubenites and Gadites had very large herds and flocks. They looked over Gilead and saw that it was good land for animals.

moments.title: Jephthah becomes leader
moments.text: When the Ammonites made war on Israel, the elders of Gilead brought Jephthah back from the land of Tob, though they had forced him out. The people made him their leader and commander, and he repeated his terms before the LORD at Mizpah.

moments.title: Gilead fights Ephraim
moments.text: Jephthah gathered the men of Gilead and fought Ephraim, and the Gileadites took the crossing places of the Jordan. Jephthah judged Israel six years and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.

moments.title: Elijah from Gilead
moments.text: Elijah the Tishbite was among the settlers of Gilead. He told King Ahab that there would be no dew or rain in the coming years except at his word.

cards.name: Syria
cards.line: Syria, called Aram in the Old Testament, was the land north of Israel, home to Damascus and to kings who fought Israel and Judah.

moments.title: Naaman the commander
moments.text: Naaman, the commander of the king of Aram's army, was a great man, but he had leprosy. A young girl taken from Israel told his wife about the prophet in Samaria, and the king sent Naaman to Israel with a letter and gifts.

moments.title: Aram's king is enraged
moments.text: The king of Aram was at war against Israel, but Elisha kept warning Israel's king. The angry king of Aram demanded to know which of his servants was on Israel's side.

moments.title: Elisha and Hazael in Damascus
moments.text: Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad, king of Aram, was sick. Hazael brought a gift and asked if the king would recover, and Elisha said the LORD had shown him that Hazael would be king over Aram.

moments.title: Aram marches on Jerusalem
moments.text: Rezin, king of Aram, marched up to fight Jerusalem with Israel's king, but could not overpower the city. Aram's plot against Judah made Ahaz and his people tremble, and the LORD sent Isaiah to tell Ahaz not to fear.

moments.title: Jesus' fame spreads
moments.text: News about Jesus spread all over Syria. People brought Him all who were ill, in pain, demon-possessed, having seizures, or paralyzed, and He healed them.

cards.name: Bashan
cards.line: Bashan was a rich region east of the Jordan River, ruled by King Og, that Israel took and gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

moments.title: Israel defeats King Og
moments.text: Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to fight Israel at Edrei. The LORD told Moses not to fear, and Israel struck Og's army down and took his land.

moments.title: Sixty cities taken
moments.text: Israel captured all sixty cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan, in the region of Argob. Not one city was left untaken, though they had high walls, gates, and bars.

moments.title: Og, last of the Rephaim
moments.text: Og king of Bashan was the only one left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His iron bed was nine cubits long and four cubits wide.

moments.title: Land given to Manasseh
moments.text: Moses gave all of Bashan, the kingdom of Og, to the half-tribe of Manasseh. Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the region of Argob and renamed Bashan Havvoth-jair.

moments.title: Golan, a city of refuge
moments.text: Moses set aside three cities east of the Jordan where a person could flee after killing a neighbor unintentionally, with no prior malice. Golan in Bashan was one of them.

cards.name: Dan
cards.line: Dan was a city in the far north of Israel, once called Laish, that the tribe of Dan took and named; it became known for idol worship.

moments.title: Abram chases the raiders
moments.text: When Abram heard that Lot had been captured, he took 318 trained men from his household and chased the enemy as far as Dan.

moments.title: The Danites take Laish
moments.text: The tribe of Dan attacked the quiet people of Laish, burned the city, rebuilt it, and named it Dan. They set up idols there.

moments.title: Jeroboam's golden calf
moments.text: King Jeroboam set up one golden calf in Dan and another in Bethel. The people walked all the way to Dan to worship the calf, and this became a sin.

moments.title: Ben-hadad conquers Dan
moments.text: King Asa sent silver and gold to Ben-hadad of Aram. Ben-hadad then sent his army against Israel and conquered Dan and other cities.

moments.title: Horses heard from Dan
moments.text: Jeremiah warned that the snorting of enemy horses was heard from Dan. The whole land shook as the enemy came to devour it.

cards.name: Sidon
cards.line: Sidon was an old Phoenician harbor city on the Mediterranean coast, known for trade, and it appears in the stories of Elijah, Jesus, and Paul.

moments.title: Elijah sent to Zarephath of Sidon
moments.text: When the brook dried up, the LORD told Elijah to go to Zarephath of Sidon. A widow there shared her last flour and oil, and the jar and jug did not run out.

moments.title: A Canaanite woman's faith
moments.text: Jesus withdrew to the district of Tyre and Sidon, where a Canaanite woman begged Him to help her daughter. He praised her great faith, and her daughter was healed.

moments.title: Jesus passes through Sidon
moments.text: Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon on His way to the Sea of Galilee and the Decapolis.

moments.title: Paul visits friends
moments.text: On the way to Italy, Paul's ship landed at Sidon. Julius, the Roman army officer in charge of Paul, let him visit his friends and receive their care.

cards.name: Negeb
cards.line: The Negev is the dry southern region of Canaan, where Abram traveled, Isaac lived, and the spies passed through, and where Caleb's daughter Acsah received land.

moments.title: Abram travels toward the Negev
moments.text: Abram journeyed on toward the Negev, but a severe famine sent him down to Egypt. Later he came back up into the Negev with his wife, Lot, and all his possessions.

moments.title: Isaac lives in the Negev
moments.text: Isaac was living in the Negev after returning from Beer-lahai-roi. One evening he saw Rebekah coming, and he took her as his wife and was comforted.

moments.title: The spies go through the Negev
moments.text: Moses sent men to spy out Canaan and told them to go up through the Negev. They came to Hebron and cut a huge cluster of grapes in the Valley of Eshcol.

moments.title: Acsah receives land in the Negev
moments.text: Caleb gave his daughter Acsah land in the Negev. She asked him for springs of water as well, and he gave her the upper and lower springs.

cards.name: Gilgal
cards.line: Gilgal was Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan into Canaan, and it later became a place where Saul was made king and then failed.

moments.title: Twelve stones at Gilgal
moments.text: After crossing the Jordan on dry ground, Israel camped at Gilgal. Joshua set up the twelve stones taken from the river to remind children of what the LORD did.

moments.title: Shame of Egypt rolled away
moments.text: At Gilgal Joshua circumcised the sons of Israel, who had been born in the wilderness. The LORD said He had rolled away the shame of Egypt from them, and the place was called Gilgal.

moments.title: Passover in the land
moments.text: Camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho, the Israelites kept the Passover. They ate the land's produce, and the day after that, the manna stopped.

moments.title: Saul confirmed as king
moments.text: Samuel called the people to Gilgal to make Saul's kingship official again. There they confirmed Saul as king before the LORD, offered peace offerings, and rejoiced greatly.

moments.title: Saul's offering and loss of kingdom
moments.text: Saul waited seven days for Samuel at Gilgal, but his troops began to desert. He offered the burnt offering himself, and Samuel said Saul would not keep ruling for long because he did not obey the LORD's command.

cards.name: Valley of Jezreel
cards.line: The Valley of Jezreel is a wide, fertile plain in Israel where enemy armies camped against Gideon and where Ahab, Jehu, and Jezebel's story played out nearby.

moments.title: Enemy armies camp here
moments.text: The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern peoples crossed the Jordan and camped in the Valley of Jezreel. The Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, and he rallied Israel to meet them.

cards.name: Ramah
cards.line: Ramah, meaning "high place," is the name of several towns, and one was Samuel's home, where he judged Israel and built an altar to the LORD.

moments.title: Israel asks for a king
moments.text: The elders of Israel came to Samuel at Ramah and asked him to appoint a king like the other nations. The LORD told Samuel they had rejected Him as their king, and Samuel was to warn them.

moments.title: David runs to Samuel
moments.text: David ran from Saul to Samuel at Ramah, and they stayed at Naioth. Saul's messengers and then Saul himself came, and the Spirit of God came upon each of them so they prophesied.

moments.title: Samuel is buried
moments.text: When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him. They buried him at his home in Ramah.

moments.title: Baasha builds up Ramah
moments.text: Baasha of Israel fortified Ramah, in Benjamin, to block Asa's land. When he stopped, Asa carried off its stones and timbers to build Geba and Mizpah.

moments.title: Jeremiah is freed
moments.text: At a Ramah near Jerusalem, not Samuel's town, Nebuzaradan found Jeremiah in chains among captives bound for Babylon. He set Jeremiah free.

cards.name: Cush
cards.line: Cush is a land south of Egypt, and the Bible says its people will one day stretch out their hands to God.

moments.title: Tirhakah, King of Cush
moments.text: Sennacherib is warned that Tirhakah, king of Cush, has set out to fight him. Sennacherib sends messengers to Hezekiah again, and Hezekiah spreads the letter out before the LORD.

moments.title: Cush Reaches Out to God
