moments.text: The psalm says messengers will come from Egypt, and Cush will stretch out her hands to God. The kingdoms of the earth are told to sing praises to Him.

moments.title: A Warning About Cush
moments.text: The LORD has Isaiah go naked and barefoot for three years as a sign against Egypt and Cush. The king of Assyria will lead away captives of Cush, and those who made Cush their hope will be ashamed.

moments.title: Offerings from Beyond Cush
moments.text: The LORD says His worshipers, His scattered people from beyond the rivers of Cush, will bring Him an offering. He also says He will leave a humble people who trust in His name.

cards.name: Asia
cards.line: Asia was a Roman province in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus as its capital, where Paul taught for two years and where the seven churches of Revelation were found.

moments.title: The Spirit Redirects Paul
moments.text: The Holy Spirit kept Paul and his team from speaking the word in Asia. They traveled through Phrygia and Galatia instead, and later a vision led them to Macedonia.

moments.title: The Word Spreads Through Asia
moments.text: Paul held daily talks in the lecture hall of Tyrannus for two years. Everyone in Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.

moments.title: Trouble Over Artemis
moments.text: Demetrius the silversmith said Paul had turned many people in Asia away from man-made gods. His words stirred up a great riot in Ephesus.

moments.title: Hardship in Asia
moments.text: Paul wrote that he and his team faced a burden far beyond their strength in Asia. They gave up hope of staying alive, but they learned to trust God, who raises the dead.

moments.title: John Writes to the Seven Churches
moments.text: John greeted the seven churches in Asia with grace and peace from God. He was told to write what he saw and send it to them.

cards.name: Galatia
cards.line: Galatia was a region in central Asia Minor where Paul traveled and strengthened the disciples, and where churches received his letter about the true gospel.

moments.title: Paul Travels Through Galatia
moments.text: After the Holy Spirit kept them from speaking the word in Asia, Paul and his companions traveled through the region of Phrygia and Galatia.

moments.title: Strengthening the Disciples
moments.text: After some time in Antioch, Paul went from place to place through Galatia and Phrygia. He strengthened all the disciples there.

moments.title: Turning to a Different Gospel
moments.text: Paul wrote to the churches of Galatia. He was amazed that they were quickly turning to a different gospel, and he warned that no other gospel is the true one.

cards.name: Kadesh
cards.line: Kadesh was a city on the edge of Edom's land where Israel camped, received the spies' report, and stayed a very long time after refusing to trust God.

moments.title: The spies return
moments.text: The twelve men came back to Moses, Aaron, and all Israel at Kadesh and showed them the fruit of the land. Caleb said to take the land, but the other spies said the people were too strong.

moments.title: Israel's long stay
moments.text: After the people rebelled and were turned back, they wept before the LORD, but He would not listen. For this reason they stayed in Kadesh a very long time.

moments.title: A message to Edom
moments.text: From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to the king of Edom. They asked to pass through his land on the King's Highway, but Edom refused and came out with a large army.

moments.title: Leaving for Mount Hor
moments.text: After Edom refused them, Israel turned away. They set out from Kadesh, and all the Israelites came to Mount Hor.

cards.name: Macedonia
cards.line: Macedonia was a Roman province north of Greece, and the first part of Europe to hear the gospel from Paul after he was called there.

moments.title: The Call to Macedonia
moments.text: During the night, Paul had a vision of a man of Macedonia pleading, "Come over to Macedonia and help us." As soon as he saw it, they got ready to leave, concluding that God had called them to preach the gospel there.

moments.title: Arriving at Philippi
moments.text: Paul and his companions stayed several days in Philippi, the leading city of that part of Macedonia. There the Lord opened Lydia's heart, and she and her household were baptized.

moments.title: Generous Churches of Macedonia
moments.text: Paul told the Corinthians about the grace God gave the churches of Macedonia. Though they suffered and were very poor, they were full of joy and gave freely, even beyond what they were able to give.

cards.name: Mizpah
cards.line: Mizpah, meaning watch-tower, is a name used for more than one place in the Bible, where Israel met, prayed, and faced hard moments before the LORD.

moments.title: Laban and Jacob's witness
moments.text: Laban and Jacob made a covenant and set up a mound of stones as a witness. The place was also called Mizpah, because Laban asked the LORD to keep watch between them.

moments.title: Jephthah's daughter
moments.text: After Jephthah defeated the Ammonites, he came home to Mizpah. His only child, his daughter, came out to meet him with tambourines and dancing, and he grieved over the vow he had made to the LORD.

moments.title: Israel gathers over a wicked deed
moments.text: All Israel assembled as one man before the LORD at Mizpah. They asked the Levite how the wicked thing had happened.

moments.title: Samuel leads Israel to repent
moments.text: Samuel called Israel to Mizpah to pray for them. They poured out water, fasted, and confessed, "We have sinned against the LORD."

moments.title: Victory and the Ebenezer stone
moments.text: When the Philistines came, the LORD thundered against them and Israel charged out of Mizpah and chased them. Samuel then set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen and named it Ebenezer, saying, "Thus far the LORD has helped us."

cards.name: Tarshish
cards.line: Tarshish was a far-off sea destination, known for ships that brought riches to Solomon, and the place Jonah tried to sail to when he fled from the LORD.

moments.title: Solomon's ships of Tarshish
moments.text: King Solomon had ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram's fleet. Once every three years the ships of Tarshish arrived bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

moments.title: Ships meant for Tarshish
moments.text: Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah agreed to make ships to go to Tarshish. Eliezer prophesied against Jehoshaphat, and the ships were wrecked and could not sail to Tarshish.

moments.title: Jonah heads for Tarshish
moments.text: God told Jonah to go to Nineveh. Instead Jonah got up to flee to Tarshish, paid the fare on a ship at Joppa, and went aboard to sail away from the presence of the LORD.

moments.title: Why Jonah fled toward Tarshish
moments.text: When God saw Nineveh turn from its evil ways, He relented, and Jonah became angry. Jonah prayed that he had fled toward Tarshish because he knew God is gracious and compassionate.

cards.name: Mount Hermon
cards.line: Mount Hermon is a tall, snow-capped mountain at Israel's northern edge, a landmark that marked the edge of the land God gave His people.

moments.title: Joshua wins the north
moments.text: Joshua took the whole land and struck down all its kings. His win reached Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon, at the foot of Mount Hermon.

moments.title: Hermon in Manasseh's land
moments.text: The half-tribe of Manasseh grew large and settled from Bashan to Baal-hermon, which is also called Senir and Mount Hermon.

cards.name: Megiddo
cards.line: Megiddo was a city on the edge of the plain of Esdraelon, a famous battlefield where two kings of Judah, Ahaziah and Josiah, met their deaths.

moments.title: Ahaziah dies at Megiddo
moments.text: King Ahaziah of Judah fled from Jehu and was shot in his chariot. He escaped to Megiddo and died there.

moments.title: Josiah goes to battle
moments.text: Neco of Egypt warned Josiah to stop opposing God, but Josiah did not listen. He disguised himself and went to fight on the Plain of Megiddo.

moments.title: Josiah is killed
moments.text: Pharaoh Neco killed King Josiah at Megiddo. His servants carried his body from there to Jerusalem, where he was buried in his own tomb.

cards.name: Ai
cards.line: Ai was a Canaanite city east of Bethel, near where Abram once camped and where Israel first lost, then won, a battle under Joshua.

moments.title: Abram camps near Ai
moments.text: Abram pitched his tent in the hill country with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on His name.

moments.title: Israel is defeated at Ai
moments.text: Joshua sent spies to Ai, and about three thousand men went up to attack. They fled before the men of Ai, and the people's hearts melted like water.

moments.title: The ambush and the fall of Ai
moments.text: The men of Ai chased Israel and left their city wide open. Joshua held out his battle lance as the LORD said, and the hidden men captured and burned the city.

moments.title: Ai becomes a heap of ruins
moments.text: Israel defeated the people of Ai and took the king alive. Joshua burned the city and made it a permanent heap of ruins.

cards.name: Ophir
cards.line: Ophir was a faraway region famous for its fine gold, and Solomon's ships sailed there to bring back gold, precious stones, and special wood.

moments.title: Solomon's gold fleet
moments.text: Hiram sent skilled sailors to serve with Solomon's servants. They sailed to Ophir and brought back 420 talents of gold (a talent was a very heavy weight) to Solomon.

moments.title: Almug wood and gems
moments.text: Hiram's fleet brought a great cargo of almug wood and precious stones from Ophir, along with gold.

moments.title: More ships for Ophir gold
moments.text: Hiram sent ships with experienced sailors, who went with Solomon's servants to Ophir. They got 450 talents of gold there and brought it to King Solomon.

cards.name: Kadesh-barnea
cards.line: Kadesh-barnea was a desert city on the southern edge of the Promised Land, where Israel refused to enter the land and was sent to wander for forty years.

moments.title: Told to take the land
moments.text: When Israel reached Kadesh-barnea, Moses said the LORD had placed the land before them. He told them to go up and take it and not to be afraid or discouraged.

moments.title: Twelve men sent to spy
moments.text: Moses sent twelve men, one from each tribe, from Kadesh-barnea to inspect the land. They saw the land at the Valley of Eshcol, but they discouraged the Israelites from entering it.

moments.title: Israel rebels against God
moments.text: The LORD told Israel to go up and possess the land, but they rebelled. They neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.

moments.title: Forty years of wandering
moments.text: Because Israel did not follow Him wholeheartedly, the LORD swore that the men twenty or older would not see the land, except Caleb and Joshua. From Kadesh-barnea until the Brook of Zered was thirty-eight years, until that generation had died.

moments.title: Caleb sent from Kadesh-barnea
moments.text: Caleb was forty years old when Moses sent him from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land. He brought back an honest report, and Moses promised him the land because he wholly followed the LORD.

cards.name: Kidron
cards.line: The Kidron is a valley just east of Jerusalem where David crossed in sorrow, and where godly kings burned idols and dumped unclean things.

moments.title: David crosses the valley
moments.text: As David leaves Jerusalem, the king crosses the Kidron Valley while everyone in the countryside weeps loudly. The people pass on toward the way of the wilderness.

moments.title: Asa burns an idol
moments.text: Asa removes his grandmother Maacah as queen mother because she made a hateful Asherah pole. He chops it down and burns it in the Kidron Valley.

moments.title: Hezekiah's cleansing
moments.text: The priests cleanse the house of the LORD and bring out the unclean things they find. The Levites carry them out to the Kidron Valley.

moments.title: Josiah destroys idols
moments.text: King Josiah has the articles made for Baal and Asherah burned in the fields of Kidron. He also burns the Asherah pole in the valley and throws the dust of the crushed altars into it.

cards.name: Meribah
cards.line: Meribah, meaning quarrel, names waters in the wilderness where Israel quarreled with the LORD, once near Rephidim and later at Kadesh, where Moses and Aaron rebelled.

moments.title: Israel tests the LORD
moments.text: The LORD said Moses would strike the rock by Horeb so the people could drink. Moses named the place Massah and Meribah because Israel quarreled and asked, "Is the LORD among us or not?"

moments.title: The LORD shows His holiness
moments.text: The LORD told Moses and Aaron they did not trust Him to show His holiness, so they would not bring the assembly into the land. These were the waters of Meribah, where Israel quarreled with the LORD.

cards.name: Susa
cards.line: Susa was a great Persian city where King Xerxes ruled from his citadel, a protected fortress part of the city, and where the story of Queen Esther took place.

moments.title: The king's great feast
moments.text: King Xerxes sat on his royal throne in the citadel of Susa, the protected part of the city. He held a seven-day feast in the palace garden court for all the people in the citadel, from the least to the greatest.

moments.title: Esther taken to the palace
moments.text: Mordecai, a Jewish man, lived at the citadel of Susa. Many young women were gathered there, and Esther was taken to the palace and placed under the care of Hegai.

moments.title: The edict and a city in confusion
moments.text: The order to destroy all the Jews was issued in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was in confusion.

moments.title: Esther asks the Jews to fast
moments.text: Esther told Mordecai to gather all the Jews in Susa and fast for her for three days. After that she would go to the king, even though it was against the law.

moments.title: The Jews defend themselves
moments.text: The king told Esther how many were killed in Susa. At her request, he allowed the Jews in Susa one more day, and they gathered again on the fourteenth day of Adar.

cards.name: Mount Tabor
cards.line: Mount Tabor is a lone, rounded mountain in northern Israel, where Barak gathered Israel's army before a great victory over Sisera, and a place the Bible uses to praise God.

moments.title: Barak Goes to Tabor
moments.text: Deborah tells Barak that the LORD commands him to march to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun. The LORD promises to hand Sisera over to him.

moments.title: Victory Over Sisera
moments.text: Sisera hears that Barak has gone up Mount Tabor and gathers his chariots. Deborah tells Barak the day has come, so he goes down with ten thousand men, and the LORD defeats Sisera's whole army.

moments.title: Tabor Shouts for Joy
moments.text: In a poem of praise, the psalmist says God created north and south. Tabor and Hermon are pictured shouting for joy at His name.

cards.name: Adullam
cards.line: Adullam was a Canaanite royal city in Judah's lowlands, best known for the nearby cave where David took refuge and gathered his men.

moments.title: David hides in the cave
moments.text: David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. His brothers and his father's household came down to him there.

moments.title: A band gathers around David
moments.text: People who were upset, in debt, or unhappy gathered around David, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.

moments.title: Three mighty men come to David
moments.text: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam while Philistines were camped in the Valley of Rephaim. They later brought him water from Bethlehem, but he poured it out to the LORD.

moments.title: Rehoboam fortifies Adullam
moments.text: Rehoboam built up Adullam as one of the fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin. He put officers, supplies, shields, and spears in them.

cards.name: Colossae
cards.line: Colossae was a city in Phrygia where a church of faithful believers met, and Paul wrote one of his letters to them.

moments.title: Letter to the church at Colossae
moments.text: Paul and Timothy greet the saints and faithful brothers in Christ at Colossae. They wish them grace and peace from God our Father.

cards.name: Mamre
cards.line: Mamre was a place near Hebron in Canaan, close to the cave of Machpelah, where Abraham's family buried their dead and where Jacob came home to Isaac.

moments.title: Abraham buys a burial field
moments.text: Abraham paid Ephron four hundred shekels of silver for the field and cave at Machpelah near Mamre. Then he buried his wife Sarah there.

moments.title: Isaac and Ishmael bury Abraham
moments.text: When Abraham died, his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah near Mamre. He was laid there with his wife Sarah.

moments.title: Jacob returns to Isaac
moments.text: Jacob came back to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.

moments.title: Jacob is buried at Machpelah
moments.text: Jacob's sons carried him to Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre, as he had told them.

cards.name: Bethsaida
cards.line: Bethsaida was a fishing town by the Sea of Galilee, home to Philip, Andrew, and Peter, where Jesus healed a blind man and which He warned for not repenting.

moments.title: Jesus Withdraws to Bethsaida
moments.text: After the apostles returned and reported what they had done, Jesus took them away privately to a town called Bethsaida. The crowds followed, and He welcomed them, taught them, and healed those who needed it.

moments.title: Disciples Sent Ahead
moments.text: After five thousand men had eaten the loaves, Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida. He dismissed the crowd and went up on the mountain to pray.

moments.title: A Blind Man Healed
moments.text: At Bethsaida, people begged Jesus to touch a blind man, and He led him out of the village. After Jesus placed His hands on the man's eyes a second time, the man could see everything clearly.

moments.title: Home of Philip, Andrew, and Peter
moments.text: John tells us that Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter. Jesus had told Philip, "Follow Me."

moments.title: Woe to Bethsaida
moments.text: Jesus spoke sharp words to Bethsaida because it saw His miracles and did not repent. He said Tyre and Sidon would have repented long ago if they had seen them.

cards.name: Haran
cards.line: Haran was a city in Mesopotamia where Terah's family settled and Terah died, and from which Abram set out for Canaan, the land God promised him.

moments.title: Terah settles and dies
moments.text: Terah took Abram, Sarai, and Lot toward Canaan, but they stopped and settled in Haran. Terah lived 205 years and died there.

moments.title: Abram leaves Haran
moments.text: Abram departed as the LORD had directed him. He was seventy-five years old when he left Haran with Sarai, Lot, and all the possessions and people they had acquired there, and they set out for Canaan.

cards.name: Salt Sea
cards.line: The Salt Sea is a large inland sea east of Jerusalem, where the Jordan River ends, and in the Bible it marks the edge of the Promised Land.

moments.title: Kings gather at the Valley of Siddim
moments.text: Five kings of the plain rebelled against Chedorlaomer and came together in the Valley of Siddim, which is the Salt Sea. There they lined up for battle against four kings.

moments.title: A border of the Promised Land
moments.text: God told Moses that the Salt Sea would mark the southern end of Israel's land, and the Jordan would run down to end at the Salt Sea.

moments.title: Borders for Judah and Benjamin
moments.text: The Salt Sea became part of the borders given to the tribes. It was the eastern edge of Judah's land and marked the southern border of Benjamin's land at the mouth of the Jordan.

cards.name: Mesopotamia
cards.line: Mesopotamia, the land between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, is where Abraham's family lived, where Isaac's wife came from, and where Israel's enemies later came from.

moments.title: A servant seeks a wife for Isaac
moments.text: Abraham's servant travels with ten camels to Nahor's town in Aram-naharaim. At the well he prays, and Rebekah comes out with her jar before he finishes.

moments.title: Balaam's home in Aram-naharaim
moments.text: Moses reminds Israel that Balaam son of Beor came from Pethor in Aram-naharaim. Moab and Ammon hired him to curse Israel, but the LORD turned the curse into a blessing.

moments.title: Israel serves a king of Aram-naharaim
moments.text: Israel does evil, and the LORD sells them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, king of Aram-naharaim. They serve him eight years until the LORD raises up Othniel, who prevails against him.

moments.title: Ammonites hire chariots from Aram-naharaim
moments.text: After David's men are humiliated, the Ammonites send a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim and other lands. David then sends Joab and the army.

moments.title: God appears to Abraham
moments.text: Stephen tells the council that the God of glory appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Haran. God told him to leave his country for a land He would show him.

cards.name: Valley of the Son of Hinnom
cards.line: The Valley of Ben-hinnom was a place near Jerusalem where Judah's people sacrificed their children in the fire, and God warned it would become the Valley of Slaughter.

moments.title: Ahaz burns his sons
moments.text: King Ahaz burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom and sacrificed his sons in the fire, following the awful ways of the nations the LORD had driven out.

moments.title: Manasseh's evil
moments.text: King Manasseh sacrificed his sons in the fire in the valley. He also tried to use magic and spirits, and he did great evil that made the LORD angry.

moments.title: Josiah ruins Topheth
moments.text: King Josiah made Topheth in the valley unfit for worship, so that no one could sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire to Molech.

moments.title: The broken jar
moments.text: The LORD told Jeremiah to go to the valley at the Potsherd Gate and speak to the leaders. He said the place would be called the Valley of Slaughter, and Jeremiah was to shatter a jar as a sign.

cards.name: Mount Hor
cards.line: Mount Hor is a mountain near the border of Edom where Israel camped and where Aaron the priest died after the LORD told Moses to bring him up.

moments.title: Israel camps at Mount Hor
moments.text: After leaving Kadesh, all the people of Israel came to Mount Hor and camped near the border of Edom. There the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.

moments.title: Aaron dies on the mountain
moments.text: Moses took Aaron and his son Eleazar up Mount Hor as the LORD commanded. Moses put the priest's clothes on Eleazar, and Aaron died on top of the mountain, and Israel mourned him thirty days.

moments.title: Israel leaves Mount Hor
moments.text: Israel set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea to go around the land of Edom.

cards.name: Rephidim
cards.line: Rephidim was a camp in the wilderness where Israel found no water, fought the Amalekites, and then left to go on to the Wilderness of Sinai.

moments.title: No water to drink
moments.text: Israel camped at Rephidim, but there was no water. The people argued with Moses, and God told him to strike the rock at Horeb so water would come out for them.

moments.title: The Amalekites attack
moments.text: The Amalekites attacked Israel at Rephidim. Israel prevailed while Moses held up his hands, and Aaron and Hur held them steady until sunset, so Joshua overwhelmed Amalek with the sword.

moments.title: Leaving for Sinai
moments.text: After Israel set out from Rephidim, they entered the Wilderness of Sinai and camped in front of the mountain.

cards.name: Troas
cards.line: Troas was a port city on the northwest coast of Asia Minor where Paul saw a vision that sent the gospel across the sea to Macedonia.

moments.title: The call to Macedonia
moments.text: At Troas, Paul saw a man of Macedonia pleading, "Come over to Macedonia and help us." They concluded God had called them, and they sailed from Troas.

moments.title: Eutychus raised
moments.text: Paul and his companions joined the men waiting in Troas and stayed seven days. While Paul spoke late into the night, the young man Eutychus fell from a third-story window, and Paul embraced him and said he was alive.

moments.title: An open door
moments.text: Paul went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ, and a door stood open for him in the Lord. But he had no peace because he could not find Titus there, so he went on to Macedonia.

moments.title: The cloak left behind
moments.text: Paul asked Timothy to bring the cloak he had left with Carpus at Troas, along with his scrolls, especially the parchments.

cards.name: Crete
cards.line: Crete is a large island in the Mediterranean Sea where Paul's ship sailed along its coast on the way to Rome and where Paul later left Titus.

moments.title: Sailing along Crete
moments.text: Paul's ship sailed along the sheltered side of Crete, away from the wind, and stopped at Fair Havens. Paul warned that the trip was dangerous, but most chose to sail on toward Phoenix, a harbor in Crete, to spend the winter.

moments.title: The Northeaster strikes
moments.text: A gentle south wind began to blow, so the ship sailed along the coast of Crete. Soon a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island, and the ship was driven along by the wind.

moments.title: Titus left in Crete
moments.text: Paul wrote that he left Titus in Crete to set in order what was unfinished. Titus was to appoint elders in every town.

cards.name: Gihon
cards.line: Gihon is the name of a river in Eden and also of a spring near Jerusalem, where Solomon was anointed king and Hezekiah secured the city's water.

moments.title: A river of Eden
moments.text: Gihon is named as the second river of Eden. It winds through the whole land of Cush.

moments.title: Solomon anointed king
moments.text: King David told his men to take Solomon down to Gihon. There Zadok the priest anointed Solomon, the horn was blown, and the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!"

moments.title: Hezekiah redirects the spring
moments.text: Hezekiah blocked the upper outlet of the Spring of Gihon. He guided its water down toward the western side of David's city, and he prospered in all he did.

moments.title: Manasseh builds the wall
moments.text: After the LORD brought him back to Jerusalem, Manasseh rebuilt the outer wall of the City of David from west of Gihon in the valley. He made it much higher.

cards.name: Iconium
cards.line: Iconium was a large, rich city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preached, many people believed, and the two men fled a plot to stone them.

moments.title: Arriving in Iconium
moments.text: After they were pushed out of their district, Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet and went to Iconium.

moments.title: Preaching in the synagogue
moments.text: Paul and Barnabas spoke so well in the Jewish synagogue that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed. They stayed a long time, speaking boldly as the Lord gave them power to do signs and wonders.

moments.title: Returning to Iconium
moments.text: After preaching in Derbe, Paul and Barnabas went back through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch. They strengthened the believers and chose elders for each church.

moments.title: Timothy's good name
moments.text: The brothers in Lystra and Iconium spoke well of Timothy, a disciple Paul wanted to take along with him.

cards.name: Mount Gerizim
cards.line: Mount Gerizim is a mountain in Samaria near Shechem, where Israel was told to proclaim God's blessing when they entered the land He promised them.

moments.title: Moses gives the command
moments.text: Moses told Israel that after crossing the Jordan, six tribes would stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people. Six other tribes would stand on Mount Ebal to deliver the curse.

moments.title: Israel hears the law
moments.text: Israel stood half in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, on both sides of the ark. Joshua read aloud all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, to the whole assembly.

moments.title: Jotham's story from the mountain
moments.text: When the leaders of Shechem made Abimelech their king, Jotham climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim. He called out to them and told a story about trees looking for a king.

cards.name: Rameses
cards.line: Rameses was a district and city in Egypt where Joseph settled his family, and later the starting point of Israel's journey out of Egypt.

moments.title: Joseph settles his family
moments.text: Joseph settled his father and brothers in the best part of Egypt, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded. He also gave them food for their families.

moments.title: Israel leaves Egypt
moments.text: The Israelites set out from Rameses for Succoth. About 600,000 men on foot went, besides women and children.

moments.title: A bold march out
moments.text: The Israelites marched out of Rameses in full view of the Egyptians, who were burying their firstborn that the LORD had struck down. Then Israel camped at Succoth.

cards.name: Tarsus
cards.line: Tarsus was the chief city of Cilicia, known for its schools and trade, and it was the hometown of Saul, who became the apostle Paul.

moments.title: Ananias asks for Saul
moments.text: The Lord told Ananias to go to Straight Street in Damascus and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, who was praying. The Lord said Saul was His chosen instrument to carry His name to the Gentiles.

moments.title: Barnabas looks for Saul
moments.text: Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul. When he found him, he brought him back to Antioch, and they taught large numbers of people there for a year.

moments.title: Paul speaks of his hometown
moments.text: In Jerusalem, Paul told the Roman commander he was a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. He later told the crowd he was born in Tarsus.

cards.name: Ebenezer
cards.line: Ebenezer was a place where Israel camped to fight the Philistines, and it is the name Samuel gave a stone to remember that the LORD had helped Israel.

moments.title: Israel camps at Ebenezer
moments.text: The Israelites went out to fight the Philistines and camped at Ebenezer. Israel was defeated, and about four thousand men were struck down.

moments.title: The ark is taken away
moments.text: The Philistines captured the ark of God and took it from Ebenezer to Ashdod. There they placed it in the temple of Dagon.

moments.title: The stone of help
moments.text: After Israel chased the Philistines back, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer and said, "Thus far the LORD has helped us."

cards.name: Lystra
cards.line: Lystra was a city in Lycaonia where Paul healed a lame man, and where Timothy, who later joined Paul's work, was known as a disciple.

moments.title: Fleeing to Lystra
moments.text: Paul and Barnabas learned of a plan to mistreat and stone them, so they fled to Lystra and Derbe. There they kept preaching the gospel.

moments.title: A lame man walks
moments.text: A man in Lystra had been lame from birth. Paul saw that he had faith to be healed and told him to stand, and the man jumped up and walked.

moments.title: Mistaken for gods
moments.text: The crowds called Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes. The priest of Zeus brought bulls and wreaths to offer a sacrifice, but Barnabas and Paul tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd.

moments.title: Returning to strengthen disciples
moments.text: After preaching in Derbe, Paul and Barnabas came back to Lystra. They strengthened the disciples, encouraged them to continue in the faith, and appointed elders in each church.

moments.title: Timothy joins Paul
moments.text: In Lystra Paul found a disciple named Timothy, whom the brothers there spoke well of. Paul wanted Timothy to go with him.

cards.name: Thyatira
cards.line: Thyatira was a city in Asia Minor known for dyeing cloth, the hometown of Lydia and the home of one of the seven churches in Revelation.

moments.title: A letter to the church
moments.text: Jesus, the Son of God, with eyes like blazing fire, told the church in Thyatira He knew their love, faith, service, and not giving up. He also warned them about Jezebel, who misled His servants.

moments.title: Hold fast until I come
moments.text: Jesus spoke to the rest of the people in Thyatira who did not follow Jezebel's teaching. He asked them to hold fast to what they had until He comes.

cards.name: Valley of Hinnom
cards.line: The Valley of Hinnom is a deep, narrow ravine near Jerusalem that marked tribal borders and later became a picture of the place of the wicked.

moments.title: Border of Judah
moments.text: The border of Judah's land went up the Valley of Ben-hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusites, which is Jerusalem. It then climbed to the top of the hill facing the Valley of Hinnom.

moments.title: Border of Benjamin
moments.text: Benjamin's southern border ran down the Valley of Hinnom toward the southern slope of the Jebusites and on to En-rogel.

moments.title: People settle to the valley
moments.text: After the Exile, people of Judah settled in towns all the way from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.

cards.name: Zarephath
cards.line: Zarephath was a small Phoenician town between Tyre and Sidon where God sent Elijah to stay with a poor widow during a terrible famine.

moments.title: God sends Elijah there
moments.text: The LORD tells Elijah to go to Zarephath of Sidon and stay there. He says He has commanded a widow there to provide for him.

moments.title: Elijah meets the widow
moments.text: At the city gate, Elijah finds a widow gathering sticks and asks her for water and bread. She says she has only a handful of flour and a little oil, enough for one last meal for her and her son.

moments.title: The flour and oil do not run out
moments.text: Elijah tells her not to be afraid and promises that the jar of flour and jug of oil will not run out until the day the LORD sends rain. She obeys, and there is food every day for Elijah, the woman and her household.

cards.name: Brook Kidron
cards.line: The Kidron is a brook and valley below the eastern wall of Jerusalem, where altars were thrown out and Jesus crossed to a garden before His arrest.

moments.title: Altars thrown into the valley
moments.text: During Hezekiah's Passover celebration, the people removed the altars and incense altars in Jerusalem. They threw them into the Kidron Valley.

moments.title: Jesus crosses to the garden
moments.text: After He finished speaking to His disciples, Jesus went out with them across the Kidron Valley and entered a garden. Judas knew the place, and he brought soldiers and officers there.

cards.name: Caesarea Philippi
cards.line: Caesarea Philippi was a city near Mount Hermon, the northern limit of Jesus' ministry, where Peter declared that Jesus is the Christ.

moments.title: Who do you say I am?
moments.text: Near Caesarea Philippi, Jesus asked His disciples who people say He is, then asked who they say He is. Peter answered, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God."

moments.title: On this rock
moments.text: Jesus told Peter that his answer came from the Father in heaven. He said He would build His church on this rock, and the gates of Hades would not defeat it.

moments.title: The Son of Man must suffer
moments.text: After Peter answered, Jesus began to teach that He must suffer, be killed, and rise again after three days. Peter took Him aside and told Him He was wrong, and Jesus corrected Peter in return.

cards.name: Marah
cards.line: Marah was a place in the desert where Israel found bitter water after crossing the Red Sea, and where the LORD sweetened it and spoke of healing.

moments.title: Bitter water
moments.text: After walking three days in the desert without finding water, Israel came to Marah. They could not drink the water because it was bitter, so the people grumbled against Moses.

moments.title: The LORD sweetens the water
moments.text: Moses cried out to the LORD, and He showed him a log. When Moses threw it into the water, the water became sweet.

moments.title: A test and a promise
moments.text: At Marah the LORD tested Israel. He told them that if they listened to Him and obeyed, He would not bring on them the diseases of Egypt, for He is the LORD who heals them.

cards.name: Nain
cards.line: Nain was a town in Galilee, near the plain of Esdraelon, where Jesus raised a widow's only son from the dead at the town gate.

moments.title: Jesus meets a funeral
moments.text: As Jesus came near the town gate with His disciples and a large crowd, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of a widow. When the Lord saw her, He had compassion and told her, "Do not weep."

moments.title: The dead son lives again
moments.text: Jesus touched the coffin and told the young man to get up. The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.

moments.title: The people praise God
moments.text: Awe swept over everyone, and they glorified God, saying a great prophet had appeared and that God had visited His people. The news spread through Judea and the surrounding region.

cards.name: Pergamum
cards.line: Pergamum was a city in Asia Minor where one of the seven churches stood, and Jesus spoke to it, praising its faithfulness and warning it to repent.

moments.title: Jesus speaks to Pergamum
moments.text: Jesus praises the church for holding fast to His name even when Antipas was killed, but tells it to repent of false teaching. To the one who overcomes, He promises hidden manna and a white stone.

cards.name: Philadelphia
cards.line: Philadelphia was a city in Asia Minor, home to one of the seven churches that Jesus wrote to in Revelation, and He praised it for staying faithful.

moments.title: A letter to Philadelphia
moments.text: Jesus tells the church He has set an open door before it that no one can shut. Though its strength was small, it kept His word and did not deny His name.

cards.name: Sardis
cards.line: Sardis was a city in Asia Minor and the home of one of the seven churches that Jesus spoke to in the book of Revelation.

moments.title: Wake up, Sardis
moments.text: Jesus tells the church in Sardis that it has a reputation for being alive, yet it is dead. He tells them to wake up, strengthen what remains, remember what they heard, and repent.

moments.title: A few in white
moments.text: Jesus says a few people in Sardis have not soiled their garments. They are worthy and will walk with Him in white.

cards.name: Siloam
cards.line: Siloam was a pool near Jerusalem, whose name means "Sent," where Jesus sent a blind man to wash and he came back seeing.

moments.title: The tower of Siloam falls
moments.text: Eighteen people in Jerusalem were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them. Jesus used this to teach that everyone needs to repent.

moments.title: A blind man washes and sees
moments.text: Jesus put mud on a blind man's eyes and told him to wash in the Pool of Siloam. The man went, washed, and came back seeing.

cards.name: Smyrna
cards.line: Smyrna was a city in Asia Minor, about 40 miles north of Ephesus, and it was home to one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation.

moments.title: A message to the church in Smyrna
moments.text: The First and the Last, who died and returned to life, knows the church's suffering and poverty. He tells them not to fear, to be faithful even to death, and promises them the crown of life.

cards.name: Areopagus
cards.line: The Areopagus was a rocky hill in Athens where a famous court met, and where Paul told the city's thinkers about the God who made everything.

moments.title: Paul is brought to the hill
moments.text: Philosophers took Paul to the Areopagus. They asked him to explain his new teaching about Jesus and the resurrection, because it sounded strange to them.

moments.title: Paul speaks about the unknown God
moments.text: Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus and spoke about an altar marked TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. He said the God who made the world and gives everyone life is the One he was proclaiming.

moments.title: Some believe
moments.text: When Paul left the Areopagus, some people joined him and believed. They included Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris.

cards.name: Berea
cards.line: Berea was a city in Macedonia where Paul and Silas went after leaving Thessalonica, and where people eagerly checked the Scriptures to see if the teaching was true.

moments.title: Paul and Silas arrive
moments.text: The brothers sent Paul and Silas away at night to Berea. When they arrived, they went into the Jewish synagogue.

moments.title: Fair-minded Bereans
moments.text: The Bereans received the message with great eagerness and studied the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true. Many of them believed, and so did quite a few important Greek women and men.

moments.title: Trouble follows Paul
moments.text: Jews from Thessalonica heard that Paul was telling God's word in Berea, so they came to stir up the crowds. The brothers sent Paul to the coast right away, while Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.

cards.name: Bethesda
cards.line: Bethesda was a pool in Jerusalem by the Sheep Gate, with five covered walkways where many sick people lay, and where Jesus spoke to a man.

moments.title: Jesus Asks a Sick Man
moments.text: Jesus saw a man who had been sick for thirty-eight years lying by the pool and asked, "Do you want to get well?" The man said he had no one to help him into the water.

moments.title: Told to Get Up and Walk
moments.text: Jesus told the man, "Get up, pick up your mat, and walk."

cards.name: Cherith
cards.line: Cherith is a brook valley east of the Jordan where God sent Elijah to hide and cared for him during a time of drought.

moments.title: Ravens bring food
moments.text: Elijah obeys and lives by the brook. Each morning and evening the ravens bring him bread and meat, and he drinks from the brook.

cards.name: Melita
cards.line: Melita, now called Malta, is the Mediterranean island where Paul and his shipmates came safely ashore after the shipwreck on their way to Rome.

moments.title: Safe on shore
moments.text: Everyone from the ship reached land safely and learned the island was called Malta. The islanders showed extraordinary kindness and built a fire because it was cold and rainy.

moments.title: The viper
moments.text: A viper fastened itself to Paul's hand as he laid sticks on the fire. Paul shook it off and was not harmed, so the islanders changed their minds and said he was a god.

moments.title: Welcomed by Publius
moments.text: Publius, the chief official of the island, had an estate nearby. He welcomed Paul and his companions and treated them kindly for three days.

cards.name: Straight Gate
cards.line: Straight Gate is named as a landmark, but the verses and source given only describe Straight Street in Damascus, where the Lord sent Ananias to find Saul.

moments.title: The Lord sends Ananias
moments.text: In a vision the Lord tells Ananias to go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for Saul of Tarsus, who is praying. Ananias speaks of the harm Saul has done, but the Lord says Saul is His chosen instrument.

cards.name: Sychar
cards.line: Sychar was a town of Samaria near Jacob's well, where Jesus stopped, weary from His journey, and spoke with a Samaritan woman about living water.

moments.title: Jesus rests at Jacob's well
moments.text: Jesus came to Sychar, a town of Samaria near the plot of ground Jacob gave to Joseph. Weary from His journey, He sat down by Jacob's well about the sixth hour.

cards.name: Valley of Aijalon
cards.line: The Valley of Aijalon was a valley in land first given to Dan, where Joshua asked God to make the moon stand still.

moments.title: The moon stands still
moments.text: Joshua asked the sun to stand still over Gibeon and the moon over the Valley of Aijalon. They stopped until Israel defeated its enemies, because the LORD fought for Israel.

cards.name: Aram
cards.line: Aram was the highland region northeast of Israel toward the Euphrates, later led by Damascus, and it is where Jacob fled and where David won a victory.

moments.title: Balaam brought from Aram
moments.text: Balaam says King Balak brought him from Aram to curse Israel. Balaam answers that he cannot curse those whom God has not cursed.

moments.title: David rules Aram of Damascus
moments.text: David puts soldiers in camps in Aram of Damascus. The Arameans become his servants and bring him payments, and the LORD makes David victorious wherever he goes.

moments.title: Absalom's claim about a vow
moments.text: Absalom tells David he made a promise to the LORD while living in Geshur of Aram. He uses this promise as his reason to go to Hebron.

moments.title: Jacob flees to Aram
moments.text: Hosea recalls that Jacob fled to the land of Aram. There Israel worked for a wife and tended sheep for her.

cards.name: Gibeah
cards.line: Gibeah was a city of Benjamin where a terrible crime led to war against the tribe, and where Saul, Israel's first king, later made his home.

moments.title: No Room for the Levite
moments.text: A Levite and his party passed by a foreign city and stopped at Gibeah for the night. He sat in the city square, but no one would take them into his home until an old man welcomed them.

moments.title: Benjamin Defends Gibeah
moments.text: The Benjamites refused to hand over the wicked men of Gibeah. They gathered at Gibeah to fight Israel, and twice they struck down thousands of Israelites there.

moments.title: The Trap and the Fall of Gibeah
moments.text: Israel hid men around Gibeah as a trap and drew the Benjamites away from the city. The hidden men rushed in and destroyed the whole city with their swords.

moments.title: Saul Goes Home
moments.text: After Samuel explained the rights of a king to the people, Saul went home to Gibeah. Brave men whose hearts God had touched went with him.

cards.name: Ramoth-gilead
cards.line: Ramoth-gilead was a city of refuge east of the Jordan, in Gad's land, and later a battleground between Israel and Aram where Ahab died and Jehu was anointed king.

moments.title: A city of refuge
moments.text: The LORD told Israel to set apart cities where someone who killed by accident could flee. Ramoth in Gilead, from the tribe of Gad, was named as one of them.

moments.title: Ahab wants the city back
moments.text: King Ahab said Ramoth-gilead belonged to Israel but Aram still held it. He asked Jehoshaphat of Judah to fight with him to take it.

moments.title: Ahab dies in battle
moments.text: The kings went up to Ramoth-gilead. Ahab disguised himself, but an arrow struck him and he died that evening, as the LORD had said.

moments.title: Jehu anointed king
moments.text: Elisha sent a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead with a flask of oil. He anointed Jehu king over Israel, and the army commanders then proclaimed, "Jehu is king!"

cards.name: Seir
cards.line: Seir is a mountain region southeast of the Dead Sea, the land of Esau and the Edomites, which God gave to Esau as his own possession.

moments.title: Jacob sends word to Esau
moments.text: Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom. They returned with news that Esau was coming to meet Jacob with four hundred men.

moments.title: Esau settles in Seir
moments.text: The possessions of Esau and Jacob were too great for them to live together. So Esau moved away and settled in the area of Mount Seir.

moments.title: Israel passes by Seir
moments.text: God told Israel not to provoke the descendants of Esau in Seir, because He had given Mount Seir to Esau, and to pay for the food and water. So Israel passed by their brothers.

moments.title: Seir's men fall in battle
moments.text: As Judah's singers praised the LORD, He set ambushes against the armies that came against Judah, including men of Mount Seir. The Ammonites and Moabites then destroyed the men of Seir, and afterward helped destroy one another.

cards.name: Heshbon
cards.line: Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amorites, which Israel captured and the tribe of Reuben later rebuilt.

moments.title: Israel captures Heshbon
moments.text: After Israel defeated Sihon in battle, they captured all the cities of the Amorites and lived in them, including Heshbon and its villages. Heshbon was Sihon's city.

moments.title: Reubenites rebuild Heshbon
moments.text: Moses gave Sihon's kingdom to Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh. The Reubenites then built up Heshbon and other cities.

cards.name: Lachish
cards.line: Lachish was a strong city south of Jerusalem that Joshua captured, and later Assyria's king used it as a base when he attacked Judah.

moments.title: Joshua captures Lachish
moments.text: Joshua and all Israel surrounded Lachish and attacked it. The LORD delivered it into Israel's hand, and Joshua captured it on the second day.

moments.title: King Amaziah is killed
moments.text: Men plotted against King Amaziah in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. Men were sent after him, and they killed him there.

moments.title: Hezekiah pays Assyria
moments.text: Sennacherib king of Assyria captured the walled cities of Judah. Hezekiah sent word to him at Lachish, saying he had done wrong, and he paid the silver and gold the king demanded.

moments.title: Assyria sends an army to Jerusalem
moments.text: While Sennacherib and all his forces attacked Lachish, he sent officers with a great army to Jerusalem. His servants spoke against the LORD and against Hezekiah.

cards.name: Ashdod
cards.line: Ashdod was a Philistine city near the Mediterranean coast, where the captured ark of God was taken and where Dagon fell before the LORD.

moments.title: Dagon falls before the ark
moments.text: The Philistines set the ark of God beside Dagon's statue in his temple at Ashdod. Two mornings in a row, Dagon was found fallen on his face before the ark of the LORD, and the second time his head and hands were broken off.

moments.title: The LORD's hand is heavy on Ashdod
moments.text: The hand of the LORD was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and He made them sick with tumors. The men of Ashdod said the ark of the God of Israel must not stay with them.

moments.title: Uzziah tears down the walls
moments.text: King Uzziah went to war against the Philistines and tore down the walls of Ashdod. Then he built cities near Ashdod and among the Philistines.

moments.title: Assyria captures Ashdod
moments.text: Sargon king of Assyria sent his chief commander, who attacked and captured Ashdod. Before that, the LORD had spoken through Isaiah about a sign against Egypt and Cush.

cards.name: Cyprus
cards.line: Cyprus is a large island in the Mediterranean Sea where Barnabas and Saul preached on their first journey sent by the Holy Spirit, and where Barnabas later sailed with Mark.

moments.title: Sent out to Cyprus
moments.text: The Holy Spirit sent Barnabas and Saul out, and they sailed from Seleucia to Cyprus. At Salamis they told God's word in the Jewish meeting places, with John as their helper.

moments.title: The sorcerer is struck blind
moments.text: At Paphos, the Roman governor Sergius Paulus wanted to hear God's word, but the sorcerer Elymas fought against it. Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, spoke against him, and Elymas went blind for a time, so the governor believed.

moments.title: Barnabas returns with Mark
moments.text: Paul and Barnabas disagreed sharply about taking Mark with them. They parted company, and Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus.

cards.name: Uz
cards.line: Uz was a region, probably east or southeast of Palestine, where Job lived, and it is also named in Jeremiah and Lamentations among peoples facing God's judgment.

moments.title: Job lives in Uz
moments.text: A man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was blameless and upright, feared God, and was the greatest man of all the people of the East.

cards.name: Paddan-aram
cards.line: Paddan-aram was the region around Haran, home of Rebekah's family, where Jacob was sent to find a wife and where he gained his family and wealth.

moments.title: Isaac marries Rebekah
moments.text: Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah. She was the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban.

moments.title: Jacob leaves with his family
moments.text: Jacob put his children and wives on camels and drove his livestock ahead of him. He took all the possessions he had gained in Paddan-aram and set out for his father Isaac in Canaan.

moments.title: God blesses Jacob again
moments.text: After Jacob returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him and blessed him. God changed his name from Jacob to Israel.

cards.name: Beth-shemesh
cards.line: Beth-shemesh was a city for priests on the border of Judah, about 14 miles west of Jerusalem, where the ark of the LORD returned from the Philistines.

moments.title: The ark comes home
moments.text: The Philistines sent the ark on a cart pulled by two cows. The cows went straight up the road to Beth-shemesh, where the people harvesting wheat were overjoyed to see it.

moments.title: Offerings at the large rock
moments.text: The cart stopped in Joshua's field near a large rock. The people chopped up the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering, and the Levites placed the ark on the rock.

moments.title: Seventy struck down
moments.text: God struck down seventy men of Beth-shemesh because they looked inside the ark. The people asked who can stand in the presence of the LORD, this holy God, and sent messengers to Kiriath-jearim to come and take the ark.

moments.title: Judah loses to Israel
moments.text: Amaziah would not listen to the warning of Jehoash, so the two kings faced each other at Beth-shemesh. Judah was defeated, and Jehoash captured Amaziah there.

cards.name: Hazor
cards.line: Hazor was a strong Canaanite city in northern Canaan, ruled by kings named Jabin, which Joshua burned and which Assyria later captured.

moments.title: Joshua burns Hazor
moments.text: Jabin king of Hazor gathered northern kings to fight Israel, and after the LORD gave Israel the victory, Joshua captured Hazor, killed its king, and burned the city. Of the cities built on their mounds, Hazor was the only one he burned.

moments.title: Jabin treats Israel harshly
moments.text: After Israel again did evil, the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin, who reigned in Hazor. His commander was Sisera, and Jabin was harsh to Israel for twenty years.

moments.title: Assyria captures Hazor
moments.text: In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria captured Hazor and other places. He took the people away as prisoners to Assyria.

cards.name: Kiriath-jearim
cards.line: Kiriath-jearim was a city on the border of Judah and Benjamin, best known as the place where the ark of the LORD stayed for twenty years.

moments.title: A city of the Gibeonites
moments.text: After the Israelites learned the Gibeonites lived nearby, they went to their cities. Kiriath-jearim was one of them.

moments.title: A border city
moments.text: Kiriath-jearim, also called Baalah and Kiriath-baal, marked part of the border of Judah. It was also on the edge of Benjamin's land.

moments.title: The Danites camp here
moments.text: Six hundred Danites went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim. The place west of it was called Mahaneh-dan.

moments.title: The ark comes to Kiriath-jearim
moments.text: The Philistines sent back the ark, and the men of Kiriath-jearim came for it. They took it to Abinadab's house on the hill and set apart his son Eleazar to guard it, and it stayed there twenty years.

moments.title: David brings the ark out
moments.text: David gathered all Israel and went up to Kiriath-jearim to bring up the ark of God. Later, he brought it to the tent he had pitched in Jerusalem.

cards.name: Succoth
cards.line: Succoth was a city east of the Jordan where Jacob built shelters for his livestock, and where Gideon later punished leaders who refused to help his tired troops.

moments.title: Jacob builds a home
moments.text: Jacob went on to Succoth. There he built a house for himself and shelters for his livestock, and that is why the place was called Succoth.

moments.title: Land in the valley
moments.text: Succoth was named among the cities in the valley on the east side of the Jordan. It was part of the territory of King Sihon of Heshbon.

moments.title: Gideon is refused bread
moments.text: Gideon asked the men of Succoth for bread for his worn-out troops. The leaders refused, asking if he already had the two Midianite kings in his hands.

moments.title: Gideon returns
moments.text: Gideon captured a young man of Succoth, who wrote down the names of seventy-seven leaders and elders. Gideon then took the elders and disciplined the men of Succoth with the thorns and briers of the wilderness.

cards.name: Ashkelon
cards.line: Ashkelon was one of the five Philistine cities, a seaport on the Mediterranean coast, and it is where Samson went after he lost his riddle contest.

moments.title: Samson pays his riddle debt
moments.text: After the men of the city solved his riddle, the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon Samson. He went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty men, and gave their clothes to those who had solved the riddle.

cards.name: Paran
cards.line: Paran is a desert region south of Canaan, in the Sinai area, where Ishmael lived, Israel camped, and spies were sent out to look at the Promised Land.

moments.title: Ishmael grows up
moments.text: God was with Hagar's son, and he grew up in the wilderness and became a great archer. While he lived in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother got a wife for him from Egypt.

moments.title: The cloud settles
moments.text: Israel left the Wilderness of Sinai at the LORD's command through Moses. They traveled from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran.

moments.title: Spies sent to Canaan
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to send one leader from each tribe to spy out Canaan. Moses sent them out from the Wilderness of Paran.

moments.title: The spies report
moments.text: After forty days the spies came back to Paran at Kadesh and showed the fruit of the land. Caleb said Israel could take the land, but some of the men who went up with him said the people there were too strong.

moments.title: David goes down to Paran
moments.text: After Samuel died and Israel mourned him, David went down to the Wilderness of Paran.

cards.name: Ziklag
cards.line: Ziklag was a city in southern Judah that a Philistine king gave to David, and it was his home while he was away from Saul.

moments.title: Achish gives David Ziklag
moments.text: David asked Achish for a town of his own, away from the royal city. Achish gave him Ziklag, and to this day it still belongs to the kings of Judah.

moments.title: Ziklag burned and its people taken
moments.text: David and his men came home to find Ziklag burned down by the Amalekites, and their wives and children carried off. The men wept until they had no strength left, but David found strength in the LORD his God.

moments.title: Gifts from the plunder
moments.text: After David won back what was taken, he returned to Ziklag. He sent part of the plunder as gifts to the elders of Judah and to his friends in many towns.

moments.title: News of Saul's death
moments.text: David stayed in Ziklag two days after the fight with the Amalekites. Then a man from Saul's camp told him that Saul and Jonathan were dead, and David and his men tore their clothes, mourned, and fasted.

moments.title: Mighty men join David
moments.text: While David was still kept away from Saul, skilled fighters came to him at Ziklag. Some were archers and slingers from Saul's own tribe of Benjamin.

cards.name: Mount Seir
cards.line: Mount Seir is a hill country God gave to Esau's family, the Edomites, which Israel passed by and which God later spoke against for its hatred.

moments.title: Israel wanders near Seir
moments.text: Israel wandered around Mount Seir for many days. Then the LORD told them to turn north and not to provoke Esau's descendants, because He had given Mount Seir to Esau.

moments.title: Simeonites settle on Mount Seir
moments.text: Five hundred Simeonites went to Mount Seir and struck down the Amalekites who had escaped. The writer says they have lived there to this day.

moments.title: God speaks against Mount Seir
moments.text: The LORD told Ezekiel to speak His message against Mount Seir. He said He would turn it into an empty ruin because of its ancient hatred of Israel.

cards.name: Arabia
cards.line: Arabia is a large, dry region of deserts and tribes southeast of Israel, known for trade and caravans, and where Paul went after meeting Jesus.

moments.title: A message against Arabia
moments.text: Isaiah spoke a burden against Arabia. He told the caravans of Dedanites to lodge in its thickets, and he said the glory of Kedar would be gone within a year.

moments.title: Paul goes into Arabia
moments.text: After God revealed His Son to him, Paul did not go to the apostles in Jerusalem. He went into Arabia and later returned to Damascus.

moments.title: Hagar and Mount Sinai
moments.text: Paul wrote that Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia. He used her as a picture of slavery, and he said believers are children of the free woman.

cards.name: Great Sea
cards.line: The Great Sea is the Mediterranean Sea, which marked the western edge of the land God promised to Israel.

moments.title: The western border
moments.text: Moses tells Israel that the coastline of the Great Sea will be their western boundary. The northern border also begins at the Great Sea and runs to Mount Hor.

moments.title: Land to the Great Sea
moments.text: God tells Joshua that Israel's territory will reach west as far as the Great Sea. He promises to be with Joshua and never leave him.

moments.title: Kings along the coast
moments.text: When the kings west of the Jordan hear the news, including those all along the coast of the Great Sea, they come together to wage war against Joshua and Israel.

moments.title: Judah's western border
moments.text: The western border of the clans of Judah is the coastline of the Great Sea.

moments.title: Boundaries in Ezekiel's vision
moments.text: The Lord GOD gives the boundaries of the land. The Great Sea marks the western edge, and the northern and southern borders both reach to it.

cards.name: Media
cards.line: Media was a land and kingdom east of Assyria, later joined with Persia, and its name appears in the stories of Ezra, Esther, Isaiah, and Daniel.

moments.title: Cyrus's order found
moments.text: King Darius ordered a search of the old records. A scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media, with Cyrus's order to rebuild the house of God in Jerusalem.

cards.name: Cyrene
cards.line: Cyrene was a Greek city in North Africa with many Jews, and the Bible names people from there who met Jesus and served the early church.

moments.title: Simon carries the cross
moments.text: Soldiers forced Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country, to carry the cross of Jesus as He was led away to be crucified.

moments.title: Cyrene at Pentecost
moments.text: People from the parts of Libya near Cyrene were among the visitors in Jerusalem. They heard the believers declaring the wonders of God in their own languages.

moments.title: Good news for the Greeks
moments.text: Some men from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and began telling the Greeks the good news about the Lord Jesus. The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed.

moments.title: Lucius leads at Antioch
moments.text: Lucius of Cyrene was one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch. The Holy Spirit set apart Barnabas and Saul for His work, and the church sent them off.

cards.name: Engedi
cards.line: En-gedi was a city in the wilderness of Judah near the Dead Sea, where David hid from King Saul and spared his life.

moments.title: David hides in En-gedi
moments.text: David went up and lived in the safe places of En-gedi. Saul was told that David was in the wilderness of En-gedi.

moments.title: David spares Saul in the cave
moments.text: Saul went into a cave where David and his men were hiding. David cut off a corner of Saul's robe, but he would not harm the man the LORD had chosen as king, and he held his men back.

moments.title: Enemy army at En-gedi
moments.text: Men told King Jehoshaphat that a vast army was coming and was already at Hazazon-tamar, which is En-gedi. Jehoshaphat sought the LORD and called Judah to fast.

moments.title: Fishermen along the shore
moments.text: Ezekiel saw a river flowing from the temple that makes the waters fresh. Fishermen would stand by the shore and spread their nets from En-gedi to En-eglaim.

cards.name: Greece
cards.line: Greece is a land in southeast Europe that the prophets name as a coming power, and where Paul stayed three months on his mission.

moments.title: Paul arrives in Greece
moments.text: After encouraging believers in the area, Paul comes to Greece and stays three months. When the Jews plot against him, he decides to go back through Macedonia.

cards.name: Jabbok
cards.line: The Jabbok is a stream east of the Jordan River where Jacob wrestled and was renamed Israel, and which later marked the border of the Ammonites.

moments.title: Jacob crosses the ford
moments.text: In the night Jacob took his wives, servants, and eleven sons across the ford, a shallow place to cross the Jabbok. He sent all his possessions across too.

moments.title: Jacob wrestles and is renamed
moments.text: After the family crossed the Jabbok, Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until daybreak. Jacob would not let go without a blessing, and the man said his name would now be Israel.

moments.title: Israel takes Sihon's land
moments.text: Israel defeated King Sihon and took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok. They stopped at the Ammonite border, because that border was strongly defended.

moments.title: Jabbok marks the Ammonite border
moments.text: Moses told how he gave the Reubenites and Gadites land that reached up to the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.

moments.title: Ammonite king claims the land
moments.text: The Ammonite king said Israel had taken his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok. Jephthah replied that the LORD had given Israel that land from the Amorites.

cards.name: Salem
cards.line: Salem is a city whose name means peace, ruled by Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, and often thought to be Jerusalem.

moments.title: Melchizedek, king of Salem
moments.text: Melchizedek is called king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He is named as king of Salem when he brings out bread and wine for Abram.

moments.title: God's tent in Salem
moments.text: A psalm says God's tent is in Salem and His dwelling place is in Zion. There He shattered the weapons of war.

moments.title: King of righteousness and peace
moments.text: Hebrews says Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. It explains that "king of Salem" means "king of peace."

cards.name: Sharon
cards.line: Sharon in 1 Chronicles 5:16 was a region with pasturelands, probably east of the Jordan near Gilead and Bashan, and it is named as a place where people lived.

moments.title: Families live in Sharon's pastures
moments.text: The people of this group lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its towns, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon. Their names were put in the family records in the days of Jotham and Jeroboam.

cards.name: Chebar
cards.line: The Chebar was a waterway in Chaldean land where Jewish exiles lived, and where God gave Ezekiel visions and spoke His word to him.

moments.title: Visions of God
moments.text: While Ezekiel was among the exiles by the River Kebar, the heavens opened and he saw visions of God. The word of the LORD came to him there, and the LORD's hand was upon him.

moments.title: Sitting with the exiles
moments.text: The Spirit brought Ezekiel to the exiles at Tel-abib by the River Kebar. He sat among them for seven days, overwhelmed, and then the LORD made him a watchman for Israel.

cards.name: Italy
cards.line: Italy is the land in southern Europe where Rome stood, and in the Bible Jews left it, Paul sailed toward it, and its people sent greetings.

moments.title: Jews ordered out of Rome
moments.text: Aquila and Priscilla had recently come from Italy to Corinth. Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome, so they left.

moments.title: Paul is set to sail for Italy
moments.text: It was decided that they would sail for Italy. Paul and other prisoners were handed over to an army officer named Julius.

moments.title: Greetings from those of Italy
moments.text: Near the end of Hebrews, the writer says that those from Italy send greetings. The verses do not say where they were when they sent them.

cards.name: Massah
cards.line: Massah was a place in the wilderness where Israel tested the LORD by doubting Him, and the name became a warning to remember.

moments.title: Water from the rock
moments.text: God told Moses He would stand by the rock at Horeb, and water would come out when Moses struck it. Moses did this in front of the elders of Israel.

moments.title: A name for the quarrel
moments.text: Moses named the place Massah and Meribah because the Israelites quarreled and tested the LORD, asking, "Is the LORD among us or not?"

moments.title: Levi tested at Massah
moments.text: Moses said that God tested His godly one at Massah and contested with him at the waters of Meribah. This was part of Moses' blessing on Levi.

cards.name: Ophrah
cards.line: Ophrah was the hometown of Gideon, where God called him to save Israel from Midian, but the name also belongs to a city in Benjamin.

moments.title: The angel calls Gideon
moments.text: The angel of the LORD sat under the oak in Ophrah, where Gideon was beating wheat in a winepress, a pit where grapes were crushed, to hide it from the Midianites. The LORD told him to go in his strength and save Israel.

moments.title: The altar called The LORD Is Peace
moments.text: The LORD told Gideon not to be afraid, for he would not die. Gideon built an altar there and called it The LORD Is Peace, and it still stood in Ophrah when this was written.

moments.title: Gideon's ephod
moments.text: Gideon made an ephod, a special priest's garment, from the gold and placed it in Ophrah, his hometown. All Israel worshiped it there, and it became a trap for Gideon and his household.

moments.title: Gideon is buried
moments.text: Gideon died at a ripe old age. He was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

moments.title: Abimelech kills his brothers
moments.text: Abimelech went to his father's house in Ophrah and murdered his seventy brothers on one stone. Jotham, the youngest, survived because he hid himself.

cards.name: Pamphylia
cards.line: Pamphylia was a coastal region in southern Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached on their first journey and where John Mark left the team.

moments.title: John leaves at Perga
moments.text: Paul and his friends sailed from Paphos to Perga in Pamphylia. There John left them and went back to Jerusalem.

moments.title: Preaching in Perga
moments.text: After passing through Pisidia, Paul and Barnabas came to Pamphylia and spoke the word in Perga. Then they went down to Attalia and sailed to Antioch.

cards.name: Pisgah
cards.line: Pisgah is a mountain peak in Moab, east of the Jordan, where Balak built altars and where the LORD showed Moses the promised land.

moments.title: Balak's altars on Pisgah
moments.text: Balak took Balaam to the top of Pisgah and built seven altars, offering a bull and a ram on each. There the LORD met Balaam and put a message in his mouth, a blessing that could not be changed.

moments.title: Moses told to look
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to go to the top of Pisgah and see the land with his own eyes, because he would not cross the Jordan. Joshua would lead the people across.

moments.title: Moses sees the land
moments.text: Moses went up to the top of Pisgah, and the LORD showed him the whole land He had sworn to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses died there in Moab, as the LORD had said.

cards.name: Timnah
cards.line: Timnah was a town of Judah, later held by the Philistines, and sources name two towns called Timnah, one tied to Samson's wife.

moments.title: Judah heads to Timnah
moments.text: After his wife died, Judah went up to Timnah to his sheepshearers. Tamar sat at Enaim, on the way to Timnah, to meet him.

moments.title: Samson wants a wife
moments.text: Samson went down to Timnah and saw a young Philistine woman. He told his parents to get her for him as a wife.

moments.title: The lion in the vineyards
moments.text: On the way to Timnah, a young lion came roaring at Samson in the vineyards. The Spirit of the LORD came powerfully on him, and he tore the lion apart with his bare hands.

moments.title: The Philistines take Timnah
moments.text: In the days of King Ahaz, the Philistines raided the cities of Judah and took Timnah and its villages. The LORD humbled Judah because Ahaz had been most unfaithful to Him.

cards.name: Nob
cards.line: Nob was a city of the priests near Jerusalem, where David found help while running from Saul and where Saul later had the priests killed.

moments.title: David Gets Bread and a Sword
moments.text: David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest, while fleeing from Saul. Ahimelech gave him the bread set apart for God, and later gave him the sword of Goliath.

moments.title: Saul Destroys Nob
moments.text: Saul had Doeg the Edomite strike down the priests, and Doeg also killed the people of Nob and its animals. Abiathar, a son of Ahimelech, escaped and fled to David.

moments.title: An Enemy Halts at Nob
moments.text: Isaiah says an enemy army will stop at Nob and shake a fist at Jerusalem. Then the LORD will cut down the mighty with terrifying power.

cards.name: Shittim
cards.line: Shittim was Israel's camp in the plains of Moab, near the Jordan across from Jericho, where Israel sinned and later set out to enter the promised land.

moments.title: Israel worships Baal of Peor
moments.text: While Israel stayed at Shittim, the men fell into sexual sin with Moabite women and joined in worshiping Baal of Peor. The anger of the LORD burned against them.

moments.title: Joshua sends two spies
moments.text: Joshua secretly sent two spies from Shittim to inspect the land, especially Jericho. The men then went to Jericho.

moments.title: Leaving for the Jordan
moments.text: Early in the morning Joshua and all the Israelites left Shittim and went to the Jordan. They camped there before crossing over.

cards.name: Tiberias
cards.line: Tiberias was a city on the Sea of Galilee, built by Herod Antipas and named for the emperor Tiberius, and boats from it appear in John 6.

moments.title: Boats from Tiberias
moments.text: After Jesus gave thanks and fed the people with bread, some boats from Tiberias landed near that spot. The crowd then got into boats and went to Capernaum to look for Jesus.

cards.name: Topheth
cards.line: Topheth was a place in the Valley of Ben-hinnom near Jerusalem where children were burned in the fire, and God warned it would become a burial ground.

moments.title: Topheth Made Unclean
moments.text: King Josiah made Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom unclean. He did this so that no one could sacrifice a son or daughter in the fire to Molech there.

moments.title: A Place of Child Sacrifice
moments.text: The LORD said the people of Judah built the high places of Topheth to burn their sons and daughters in the fire. He said He never commanded it, and it never even entered His mind.

moments.title: The Valley of Slaughter
moments.text: The LORD said Topheth would one day be called the Valley of Slaughter. The dead would be buried there until there was no more room.

moments.title: The Shattered Jar
moments.text: At Topheth, Jeremiah was to shatter a jar and say that God would shatter Jerusalem the same way. The LORD said He would make the city like Topheth.

moments.title: Jeremiah Returns to the Temple
moments.text: The LORD had sent Jeremiah to Topheth to deliver God's message. Then he went back to the courtyard of the LORD's house and told all the people that disaster was coming because they would not listen.

cards.name: Valley of Achor
cards.line: The Valley of Achor, meaning "Trouble," is where Achan's sin was judged, and later the Bible promises God will turn it into a place of rest and hope.

moments.title: Achan's sin judged
moments.text: Joshua and all Israel brought Achan and everything he owned to the Valley of Achor. After he was stoned, they heaped a large pile of rocks over him, and the LORD turned from His burning anger.

moments.title: A name that stays
moments.text: Because of what happened there, the place was called the Valley of Achor. The writer says it was still called that "to this day."

moments.title: A resting place for herds
moments.text: God promised that the Valley of Achor would become a resting place for herds, for His people who seek Him.

moments.title: A gateway of hope
moments.text: God said He would lead Israel into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her. There He would make the Valley of Achor into a gateway of hope.

cards.name: Baal-peor
cards.line: Baal-peor is a mountain tied to Baal of Peor, a god of Moab, where Israel joined in worshiping him and the Bible remembers it as a warning.

moments.title: Israel follows Baal of Peor
moments.text: Israel joined themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices offered to lifeless gods. This made the LORD angry, and a plague broke out among them.

moments.title: Moses reminds Israel
moments.text: Moses told the people they had seen what the LORD did at Baal-peor. He destroyed all who followed Baal of Peor, but those who held fast to the LORD were still alive.

moments.title: Hosea recalls the shame
moments.text: The LORD said He found Israel like grapes in the wilderness, but they went to Baal-peor and gave themselves to Shame. They became as hateful as the thing they loved.

cards.name: Bethphage
cards.line: Bethphage was a village on the Mount of Olives near Bethany, where Jesus sent two disciples ahead to fetch a colt before He went into Jerusalem.

moments.title: Jesus sends two disciples
moments.text: As Jesus came near Jerusalem and reached Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, He sent two disciples ahead. He told them to untie a colt and bring it to Him, and to say, "The Lord needs it."

moments.title: Jesus gives the colt instructions
moments.text: Mark tells how Jesus came to Bethphage and Bethany at the Mount of Olives and sent two disciples ahead. He told them to find a colt that no one had ever sat on and bring it to Him.

moments.title: A King on a donkey
moments.text: Matthew says this happened to fulfill the words of the prophet: the King comes to Zion, gentle and riding on a donkey. The disciples did as Jesus told them and brought the donkey and the colt.

cards.name: Decapolis
