cards.line: The Decapolis was a region of ten cities near the Sea of Galilee, where a healed man told people what Jesus had done and Jesus healed a deaf man.

moments.title: A healed man tells his story
moments.text: Jesus told the man to go home and tell his people how much the Lord had done for him. He went and proclaimed it throughout the Decapolis, and everyone was amazed.

moments.title: A deaf man healed
moments.text: Jesus came into the region of the Decapolis, where people brought Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak. Jesus opened his ears and freed his tongue, and the people were utterly astonished.

cards.name: En-dor
cards.line: Endor was a city in Issachar given to Manasseh, where King Saul sought out a medium on the night before his last battle.

moments.title: Saul visits the medium
moments.text: After the LORD did not answer him, Saul disguised himself and went at night to a medium at Endor. He asked her to bring up Samuel for him.

moments.title: A place of defeat
moments.text: Psalm 83 remembers Endor as a place where Sisera and Jabin perished. The psalmist asks God to deal with Israel's enemies in the same way.

cards.name: Ephrathah
cards.line: Ephrathah is an old name for Bethlehem in Judah, the town linked to Boaz, Ruth, and King David's family line.

moments.title: A blessing at the gate
moments.text: After Boaz tells the elders and the people that he has acquired Ruth as his wife, they say they are witnesses. They ask the LORD to make him prosperous in Ephrathah and famous in Bethlehem.

moments.title: News of the ark
moments.text: The psalm says, "We heard that the ark was in Ephrathah." The people then found it in the fields of Jaar and called one another to go worship at God's dwelling place.

cards.name: Gennesaret
cards.line: Gennesaret was a fertile plain on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus landed from the boat and healed many sick people who came to Him.

moments.title: The sick are healed
moments.text: Jesus and His disciples landed at Gennesaret, and the people recognized Him. They brought all their sick, and everyone who touched the fringe of His cloak was healed.

moments.title: Healed in every place He went
moments.text: When they landed at Gennesaret, people recognized Jesus and ran through the whole region carrying the sick on mats. Everyone who touched the fringe of His cloak was healed.

cards.name: Kishon
cards.line: The Kishon is a winter stream in central Israel where God defeated Sisera's army and where Elijah had the prophets of Baal put to death.

moments.title: Sisera drawn to the Kishon
moments.text: Through Deborah, God promised to draw Sisera, his chariots, and his troops to the River Kishon and give him into Barak's hand. Sisera then gathered his nine hundred iron chariots there.

moments.title: The river sweeps them away
moments.text: In Deborah's song, the stars fought against Sisera and the River Kishon swept his army away.

moments.title: Prophets of Baal at the Kishon
moments.text: After the people declared that the LORD is God, Elijah ordered the prophets of Baal seized. He brought them down to the Kishon Valley and killed them there.

cards.name: Magog
cards.line: Magog is a northern land ruled by Gog, named in Ezekiel's message against him and in Revelation for nations that gather to fight God's people.

moments.title: Fire on Magog
moments.text: God says He will send fire on Magog and on those who live securely in the coastlands. Then they will know that He is the LORD.

cards.name: Mount Ebal
cards.line: Mount Ebal is a mountain near Shechem where Israel was told to set up the law on stones, build an altar, and speak the curses.

moments.title: Stones and an altar commanded
moments.text: Moses tells Israel that after they cross the Jordan they must set up plastered stones on Mount Ebal and write all the words of the law on them. They are also to build an altar of uncut stones there to the LORD.

moments.title: Six tribes for the curse
moments.text: Moses says that when Israel crosses the Jordan, six tribes will stand on Mount Ebal to deliver the curse. The Levites will then call out the curses, and all the people will answer, 'Amen!'

moments.title: Joshua builds the altar
moments.text: Joshua builds an altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal, just as Moses commanded. Israel offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, and Joshua writes a copy of the law on the stones.

moments.title: The blessings and curses are read
moments.text: All Israel stands on both sides of the ark, half in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal. Joshua reads aloud all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, to everyone, including women, children, and foreigners.

cards.name: Penuel
cards.line: Penuel, also called Peniel, was a place east of the Jordan where Jacob met God, and later a city that Gideon punished and Jeroboam built up.

moments.title: Jacob leaves limping
moments.text: After Jacob saw God face to face and his life was spared, he named the place Peniel. The sun rose as he passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.

moments.title: Gideon is refused help
moments.text: Gideon asked the men of Penuel for bread for his tired men while he chased Zebah and Zalmunna. The men of Penuel gave the same answer as Succoth, and Gideon promised to tear down their tower after he won.

moments.title: Gideon tears down the tower
moments.text: After Gideon captured Zebah and Zalmunna, he pulled down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.

moments.title: Jeroboam builds Penuel
moments.text: Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and built Penuel.

cards.name: Sheep Gate
cards.line: The Sheep Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt by priests in Nehemiah's day, and it was near the pool of Bethesda where Jesus healed a man.

moments.title: Priests start the work
moments.text: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests began rebuilding at the Sheep Gate. They dedicated it and installed its doors.

moments.title: Goldsmiths and merchants repair
moments.text: The goldsmiths and merchants made repairs on the wall between the upper room above the corner and the Sheep Gate.

moments.title: Thanksgiving walk on the wall
moments.text: On the day of thanksgiving, a choir and Nehemiah with half the people walked along the top of the wall as far as the Sheep Gate. Then they stopped at the Gate of the Guard.

moments.title: Jesus at the pool nearby
moments.text: A pool called Bethesda was near the Sheep Gate, and many sick people lay there. Jesus told a man who had been sick for thirty-eight years to get up, pick up his mat, and walk.

cards.name: Shunem
cards.line: Shunem was a city in Issachar's land, where the Philistines camped before Saul's last battle and where a woman welcomed Elisha into her home.

moments.title: A city for Issachar
moments.text: When the land was divided, Shunem was named among the cities in the territory given to the tribe of Issachar.

moments.title: The Philistines camp at Shunem
moments.text: The Philistines gathered and camped at Shunem, while Saul gathered all Israel at Gilboa. When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid and trembled violently.

moments.title: A woman feeds Elisha
moments.text: A prominent woman of Shunem persuaded Elisha to have a meal. Whenever he passed by, he stopped there to eat.

cards.name: Water Gate
cards.line: The Water Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, near Ophel, where the people gathered to hear God's Law read aloud and to celebrate a feast.

moments.title: Repairs near the Water Gate
moments.text: The temple servants living on the hill of Ophel repaired a section of the wall opposite the Water Gate toward the east.

moments.title: Ezra reads the Law
moments.text: All the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate and asked Ezra to bring out the Book of the Law. He read it aloud from daybreak until noon, and the people listened closely.

moments.title: Booths in the squares
moments.text: The people brought back branches and made booths, including in the squares by the Water Gate. They had not celebrated like this since the days of Joshua, and there was great rejoicing.

cards.name: Akeldama
cards.line: Akeldama, meaning Field of Blood, was the potter's field bought with the money paid to Judas, and it became a burial place for foreigners near Jerusalem.

moments.title: The potter's field is bought
moments.text: The leaders used the silver to buy the potter's field as a burial place for foreigners. That is why it has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

moments.title: Judas and the Field of Blood
moments.text: Judas bought a field with the reward for his wickedness, and he fell there and died. Everyone in Jerusalem heard of it, so they called the field Akeldama, which means Field of Blood.

cards.name: Beth-shan
cards.line: Beth-shan was a city where the Philistines hung King Saul's body after he died in battle, and where brave men from Jabesh-gilead came to take it down.

moments.title: Saul's body hung on the wall
moments.text: After Saul died, the Philistines put his armor in the temple of the Ashtoreths. They hung his body on the wall of Beth-shan.

moments.title: Brave men take the bodies
moments.text: When the people of Jabesh-gilead heard the news, their men of valor traveled all night. They took the bodies of Saul and his sons down from the wall of Beth-shan.

cards.name: Chorazin
cards.line: Chorazin was a city where Jesus did many miracles, but its people did not repent, so He warned them of judgment.

moments.title: Jesus warns Chorazin
moments.text: Jesus spoke sadly about cities where He did most of His miracles, because the people did not turn from their sins. He said, "Woe to you, Chorazin!"

moments.title: Woe to Chorazin in Luke
moments.text: Luke also records Jesus saying, "Woe to you, Chorazin!" He said Tyre and Sidon would have turned from their sins long ago if they had seen those miracles.

cards.name: Dothan
cards.line: Dothan is a city north of Samaria where Joseph found his brothers, and where God protected the prophet Elisha from an enemy army.

moments.title: Joseph finds his brothers
moments.text: Joseph goes looking for his brothers and finds them at Dothan. They plot to kill him, but Reuben speaks up to save his life, and they strip Joseph of his robe of many colors.

moments.title: The king hunts Elisha
moments.text: The king of Aram learns that Elisha is in Dothan. He sends horses, chariots, and a great army by night to surround the city.

moments.title: Fiery chariots on the hills
moments.text: Elisha's servant is afraid when he sees the army. Elisha prays, and the LORD opens the young man's eyes to see the hills full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

moments.title: The army struck blind
moments.text: Elisha prays, and the LORD strikes the Arameans with blindness. Elisha then tells them to follow him and leads them to Samaria.

cards.name: Elim
cards.line: Elim was a green camping place in the desert, with twelve springs and seventy palm trees, where Israel stopped after leaving Marah on the way to Sinai.

moments.title: Camp by the springs
moments.text: Israel came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees. They camped there by the waters.

moments.title: Leaving Elim
moments.text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after leaving Egypt, all the Israelites set out from Elim. They came to the Desert of Sin, between Elim and Sinai.

cards.name: Ephrath
cards.line: Ephrath, also called Bethlehem, is a city that Jacob's family was traveling toward when Rachel died on the road after giving birth to Benjamin.

moments.title: Rachel's hard labor
moments.text: Jacob's family left Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began a difficult labor. The midwife told her not to be afraid, because she was having another son.

moments.title: Rachel dies on the way
moments.text: Rachel named her son Ben-oni with her last breath, but Jacob called him Benjamin. She was buried on the way to Ephrath, and Jacob set up a pillar on her grave.

cards.name: Miletus
cards.line: Miletus was a seaport city in Asia Minor, about 36 miles south of Ephesus, where Paul called the Ephesian elders to meet him.

moments.title: Paul Stops at Miletus
moments.text: Paul has decided to sail past Ephesus because he is in a hurry to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost. His ship comes opposite Chios, then arrives at Samos, and then comes to Miletus.

moments.title: Paul Calls the Elders
moments.text: From Miletus, Paul sends for the elders of the church at Ephesus and reminds them how he served the Lord and taught them. He says he is going to Jerusalem, and the Holy Spirit warns him that chains wait for him.

moments.title: Trophimus Left Sick
moments.text: Paul writes that he left Trophimus sick in Miletus.

cards.name: Paphos
cards.line: Paphos was a city on the island of Cyprus where Paul and Barnabas met a Roman governor who believed, before they sailed on to Perga.

moments.title: Paul faces Elymas
moments.text: At Paphos, the Roman governor, Sergius Paulus, wanted to hear God's word, but the sorcerer Elymas tried to turn him from the faith. Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, said Elymas would be blind for a time, and darkness came over him at once.

moments.title: Sailing from Paphos
moments.text: Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. There John left them to return to Jerusalem.

cards.name: Solomon's Portico
cards.line: Solomon's Portico was a covered walkway, probably on the east side of the temple, where crowds gathered and the first believers met in Jerusalem.

moments.title: Peter speaks to the crowd
moments.text: After a man who had been begging was healed, the people ran to Peter and John in the walkway. Peter told them the man was made strong by faith in the name of Jesus, whom God raised from the dead.

moments.title: Signs and wonders
moments.text: The apostles did many signs and wonders among the people, and the believers gathered together in the walkway. More and more people came to believe in the Lord, and the sick were healed.

cards.name: Hiddekel
cards.line: Hiddekel is the Bible's old name for the Tigris, a great river named as one of four rivers of Eden and the place where Daniel saw a vision.

moments.title: A river of Eden
moments.text: The Tigris is named as the third river of Eden. It runs along the east side of Assyria.

moments.title: Daniel's vision by the river
moments.text: Daniel is standing on the bank of the great river, the Tigris, when he looks up and sees a man dressed in linen. Only Daniel sees the vision, and he is left powerless until a hand touches him.

cards.name: Bethlehem Ephrathah
cards.line: Bethlehem Ephrathah is a small town in Judah that God chose as the place where a future ruler of Israel, whose origins are from eternity, would come.

moments.title: A ruler will come from here
moments.text: God says that although Bethlehem Ephrathah is small among the clans of Judah, One will come out of it to be ruler over Israel. His origins are of old, from the days of eternity.

cards.name: Gabbatha
cards.line: Gabbatha, also called the Stone Pavement, was the place outside Pilate's judgment hall where he sat in judgment and handed Jesus over to be crucified.

moments.title: Pilate sits in judgment
moments.text: Pilate brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at the Stone Pavement, which in Hebrew is Gabbatha. He said to the Jews, "Here is your King!"

moments.title: Jesus handed over to be crucified
moments.text: The chief priests said, "We have no king but Caesar." Then Pilate handed Jesus over to be crucified, and the soldiers took Him away.

cards.name: Lehi
cards.line: Lehi was a town in Judah where Samson, helped by the Spirit of the LORD, defeated the Philistines, and where God gave him water when he was thirsty.

moments.title: Philistines gather near Lehi
moments.text: The Philistines went up, camped in Judah, and deployed themselves near the town of Lehi. They came to arrest Samson.

moments.title: Samson breaks free
moments.text: When Samson arrived in Lehi, the Philistines came out shouting, and the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. The ropes broke loose from his hands, and with a fresh donkey's jawbone he struck down a thousand men.

moments.title: Water from the hollow place
moments.text: Samson was very thirsty and cried out to the LORD. God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and when Samson drank, his strength returned.

cards.name: Myra
cards.line: Myra was a city in Lycia, near the sea in what is now called Asia Minor, where Paul and the others moved to a ship headed for Italy.

moments.title: Paul arrives at Myra
moments.text: After sailing across the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia, Paul and those with him came to Myra in Lycia.

moments.title: A ship bound for Italy
moments.text: At Myra the Roman officer found a ship from Alexandria sailing for Italy and put Paul and the others on board.

cards.name: Peniel
cards.line: Peniel, also spelled Penuel, is the place near the Jabbok where Jacob wrestled with God and was blessed, and where he named it "face of God."

moments.title: Jacob names Peniel
moments.text: God blessed Jacob there. Jacob named the place Peniel because he had seen God face to face and his life was spared.

moments.title: Jacob leaves limping
moments.text: The sun rose as Jacob passed by Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip. To this day the Israelites do not eat the tendon attached to the hip socket.

cards.name: Pithom
cards.line: Pithom was an Egyptian store city for Pharaoh, built by Israelite slaves, and it shows how harshly Egypt treated God's people before the exodus.

moments.title: Israelites build Pithom
moments.text: The Egyptians set taskmasters over the Israelites and forced them to work. They built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.

cards.name: Plain of Jordan
cards.line: The Plain of Jordan was a well-watered stretch of land that Lot chose for himself when he and Abram parted ways, near wicked Sodom.

moments.title: Lot chooses the plain
moments.text: Lot looked out and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, was well watered like the garden of the LORD. He chose it for himself and set out toward the east, and Abram and Lot parted company.

cards.name: Raamses
cards.line: Raamses, also spelled Rameses, was a store city in Egypt that the Israelites built for Pharaoh while they were forced to work as slaves.

moments.title: Slaves build a store city
moments.text: The Egyptians put bosses over the Israelites and forced them to work hard. They built Pithom and Rameses as cities to store goods for Pharaoh.

cards.name: Spain
cards.line: Spain was a far western land where Paul hoped to travel and preach the gospel, a plan he shared in his letter to the church in Rome.

moments.title: Paul plans to go to Spain
moments.text: Paul tells the believers in Rome he hopes to see them on his way to Spain. After he delivers the gift for the poor in Jerusalem, he says he will set off for Spain by way of Rome.

cards.name: Tishbe
cards.line: Tishbe was the town linked to Elijah the Tishbite, the prophet who told King Ahab that no rain would fall except at his word.

moments.title: Elijah the Tishbite
moments.text: Elijah is called the Tishbite, a name tied to Tishbe, and he is described as among the settlers of Gilead. He tells King Ahab that no dew or rain will fall except at his word.

cards.name: Valley of Jehoshaphat
cards.line: The Valley of Jehoshaphat is the place where God says He will gather all the nations to judge them for how they treated His people Israel.

moments.title: God gathers the nations
moments.text: God says that when He restores Judah and Jerusalem, He will bring all the nations down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There He will judge them for scattering His people and dividing up His land.

moments.title: God sits to judge
moments.text: The nations are called to advance to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, where God will sit down to judge them all. Crowds fill the valley of decision, for the Day of the LORD is near.

cards.name: Valley of Sorek
cards.line: The Valley of Sorek was a valley, a dry stream bed in the western hills of Judah, and it was the home of Delilah, the woman Samson loved.

moments.title: Samson loves Delilah
moments.text: Samson fell in love with a woman in the Valley of Sorek named Delilah. The Philistine lords asked her to find the source of his great strength, and they offered her eleven hundred shekels of silver each.

cards.name: Geba
cards.line: Geba was a city of Benjamin, north of Jerusalem, that marked the northern edge of Judah and was the site of key moments under Saul and Asa.

moments.title: Jonathan attacks the outpost
moments.text: Jonathan attacked the Philistine outpost at Geba, and the Philistines heard about it. Saul then blew the ram's horn so all the Hebrews would hear.

moments.title: Asa builds up Geba
moments.text: King Asa called all the men of Judah to carry away the stones and timbers Baasha had used at Ramah. With them he built up Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

moments.title: Geba marks Judah's northern edge
moments.text: Josiah made the high places unfit for worship where priests had burned incense. This reached across Judah, from Geba in the north to Beersheba in the south.

cards.name: Tekoa
cards.line: Tekoa was a town in Judah, south of Jerusalem, home of a wise woman who spoke to David and of the prophet Amos the shepherd.

moments.title: Joab sends for a wise woman
moments.text: Joab wanted David to bring Absalom home. He sent to Tekoa for a wise woman and told her to act like a mourner and speak to the king.

moments.title: Rehoboam makes Tekoa strong
moments.text: Rehoboam built up cities in Judah to keep them safe, and Tekoa was one of them. He added strong walls, officers, food, shields, and spears.

moments.title: Amos the shepherd of Tekoa
moments.text: Amos was among the sheepherders of Tekoa. His words about Israel were given in the days when Uzziah was king of Judah.

cards.name: Anathoth
cards.line: Anathoth was a priests' city in the land of Benjamin, a few miles from Jerusalem, and it was the hometown of the prophet Jeremiah.

moments.title: A city given to the priests
moments.text: Anathoth was one of four cities in Benjamin's land that were given to the family of Aaron the priest, along with the grassy land around it for their animals.

moments.title: Abiathar's fields in Anathoth
moments.text: King Solomon told the priest Abiathar to go back to his fields in Anathoth. He spared Abiathar's life because he had carried the ark before David and shared David's sufferings.

moments.title: Jeremiah the priest of Anathoth
moments.text: Jeremiah was one of the priests of Anathoth. The LORD called him to be a prophet to the nations, someone who speaks God's words.

moments.title: Danger from Anathoth's people
moments.text: The people of Anathoth were seeking Jeremiah's life and told him not to speak for the LORD, or they would kill him. The LORD said He would punish them.

moments.title: A field in Anathoth is bought
moments.text: As the LORD had said, Jeremiah's cousin Hanamel came to him in the courtyard of the guard and asked him to buy his field in Anathoth. Jeremiah paid seventeen shekels of silver and signed the deed before witnesses.

cards.name: Ekron
cards.line: Ekron was the northernmost of the five main Philistine cities, where the ark of God caused great fear and where King Ahaziah wrongly sought help from Baal-zebub.

moments.title: The ark comes to Ekron
moments.text: The Philistines sent the ark of God to Ekron. The people cried out in fear that it would kill them, so the rulers were told to send it back to its place.

moments.title: Rulers return to Ekron
moments.text: The five Philistine rulers watched the ark reach Beth-shemesh and then went back to Ekron. The Philistines had sent a gold tumor for each of their cities, including Ekron, as a guilt offering to the LORD.

moments.title: The Philistines flee to Ekron
moments.text: After David struck down Goliath, Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout. They chased the Philistines to the gates of Ekron, and bodies lay along the road.

cards.name: Jabesh-gilead
cards.line: Jabesh-gilead was a city east of the Jordan River whose people were punished by Israel, rescued by King Saul, and later honored Saul by burying him.

moments.title: Judged for missing the gathering
moments.text: No one from Jabesh-gilead came to the meeting at Mizpah. Israel sent 12,000 men against the city, and four hundred young women who were unmarried were brought to Shiloh and given to the Benjamites.

moments.title: Nahash lays siege
moments.text: Nahash the Ammonite surrounded the city. The elders asked for seven days to look for someone to save them, and sent messengers throughout Israel.

moments.title: Hope of rescue
moments.text: Messengers brought word that help would come the next day. The men of Jabesh rejoiced and told Nahash they would come out to him the next day.

moments.title: Saul is buried
moments.text: The brave men of Jabesh-gilead traveled all night to take the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan. They burned them, buried the bones under the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and fasted seven days.

moments.title: David honors their kindness
moments.text: At Hebron, the men of Judah made David king and told him the men of Jabesh-gilead had buried Saul. David sent messengers to them, asking the LORD to bless them for their kindness.

cards.name: Rabbah
cards.line: Rabbah was the chief city of the Ammonites, east of the Jordan, and it is where David's army fought and the prophets said God would bring ruin.

moments.title: Og's iron bed
moments.text: Moses said that only Og, king of Bashan, had remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. His iron bed, about nine cubits (roughly 13 feet) long, was still in Rabbah of the Ammonites.

moments.title: Joab surrounds Rabbah
moments.text: In the spring, David sent Joab and the whole army of Israel to destroy the Ammonites and surround Rabbah. David stayed in Jerusalem.

moments.title: David captures the city
moments.text: Joab took the royal fortress and the water supply, then asked David to bring the rest of the troops. David came and captured Rabbah, and he took the king's gold crown and much plunder.

moments.title: Jeremiah's message
moments.text: The LORD said through Jeremiah that He would sound the battle cry against Rabbah. It would become a heap of ruins, and its villages would be burned.

moments.title: Ezekiel's message
moments.text: Because Ammon cheered when Israel was laid waste, the Lord GOD said He would make Rabbah a pasture for camels. Then they would know that He is the LORD.

cards.name: Mahanaim
cards.line: Mahanaim was a city east of the Jordan River, named by Jacob after he saw God's camp, and later a royal base for Ish-bosheth and David.

moments.title: Jacob Names Mahanaim
moments.text: As Jacob traveled, the angels of God met him. He said, "This is the camp of God," and named the place Mahanaim.

moments.title: Ish-bosheth Made King
moments.text: Abner, the commander of Saul's army, moved Saul's son Ish-bosheth to Mahanaim. There he made him king over Israel, while Judah followed David.

moments.title: David Finds Help
moments.text: David came to Mahanaim, where Shobi, Machir, and Barzillai met him. They brought beds, food, and supplies for his hungry and tired people.

moments.title: Barzillai Provides for the King
moments.text: Barzillai, a very wealthy man of eighty, had provided for David while he stayed in Mahanaim. David asked him to come to Jerusalem, but Barzillai asked to go home, so David kissed him and blessed him.

cards.name: Beth-horon
cards.line: Beth-horon was a pair of towns, Upper and Lower, on a steep road near Gibeon, where Israel won a great battle and where Solomon later built strong walls.

moments.title: Chased down the pass
moments.text: The LORD threw Israel's enemies into confusion at Gibeon. Israel chased them along the uphill road to Beth-horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

moments.title: Hailstones from the sky
moments.text: As the enemy fled down from Beth-horon toward Azekah, the LORD cast large hailstones on them. More died from the hailstones than from the swords of Israel.

moments.title: Solomon builds up the towns
moments.text: Solomon rebuilt Upper and Lower Beth-horon as strong cities, built up for defense with walls, gates, and bars.

cards.name: Debir
cards.line: Debir, also called Kiriath-sepher, was a city that Israel captured under Joshua and that Caleb's people marched against, where Othniel won Caleb's daughter Acsah as his wife.

moments.title: Joshua conquers Debir
moments.text: Joshua and all Israel turned toward Debir and fought against it. They captured the city, its king, and its villages, and left no survivors, as they had done at Hebron and Libnah.

moments.title: Caleb marches on Debir
moments.text: Caleb marched against the people of Debir, which used to be called Kiriath-sepher. He promised his daughter Acsah in marriage to the man who would capture it, and Othniel did.

cards.name: Hormah
cards.line: Hormah was a Canaanite city in the south, once called Zephath, where Israel was driven back after rebelling and later won a victory and named the place.

moments.title: Israel Is Driven Back
moments.text: Israel went up into the hill country without the ark or Moses. The Amalekites and Canaanites attacked them and chased them all the way to Hormah.

moments.title: Israel's Vow and Victory
moments.text: Israel vowed to the LORD to destroy the Canaanite cities if He gave them the people. The LORD heard, and Israel named the place Hormah.

moments.title: Moses Remembers the Defeat
moments.text: Moses told the people they had rebelled and gone up anyway, and the Amorites chased them like a swarm of bees all the way to Hormah. Afterward they returned and wept before the LORD.

moments.title: Judah and Simeon Take Zephath
moments.text: The men of Judah went with the Simeonites and attacked the Canaanites in Zephath. They devoted the city to destruction, so it was called Hormah.

cards.name: Tirzah
cards.line: Tirzah was an old Canaanite city that later became a royal home for the kings of northern Israel, where kings reigned, fell, and died.

moments.title: A king of Tirzah is listed
moments.text: The king of Tirzah is named as one of the kings in a list. The verse says there were thirty-one kings in all.

moments.title: Jeroboam's son dies
moments.text: Jeroboam's wife went to Tirzah. As soon as she stepped over the threshold of the house, the boy died.

moments.title: Baasha reigns in Tirzah
moments.text: Baasha became king of all Israel in the third year of Asa's reign over Judah. He reigned in Tirzah twenty-four years.

moments.title: Zimri kills Elah
moments.text: King Elah was in Tirzah getting drunk when his servant Zimri plotted against him. Zimri killed him and reigned in his place.

moments.title: Omri surrounds Tirzah
moments.text: Omri and the Israelites marched up and surrounded Tirzah. When Zimri saw the city was captured, he burned the royal palace down upon himself.

cards.name: Kedesh
cards.line: Kedesh was a city of refuge in Naphtali's hill country in Galilee, where Barak gathered his army and which Assyria later captured.

moments.title: A city of refuge
moments.text: Israel set apart Kedesh in Galilee as one of the cities of refuge. Someone who killed another person by accident could flee there and be safe from the avenger of blood.

moments.title: Deborah and Barak gather the army
moments.text: Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh, where he called together the men of Zebulun and Naphtali. Ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah went too.

moments.title: Captured by Assyria
moments.text: In the days of King Pekah, Tiglath-pileser of Assyria captured Kedesh and the land of Naphtali. He took the people to Assyria as captives.

cards.name: Aphek
cards.line: Aphek, meaning "strength," is the name of several Bible towns, including places where the Philistines gathered for war and where Israel fought the Arameans.

moments.title: Philistines camp at Aphek
moments.text: The Israelites camped at Ebenezer while the Philistines camped at Aphek. Then the battle began.

moments.title: Philistines gather forces
moments.text: The Philistines brought all their forces together at Aphek, while Israel camped by the spring in Jezreel.

moments.title: Victory over the Arameans
moments.text: Ben-hadad led the Arameans up to Aphek to fight Israel. The LORD gave Israel the victory, and a wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the men who fled into the city.

moments.title: Elisha's promise of victory
moments.text: Elisha had the king of Israel shoot an arrow from the east window. He said it was the LORD's arrow of victory, and Israel would strike the Arameans in Aphek.

cards.name: Bozrah
cards.line: Bozrah was a fortress city in Edom, home of an early Edomite king, and the prophets named it when they spoke of God's judgment on Edom.

moments.title: Jobab from Bozrah
moments.text: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah reigned in his place over Edom. Bozrah is named as the city he came from.

moments.title: A sacrifice in Bozrah
moments.text: Isaiah says the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom. It is part of His day of vengeance, when He pays back wrong.

moments.title: One coming from Bozrah
moments.text: Isaiah asks who is coming from Edom, from Bozrah, in clothes stained crimson. The answer is, "It is I, proclaiming that right has won, mighty to save."

moments.title: Bozrah to be a ruin
moments.text: The LORD swears by Himself that Bozrah will become an empty waste, a disgrace, a ruin, and a curse. He says an eagle will spread its wings over Bozrah, and Edom's mighty men will be afraid.

moments.title: Fire on Bozrah's fortresses
moments.text: Because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, the LORD says He will send fire upon Teman to burn up the strong towers of Bozrah.

cards.name: Brook of Egypt
cards.line: The Brook of Egypt was a stream that marked the far southwestern edge of the land God gave Israel, near the Great Sea.

moments.title: Southern border of Judah
moments.text: Judah's southern border ran to Azmon, joined the Brook of Egypt, and ended at the Sea.

moments.title: Southern edge of the land
moments.text: In Ezekiel's vision of the land, the southern border ran from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea.

cards.name: Peor
cards.line: Peor is a mountain peak in Moab where Balak took Balaam to curse Israel, and its name later came to mean Israel's sin and the plague.

moments.title: Balak takes Balaam up Peor
moments.text: Balak led Balaam to the top of Peor, hoping God would let him curse Israel from there. Balaam had seven altars built, and Balak offered a bull and a ram on each one.

moments.title: The plague because of Peor
moments.text: Israel was led into unfaithfulness to the LORD at Peor through the counsel of Balaam. A plague struck the congregation, and the LORD later told Israel to attack the Midianites for what they did there.

moments.title: Remembering the sin of Peor
moments.text: When the tribes west of the Jordan feared that an altar was rebellion, they asked if the sin of Peor was not enough. They reminded everyone that it had brought a plague on the LORD's people.

cards.name: Shinar
cards.line: Shinar is the plain between the rivers, later called Babylonia, where people began to build the tower city of Babel and where Nimrod's kingdom began.

moments.title: Nimrod's kingdom begins
moments.text: Nimrod's kingdom began in Babylon, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar. From there he went on into Assyria and built Nineveh and other cities.

moments.title: The tower of Babel
moments.text: People settled on a plain in Shinar and began to build a city and a tower to make a name for themselves. The LORD confused their language and scattered them over all the earth, and they stopped building the city.

moments.title: Temple items carried to Shinar
moments.text: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar take King Jehoiakim and some objects from God's house. Nebuchadnezzar carried the objects to the land of Shinar and put them in the treasury of his god.

cards.name: Valley of Rephaim
cards.line: The Valley of Rephaim is a valley near Jerusalem, close to the border of Judah and Benjamin, where the Philistines camped and David fought them.

moments.title: First Philistine Battle
moments.text: The Philistines spread out in the Valley of Rephaim. David asked the LORD if he should go up, and He promised to give David victory over them, so David defeated them at Baal-perazim.

moments.title: Water from Bethlehem
moments.text: Philistines camped in the valley while David longed for water from Bethlehem's well. Three mighty men broke through the camp to bring it, and David poured it out to the LORD.

moments.title: Second Philistine Battle
moments.text: The Philistines came again to the valley. The LORD told David to circle behind them and wait for the sound in the balsam trees, and David obeyed and struck them down from Gibeon to Gezer.

cards.name: Zin
cards.line: Zin is a desert region south of Canaan, where Israel's spies searched the land, Miriam died, and Moses and Aaron failed to honor God at the waters.

moments.title: The spies search the land
moments.text: Men sent by Moses spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob. They brought back a giant cluster of grapes, pomegranates, and figs from the land.

moments.title: Miriam dies at Kadesh
moments.text: Israel entered the Wilderness of Zin and stayed in Kadesh, where Miriam died and was buried. Soon the people had no water and quarreled with Moses and Aaron.

moments.title: Moses and Aaron at Meribah
moments.text: At the waters of Meribah-kadesh in Zin, Moses and Aaron broke faith with God by failing to treat Him as holy in front of Israel. Because of this, Moses would see the land but not enter it.

moments.title: A border for Judah
moments.text: Zin marked the southern edge of the land God gave Israel. The tribe of Judah received land reaching to the Wilderness of Zin.

cards.name: Azekah
cards.line: Azekah was a city of Judah in the low hills, where God sent hailstones on fleeing enemies and where Babylon's army later fought against Judah.

moments.title: Hailstones on the road to Azekah
moments.text: As the Amorite armies fled from Israel, the LORD cast down large hailstones on them along the descent from Beth-horon to Azekah. More of them died from the hailstones than from the swords of the Israelites.

moments.title: Philistines camp near Azekah
moments.text: The Philistines gathered for war at Socoh in Judah and camped between Socoh and Azekah. Israel stood across the valley from them.

moments.title: Babylon fights against Azekah
moments.text: Babylon's army was fighting against Jerusalem, Lachish, and Azekah. These were the only cities with strong defenses still left in Judah.

cards.name: Ezion-geber
cards.line: Ezion-geber was an ancient harbor city on the Red Sea, near Elath, where Israel camped in the wilderness and where kings of Israel and Judah built ships.

moments.title: Israel camps at Ezion-geber
moments.text: On their journey through the wilderness, the Israelites set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber. Then they moved on to Kadesh in the Wilderness of Zin.

moments.title: Solomon goes to Ezion-geber
moments.text: After the house of the LORD was finished, Solomon went to Ezion-geber and Eloth on the coast of Edom. Hiram sent ships and skilled sailors, who went with Solomon's servants to Ophir and brought back 450 talents of gold.

moments.title: Jehoshaphat's ships are wrecked
moments.text: Jehoshaphat joined with Ahaziah to build ships at Ezion-geber to sail to Tarshish. Eliezer prophesied against him, and the ships were wrecked and never sailed.

cards.name: Geshur
cards.line: Geshur was a small kingdom northeast of Bashan whose people Israel did not drive out, and it became the place where David's son Absalom took refuge.

moments.title: Geshurites stay in the land
moments.text: The Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites. Geshur and Maacath kept living among the Israelites.

moments.title: Absalom flees to Geshur
moments.text: After Amnon's death, Absalom fled to Talmai, the king of Geshur, and stayed there three years. David mourned for his son every day.

moments.title: Joab brings Absalom home
moments.text: Joab saw that David longed for Absalom. Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

moments.title: A vow made in Geshur
moments.text: Absalom later told David that while he was living in Geshur of Aram, he had vowed to worship the LORD in Hebron if the LORD brought him back to Jerusalem.

cards.name: Migdol
cards.line: Migdol, meaning "tower," is a name for places on Egypt's edge, including a camp near the sea where Israel stopped and a city named in warnings.

moments.title: Camp Near Migdol
moments.text: God told Moses to have the Israelites turn back and camp by the sea, between Migdol and the sea. Pharaoh would think they were boxed in, and God would gain honor over him.

moments.title: A Stop on the Journey
moments.text: Israel set out from Etham, turned back to Pi-hahiroth, and camped near Migdol. From there they crossed through the sea into the wilderness.

moments.title: Jews Living in Egypt
moments.text: God's word came to Jeremiah about the Jews living in Egypt, including those in Migdol. God reminded them that Jerusalem lay in ruins because of the evil of the people.

moments.title: Warning of Babylon's Sword
moments.text: God told Jeremiah to announce in Egypt, and to proclaim in Migdol and other cities, that Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon was coming against Egypt. Egypt's warriors would fall.

moments.title: From Migdol to Syene
moments.text: God said He would turn Egypt into a ruin, an empty wasteland from Migdol to Syene. He said Egypt's allies would fall by the sword, from Migdol to Syene.

cards.name: Riblah
cards.line: Riblah was an ancient city in the land of Hamath, where foreign kings made their base and where Judah's last kings and leaders met hard punishment.

moments.title: Jehoahaz Imprisoned
moments.text: Pharaoh Neco locked up Jehoahaz at Riblah so he could not rule in Jerusalem. Neco also made Judah pay a heavy fine of silver and gold.

moments.title: Zedekiah Judged
moments.text: Soldiers from Babylon caught King Zedekiah and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where the king decided his punishment. Zedekiah's sons were killed before his eyes, and then he was blinded and taken to Babylon in bronze chains.

moments.title: Leaders Put to Death
moments.text: Nebuzaradan brought the priests, officials, and other men taken from Jerusalem to the king of Babylon at Riblah. There the king put them to death, and the people of Judah were taken away from their own land.

cards.name: Shur
cards.line: Shur is a desert region on the northeast edge of Egypt, where Hagar met God, Israel walked after the Red Sea, and Ishmael's family settled.

moments.title: Hagar on the road to Shur
moments.text: Hagar ran away from Sarai, and the angel of the LORD found her by a spring on the road to Shur. He told her to go back and promised her many descendants.

moments.title: Abraham between Kadesh and Shur
moments.text: Abraham settled between Kadesh and Shur and stayed in Gerar. There God warned King Abimelech in a dream to return Sarah to him.

moments.title: Ishmael's family settles
moments.text: Ishmael's descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, near the border of Egypt. The account also tells of Ishmael's death at 137 years.

moments.title: Israel in the Desert of Shur
moments.text: Moses led Israel from the Red Sea into the Desert of Shur. They walked three days without finding water, then came to bitter water at Marah, which the LORD made sweet.

moments.title: Saul strikes the Amalekites
moments.text: Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur. But he and his troops spared King Agag and the best of the animals.

cards.name: Zoar
cards.line: Zoar was a small city near Sodom, also called Bela, that God spared from destruction so Lot had a safe place to run.

moments.title: A Town Spared for Lot
moments.text: Lot asks to flee to a small nearby town, and he is told it will not be destroyed. It is called Zoar, and Lot had reached it by the time the sun had risen.

moments.title: Lot Leaves Zoar
moments.text: After Sodom and Gomorrah are destroyed, Lot is afraid to stay in Zoar. He and his two daughters leave and settle in a cave in the mountains.

cards.name: Zorah
cards.line: Zorah was a hilltop town in the foothills, given to the tribe of Dan, and it was the hometown of Manoah and his son Samson.

moments.title: Manoah of Zorah
moments.text: A man named Manoah lived in Zorah, and his wife had no children. The angel of the LORD told her she would have a son who would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines.

moments.title: Danites send out spies
moments.text: The Danites had not yet come into an inheritance among the tribes, so they sent five men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol to explore the land. The men came back and said the land was very good.

moments.title: Six hundred leave Zorah
moments.text: After the spies urged their brothers to go take the land, six hundred Danites left Zorah and Eshtaol armed with weapons of war. They camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah.

moments.title: Samson is buried near Zorah
moments.text: After Samson died, his brothers and his father's family carried him back. They buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of his father Manoah.

cards.name: Beth-peor
cards.line: Beth-peor was a city in Moab, east of the Jordan, in Reuben's land, and valleys facing it are where Israel stayed and where Moses was buried.

moments.title: Israel stays in the valley
moments.text: Moses tells how the people stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor. He was told to encourage Joshua, who would lead them across into the land.

moments.title: Moses teaches the law
moments.text: Moses gave Israel the laws and commands in the valley facing Beth-peor. This was in the land of Sihon, whom Moses and Israel had defeated.

moments.title: Moses is buried
moments.text: After Moses died in Moab, the LORD buried him in a valley facing Beth-peor. No one to this day knows where his grave is.

moments.title: A city for Reuben
moments.text: Beth-peor is listed among the cities of the plateau that once belonged to Sihon king of the Amorites. It became part of the land given to the tribe of Reuben.

cards.name: Gerar
cards.line: Gerar was an ancient city in the south of Canaan, near Gaza, where Abraham and Isaac stayed and where God protected and blessed them.

moments.title: Abraham and Sarah in Gerar
moments.text: While Abraham stayed in Gerar, he said Sarah was his sister, and King Abimelech had her brought to him. God came to Abimelech in a dream and told him to return her, because Abraham was a prophet.

moments.title: Isaac settles in Gerar
moments.text: During a famine, Isaac went to Abimelech at Gerar. The LORD told him not to go to Egypt and promised to bless him, so Isaac settled in Gerar.

moments.title: Quarrel over the wells
moments.text: The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen and said, "The water is ours!" Isaac named that well Esek, and they quarreled over a second well too, but he dug a third and they did not quarrel over it.

moments.title: Asa chases the Cushites
moments.text: After the LORD struck down the Cushites, Asa and his army pursued them as far as Gerar. Judah attacked the cities around Gerar and carried off much plunder.

cards.name: Michmash
cards.line: Michmash was a town of Benjamin on the road to Jerusalem, where the Philistines camped and where Israel won a great victory over them.

moments.title: Philistines camp at Michmash
moments.text: The Philistines gathered a huge army with chariots, horsemen, and troops as many as the sand on the seashore. They camped at Michmash, and the men of Israel hid in fear.

moments.title: Jonathan crosses the pass
moments.text: Jonathan and his armor-bearer went toward the Philistine outpost at the pass between two cliffs. Jonathan said nothing can hinder the LORD from saving, whether by many or by few.

moments.title: Israel strikes the Philistines
moments.text: Israel struck down the Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon. By the end of that day the people were very faint.

cards.name: Sepharvaim
cards.line: Sepharvaim was a city whose people Assyria moved to Samaria, and Assyrian leaders later named it to mock the LORD's power to save Jerusalem.

moments.title: People taken from Sepharvaim
moments.text: The king of Assyria took people from Sepharvaim and other places and settled them in the towns of Samaria to replace the Israelites who had been exiled.

cards.name: Ziph
cards.line: Ziph was a city in the hill country of Judah, and the wilderness near it is where David hid from King Saul.

moments.title: David Hides in Ziph
moments.text: David stayed in the safe hiding places in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Saul searched for him day after day, but God did not let Saul catch David.

moments.title: Jonathan Encourages David
moments.text: While David was in Horesh in the Wilderness of Ziph, Jonathan came and helped him trust God. He told David he would be king, and the two made a promise before the LORD.

moments.title: Saul Hunts in Ziph
moments.text: The Ziphites told Saul that David was hiding near them. Saul took three thousand chosen men down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there.

moments.title: Rehoboam Strengthens Ziph
moments.text: Rehoboam made the walls and defenses of Ziph and other cities of Judah and Benjamin stronger. He put officers in them, with supplies of food, oil, and wine.

cards.name: Abarim
cards.line: Abarim is a mountain range east of the Jordan in Moab, facing Jericho, where Moses was told to go up and view the Promised Land before he died.

moments.title: Moses told to go up Abarim
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land given to the Israelites. After he saw it, Moses would die, as his brother Aaron did.

moments.title: Israel camps in the Abarim mountains
moments.text: The Israelites set out and camped in the mountains of Abarim facing Nebo. Then they moved on to the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.

moments.title: Moses told to climb Mount Nebo
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to go up into the Abarim Range to Mount Nebo and view Canaan. He would see the land from a distance and die there, but he would not enter it.

cards.name: Makkedah
cards.line: Makkedah was a Canaanite royal city in the plains of Judah, where five kings hid in a cave and where Joshua won a key victory.

moments.title: Five kings hide in the cave
moments.text: After the battle at Gibeon, the five kings who fled were found hiding in a cave at Makkedah. Joshua had large stones rolled against the cave's mouth and men posted to guard it.

moments.title: Joshua's camp at Makkedah
moments.text: The army came back safely to Joshua at Makkedah, and no one dared to speak a word against the Israelites.

moments.title: The city is captured
moments.text: On that same day Joshua captured Makkedah and put its king to death. Then he and all Israel moved on to fight against Libnah.

cards.name: Rehoboth
cards.line: Rehoboth, meaning "wide places," is a name shared by three places in the Bible: a city in Assyria, a well Isaac dug, and a town on the Euphrates.

moments.title: A city in Assyria
moments.text: Nimrod went out from Shinar into Assyria and built cities there. Rehoboth-Ir is named with Nineveh and Calah.

moments.title: Isaac's well with room
moments.text: After quarrels over other wells, Isaac dug one that nobody fought over. He named it Rehoboth and said the LORD had made room for them, and they would be fruitful in the land.

moments.title: Shaul's hometown
moments.text: Shaul came from Rehoboth on the Euphrates. He reigned as king in Edom after Samlah died.

cards.name: Abel-meholah
cards.line: Abel-meholah was a city in the Jordan valley, best known as the hometown of Elisha, whom God chose to become the prophet after Elijah.

moments.title: The Midianites flee
moments.text: When Gideon's three hundred men sounded their horns, the LORD set the Midianites against one another. Their army ran as far as the border of Abel-meholah.

moments.title: Part of Solomon's district
moments.text: Abel-meholah was named in the district run by Baana son of Ahilud, one of Solomon's officers. His district went from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam.

moments.title: Elisha is chosen
moments.text: The LORD told Elijah to anoint Elisha from Abel-meholah as the next prophet. Elijah found Elisha plowing and threw his cloak around him.

cards.name: Baal-perazim
cards.line: Baal-perazim was a place near the valley of Rephaim where David defeated the Philistines, and he named it for the way God burst out against his enemies.

moments.title: A bursting flood
moments.text: David went to Baal-perazim and defeated the Philistines. He said the LORD had burst out against his enemies like a bursting flood, so he named the place Baal-perazim.

moments.title: Idols left behind
moments.text: The Philistines abandoned their idols there. David and his men carried them away, and David ordered that they be burned in the fire.

cards.name: Beer-lahai-roi
cards.line: Beer-lahai-roi is a well in the wilderness south-west of Beersheba, where the Lord met Hagar and where Isaac later lived.

moments.title: Isaac Near the Well
moments.text: Isaac had just returned from Beer-lahai-roi, since he was living in the Negev. Then he met Rebekah, took her as his wife, and loved her.

moments.title: God Blesses Isaac
moments.text: After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac, who lived near Beer-lahai-roi.

cards.name: Brook Eshcol
cards.line: The Valley of Eshcol was a valley in Canaan where Israel's spies cut a huge cluster of grapes, and it was named for that cluster.

moments.title: The giant cluster of grapes
moments.text: The spies cut a branch with one cluster of grapes, and two men carried it on a pole. They also took pomegranates and figs, and the place was named the Valley of Eshcol for the cluster.

moments.title: Spying out the land
moments.text: Moses later recalled that the twelve spies went up into the hill country and came to the Valley of Eshcol. There they spied out the land and took some of its fruit.

moments.title: Seeing the land at Eshcol
moments.text: Moses later said the spies went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land. Then they discouraged Israel from entering the land the LORD had given them.

cards.name: Carchemish
cards.line: Carchemish was a city on the Euphrates River where Egypt's army marched to fight, and where Babylon later defeated Pharaoh Neco's army.

moments.title: Neco marches toward Carchemish
moments.text: Neco king of Egypt marched up to fight at Carchemish by the Euphrates. Josiah went out to confront him, even though Neco said God had told him to hurry.

moments.title: Assyria's king boasts of Carchemish
moments.text: The king of Assyria boasted of cities he had taken, asking if Calno was not like Carchemish. God said He would punish the king for his proud heart.

moments.title: Egypt defeated at Carchemish
moments.text: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah about Pharaoh Neco's army. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated it at Carchemish on the Euphrates River.

cards.name: Derbe
cards.line: Derbe was a small city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas fled from danger, preached the gospel, and made many disciples.

moments.title: Fleeing to Derbe
moments.text: When people in Iconium planned to stone them, Paul and Barnabas fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe. They kept preaching the gospel there.

moments.title: Many Disciples Made
moments.text: After Paul was stoned in Lystra, he got up and left the next day with Barnabas for Derbe. They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples.

moments.title: Paul Returns to Derbe
moments.text: On his next trip, Paul came to Derbe and then went on to Lystra. This shows he came back to the region where the gospel had been preached.

moments.title: Gaius of Derbe
moments.text: Gaius from Derbe is named among the men who accompanied Paul. He is one of the people from Derbe we meet in the Bible.

cards.name: Etam
cards.line: Etam was a rocky place in Judah where Samson stayed in a cave, and the name also belongs to a town King Rehoboam built up for defense.

moments.title: Samson stays in the cave
moments.text: After Samson struck the Philistines with a great slaughter, he went down and stayed in the cave at the rock of Etam.

moments.title: Judah comes for Samson
moments.text: Three thousand men of Judah came to the cave at Etam to arrest Samson and give him to the Philistines. Samson let them tie him with two new ropes and lead him up from the rock.

moments.title: Rehoboam strengthens Etam
moments.text: King Rehoboam built up Etam with other cities in Judah for defense. He strengthened their fortifications and put officers, supplies, shields, and spears in them.

cards.name: Gath-hepher
cards.line: Gath-hepher was a city on the border of Zebulun's land, and it is known as the hometown of the prophet Jonah son of Amittai.

moments.title: On Zebulun's Border
moments.text: When the land was divided, the border of Zebulun's territory crossed eastward to Gath-hepher. It was one of the places marking the edge of the tribe's inheritance.

cards.name: Havilah
cards.line: Havilah is a region known for its pure gold, found by the river Pishon in Genesis and later named as a boundary mark.

moments.title: Land of pure gold
moments.text: The river Pishon winds through the whole land of Havilah. The Bible says the gold there is pure, and bdellium and onyx are found there too.

moments.title: Where Ishmael's family settled
moments.text: Ishmael's descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, near the border of Egypt. They lived in hostility toward all their brothers.

moments.title: Saul strikes the Amalekites
moments.text: Saul struck down the Amalekites all the way from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt. But he and his troops spared King Agag and the best of the animals.

cards.name: Keilah
cards.line: Keilah was a walled city in the lowland of Judah that David saved from the Philistines, then left when its people might hand him over to Saul.

moments.title: David saves Keilah
moments.text: The Philistines were attacking Keilah and looting its threshing floors. The LORD told David to go, and David and his men struck the Philistines with a mighty blow and saved the people of Keilah.

moments.title: Saul plans to trap David
moments.text: Saul heard that David was in Keilah and said God had delivered him, since David was in a town with gates and bars. Saul called his troops to go to war and besiege David and his men.

moments.title: The LORD warns David
moments.text: David asked the LORD if Saul would come and if the citizens of Keilah would give him up. The LORD said they would.

moments.title: David leaves Keilah
moments.text: David and his men, about six hundred strong, left Keilah and kept moving from place to place. When Saul heard David had escaped, he decided not to go.

cards.name: Kibroth-hattaavah
cards.line: Kibroth-hattaavah was a camp in the wilderness where Israel buried people who craved other food, and its name means graves of craving.

moments.title: Graves of craving
moments.text: While the people were still eating the meat, the LORD's anger burned and He struck them with a severe plague. They named the place Kibroth-hattaavah because they buried the people who had craved other food there.

moments.title: A stop on the journey
moments.text: Israel set out from the Wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah. Then they moved on and camped at Hazeroth.

moments.title: Moving on to Hazeroth
moments.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.

moments.title: Making the LORD angry
moments.text: At Kibroth-hattaavah, Israel made the LORD angry. They did the same at Taberah and at Massah.

cards.name: Laish
cards.line: Laish was a quiet, faraway city in the north that the tribe of Dan attacked and burned, then rebuilt and renamed Dan.

moments.title: Spies see a peaceful city
moments.text: Five men from Dan came to Laish and saw people living securely, quiet and unsuspecting. The land lacked nothing, and the city had no cruel ruler and no allies.

moments.title: Dan attacks Laish
moments.text: The Danites took Micah's idols and his priest and went to Laish. They struck the quiet, unsuspecting people with swords and burned the city, and no one was there to rescue them.

moments.title: Laish becomes Dan
moments.text: The Danites rebuilt the city and lived there. They named it Dan, after their ancestor Dan, a son of Israel, and set up Micah's carved idol there.

cards.name: Lo-debar
cards.line: Lo-debar was a town in Gilead, east of the Jordan, where Machir lived and where Jonathan's son Mephibosheth stayed before David sent for him.

moments.title: David sends for Mephibosheth
moments.text: Ziba tells David that Jonathan's son is in Lo-debar at the house of Machir. King David has him brought from Machir's house in Lo-debar.

cards.name: Maon
cards.line: Maon was a city in the hill country of Judah, and the wilderness around it became a hiding place for David when King Saul hunted him.

moments.title: David hides from Saul
moments.text: David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon when Saul came looking for him. David went down to the rock and stayed there, and Saul pursued him.

moments.title: Nabal's home
moments.text: A very wealthy man named Nabal lived in Maon, but his business was in Carmel. He owned a thousand goats and three thousand sheep.

cards.name: Moreh
cards.line: Moreh is a hill in the valley where Gideon camped near Midian, and the Oak of Moreh near Shechem is where Abram stopped in Canaan.

moments.title: Abram at the Oak of Moreh
moments.text: Abram traveled through Canaan as far as the Oak of Moreh at Shechem. There the LORD appeared to him and promised to give the land to his offspring, and Abram built an altar.

moments.title: Midian camps near Moreh
moments.text: Gideon and his men camped beside the spring of Harod, and the camp of Midian was north of them near the hill of Moreh. There the LORD cut Gideon's army down to three hundred men.

cards.name: Sin
cards.line: The Desert of Sin was a wilderness region between Elim and Sinai where Israel camped after leaving Egypt and where God first provided bread from heaven.

moments.title: Israel arrives in Sin
moments.text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after leaving Egypt, Israel set out from Elim and came to the Desert of Sin, between Elim and Sinai.

moments.title: The people grumble
moments.text: In the desert the whole congregation grumbled against Moses and Aaron. They said they missed the pots of meat and bread in Egypt and feared they would starve.

moments.title: God promises bread from heaven
moments.text: The LORD said He would rain down bread from heaven. The people were to gather enough for each day, and twice as much on the sixth day.

moments.title: Israel leaves Sin
moments.text: The people left the Desert of Sin as the LORD commanded, moving on from place to place.

cards.name: Thebes
cards.line: Thebes was a great city of ancient Egypt on the Nile, home of the god Amon, and the Bible shows God judging it along with Egypt.

moments.title: Judgment on Amon of Thebes
moments.text: The LORD says He will punish Amon, the god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh and Egypt. He says those who trust in Pharaoh will be punished too.

moments.title: Thebes Will Be Split Open
moments.text: God says He will carry out judgment on Thebes and cut off its crowds. He says Thebes will be split open when He sets fire to Egypt.

moments.title: A Lesson for Nineveh
moments.text: Nahum asks Nineveh if it is better than Thebes. Thebes sat by the Nile with water as its wall and strong allies, yet it went into captivity.

cards.name: Baal-zephon
cards.line: Baal-zephon was a place near the Gulf of Suez, opposite where the Israelites camped by the sea just before they crossed it.

moments.title: God sets the camp
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to have the Israelites turn back and camp by the sea, directly opposite Baal-zephon. He said Pharaoh would think they were boxed in, and that He would gain honor by means of Pharaoh and his army.

moments.title: Pharaoh catches up
moments.text: The Egyptians chased Israel and overtook them camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon. The people were terrified, but Moses told them the LORD would fight for them.

moments.title: A stop on the journey
moments.text: The list of Israel's travels says they set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped near Migdol. Then they set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea.

cards.name: Cenchreae
cards.line: Cenchreae was the eastern harbor of Corinth, a port city where Paul kept a vow and where a church was served by Phoebe.

moments.title: Paul keeps his vow
moments.text: After staying in Corinth for quite some time, Paul said goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria with Priscilla and Aquila.

moments.title: Phoebe, servant of the church
moments.text: Phoebe was a servant of the church in Cenchrea. Paul spoke well of her and said she had been a great help to many people, including him.

cards.name: Dung Gate
cards.line: The Dung Gate was a gate in the south-west part of Jerusalem's wall, and Nehemiah's builders rebuilt it after the city's gates were burned.

moments.title: The gate is rebuilt
moments.text: Malchijah, ruler of the district of Beth-haccherem, rebuilt the Dung Gate. He put in its doors, bolts, and bars.

cards.name: Harod
cards.line: Harod was a spring where Gideon's army camped before facing Midian, and where God likely cut his large army down to just three hundred men.

moments.title: Gideon camps at the spring
moments.text: Gideon and all his men camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of them in the valley near the hill of Moreh.

moments.title: God chooses men at the water
moments.text: God said Gideon had too many men, so He had them tested at the water by how they drank. Only three hundred lapped with their hands, and God said He would save Israel through them.

cards.name: Highway
cards.line: The King's Highway was a main road that Israel asked Edom and King Sihon of the Amorites for permission to travel along as they passed through their lands.

moments.title: Edom Says No
moments.text: Israel asked to pass through Edom's land and promised to stay on the King's Highway and pay for any water. Edom refused and came out with a large army, so Israel turned away.

moments.title: Sihon Says No
moments.text: Israel asked King Sihon of the Amorites to let them pass through his land, promising to stay on the King's Highway. Sihon refused and fought Israel, and Israel took his land and cities, including Heshbon.

cards.name: India
cards.line: India was the eastern edge of King Xerxes' huge Persian kingdom, the far end of his 127 provinces, which stretched from India to Cush.

moments.title: The edge of Xerxes' kingdom
moments.text: The book of Esther begins by saying that Xerxes ruled 127 provinces from India to Cush. India is named as one end of his huge kingdom.

moments.title: Mordecai's orders go out
moments.text: Mordecai's orders for the Jews went to all 127 provinces from India to Cush. Each province got them in its own script and language.

cards.name: Kir-hareseth
cards.line: Kir-hareseth was a walled city and fortress of Moab, the last Moabite city left standing when Israel invaded, and a place the prophet Isaiah mourned.

moments.title: The last city standing
moments.text: Israel destroyed the Moabite cities, covered the good fields with stones, stopped up the springs, and cut down the good trees. Only Kir-hareseth was left with its stones in place, but men with slings surrounded it and attacked it too.

moments.title: The king's desperate offering
moments.text: The king of Moab could not break through the enemy lines. He offered his firstborn son as a burnt offering on the city wall, and great fury came against the Israelites, so they withdrew and went home.

moments.title: Isaiah's message about Kir-hareseth
moments.text: Isaiah's message spoke of Moab's pride and empty boasting. It called on Moab to wail and moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, and said his heart laments for the city like a harp.

cards.name: Kiriath-sepher
cards.line: Kiriath-sepher, later called Debir, was a city in Judah's land that Othniel captured, winning Caleb's daughter Acsah as his wife.

moments.title: Caleb's challenge
moments.text: Caleb marched against the people of Debir, which was once called Kiriath-sepher. He promised his daughter Acsah in marriage to the man who struck down the city and captured it.

moments.title: Othniel captures the city
moments.text: Othniel, son of Caleb's brother Kenaz, captured the city. Caleb gave him his daughter Acsah to be his wife.

moments.title: Judah marches on Debir
moments.text: The men of Judah marched against the people of Debir, formerly Kiriath-sepher. Caleb offered Acsah to the one who captured it, and Othniel took the city and received her.

cards.name: Meribah-kadesh
cards.line: Meribah-kadesh was a watering place in the Wilderness of Zin where Moses and Aaron failed to honor God as holy, and Ezekiel's vision names it on the southern border.

moments.title: Moses and Aaron break faith
moments.text: At the waters of Meribah-kadesh, God says Moses and Aaron broke faith with Him by failing to treat Him as holy in front of the Israelites. Because of this, Moses would see the land from a distance but not enter it.

moments.title: The southern border in Ezekiel's vision
moments.text: In Ezekiel's vision, the southern border of the land runs from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt to the Great Sea.

moments.title: The southern edge of Gad
moments.text: Gad's portion has its southern border running from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, then along the Brook of Egypt and out to the Great Sea.

cards.name: Mount Paran
cards.line: Mount Paran is a mountain, probably in the hilly wilderness south of the Promised Land, named in two poems about God coming in glory.

moments.title: God shines from Paran
moments.text: In his blessing before he died, Moses said the LORD came from Sinai and shone forth from Mount Paran. He came with many thousands of holy ones and flaming fire at His right hand.

moments.title: The Holy One from Paran
moments.text: In his prayer, Habakkuk said that God came from Teman, and the Holy One came from Mount Paran. His glory covered the heavens, and His praise filled the earth.

cards.name: Naioth
cards.line: Naioth in Ramah was a place where Samuel led a group of prophets, and where David took shelter from King Saul.

moments.title: David Hides with Samuel
moments.text: David ran away from Saul and told Samuel everything Saul had done to him. Then David and Samuel went to Naioth and stayed there.

moments.title: Saul's Messengers Prophesy
moments.text: Saul sent messengers to seize David, but the Spirit of God came upon them and they prophesied. He sent more messengers a second and a third time, and they prophesied as well.

moments.title: Saul Prophesies at Naioth
moments.text: Saul went to Naioth himself, and the Spirit of God came upon him too. He prophesied, took off his robes, and lay there all day and night.

moments.title: David Leaves Naioth
moments.text: David fled from Naioth in Ramah and went to Jonathan. He asked what he had done wrong that Saul wanted to take his life.

cards.name: Perga
cards.line: Perga was a city in Pamphylia where Paul and his companions landed on their first journey, and where they later spoke the word before heading home.

moments.title: John leaves the group
moments.text: Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. There John left them and returned to Jerusalem.

moments.title: On to Pisidian Antioch
moments.text: From Perga, Paul and his companions traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch.

moments.title: The word spoken in Perga
moments.text: On the way back, they spoke the word in Perga. Then they went down to Attalia.

cards.name: Pi-hahiroth
cards.line: Pi-hahiroth was a camping spot by the sea in Egypt, where God led the Israelites just before He rescued them from Pharaoh's army.

moments.title: Camp by the sea
moments.text: The LORD told Moses to turn the Israelites back and camp at Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. He said He would harden Pharaoh's heart so Pharaoh would chase them, and the Egyptians would know that He is the LORD.

moments.title: Pharaoh catches up
moments.text: Pharaoh changed his mind and chased Israel with his chariots and army, and he overtook them camped by the sea near Pi-hahiroth. The Israelites were terrified and cried out to the LORD.

moments.title: A stop on the journey
moments.text: Israel's travel list says they left Etham, turned back to Pi-hahiroth, and camped near Migdol. From there they set out and crossed through the sea.

cards.name: Taberah
cards.line: Taberah was a place in the wilderness where the fire of the LORD burned among the complaining Israelites, and its name means "burning."

moments.title: Fire at Taberah
moments.text: The people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down. The place was named Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.

moments.title: Israel made the LORD angry
moments.text: At Taberah, the Israelites provoked the LORD. Moses later named it with Massah and Kibroth-hattaavah as places where they kept making Him angry.

cards.name: Tel-abib
cards.line: Tel-abib was a place by the River Kebar where Jewish exiles lived, and where Ezekiel sat among them before God made him a watchman.

moments.title: Ezekiel sits with the exiles
moments.text: The Spirit took Ezekiel away, and he came in bitterness and anger to the exiles at Tel-abib. He sat among them for seven days, overwhelmed.

moments.title: God makes Ezekiel a watchman
moments.text: After seven days, the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel. God made him a watchman for Israel and told him to give them warnings from Him.

cards.name: Thebez
cards.line: Thebez was a city north-east of Shechem where the wicked king Abimelech was killed by a woman with a millstone, an event the Bible remembers.

moments.title: Abimelech takes Thebez
moments.text: After the people in the tower of Shechem were killed by fire, Abimelech went to Thebez, camped against it, and captured it. The people fled into a strong tower inside the city.

moments.title: A woman's millstone
moments.text: As Abimelech came to set the tower on fire, a woman dropped an upper millstone on his head. He told his armor-bearer to kill him so no one could say a woman killed him, and he died.

cards.name: Timnath-serah
cards.line: Timnath-serah was a city in the hill country of Ephraim that Joshua received as his inheritance, where he rebuilt, settled, and was later buried.

moments.title: Joshua's city
moments.text: After the land was divided, the Israelites gave Joshua the city of Timnath-serah, as the LORD had commanded and as he requested. He rebuilt the city and settled in it.

moments.title: Joshua is buried
moments.text: Joshua, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110. They buried him in his own inheritance at Timnath-serah, north of Mount Gaash.

cards.name: Valley of Shaveh
cards.line: The Valley of Shaveh, also called the King's Valley, is where Abram was met after his victory, and where Absalom later set up his pillar.

moments.title: Abram Meets the Kings
moments.text: After Abram defeated Chedorlaomer and the kings with him, the king of Sodom went out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh. Melchizedek, priest of God Most High, brought bread and wine and blessed Abram, and Abram gave him a tenth of everything.

moments.title: Absalom's Monument
moments.text: Absalom set up a pillar for himself in the King's Valley because he had no son to keep the memory of his name. He gave it his name, and it was still called Absalom's Monument when this was written.

cards.name: Abel-shittim
cards.line: Abel-shittim, also called Shittim, was a place east of the Jordan on the plains of Moab, Israel's last camp before they crossed into Canaan.

moments.title: Camp by the Jordan
moments.text: Israel camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth to Abel-shittim. This was across from Jericho.

cards.name: Adria
cards.line: Adria, or the Adriatic Sea, was the water between Greece and Italy, where Paul's ship was driven across it for fourteen nights.

moments.title: Driven across the sea
moments.text: On the fourteenth night the ship was still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were near land, and they dropped four anchors and prayed for daybreak.

cards.name: Aenon
cards.line: Aenon, near Salim, was a place with plenty of water where John the Baptist baptized people while Jesus was also baptizing in the Judean countryside.

moments.title: John baptizes at Aenon
moments.text: John was baptizing at Aenon near Salim because the water was plentiful there. People kept coming to be baptized.

moments.title: John's joy in Jesus
moments.text: John's disciples told him that everyone was going to Jesus. John said he was not the Christ but was sent ahead of Him, and his joy in the bridegroom was complete.

cards.name: Ahava
cards.line: Ahava was a canal or stream where Ezra gathered people returning from captivity before their trip from Babylon to Jerusalem, and where they fasted and asked God for protection.

moments.title: Gathering at the canal
moments.text: Ezra gathered the returning exiles at the canal and they camped three days. He found no Levites, so he sent leaders to ask for ministers for God's house.

moments.title: A fast for a safe journey
moments.text: At the Ahava Canal Ezra announced a fast so they could humble themselves and ask God for a safe journey. He was ashamed to ask the king for soldiers, so they trusted God, and He granted their request.

moments.title: Setting out for Jerusalem
moments.text: On the twelfth day of the first month they left the Ahava Canal for Jerusalem. The hand of God was upon them and protected them from enemies and bandits along the way.

cards.name: Allon-bacuth
cards.line: Allon-bacuth was an oak tree below Bethel where Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, was buried, and Jacob gave the spot a name that means oak of weeping.

moments.title: Deborah is buried
moments.text: Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. Jacob named the tree Allon-bacuth.

cards.name: Besor
cards.line: Besor is a brook, or valley, in the far south of Judah where David left behind 200 tired men while he chased the Amalekite raiders.

moments.title: Two hundred stay behind
