moments.text: David and his six hundred men came to the Brook of Besor. Two hundred men were too exhausted to cross, so they stayed there while David and four hundred men kept chasing the raiders.

moments.title: David shares the plunder
moments.text: When David came back to the men at the brook, some wicked men wanted to keep the plunder from them. David said the LORD had given the victory, and that those who stayed with the supplies would share alike with those who fought.

cards.name: Bochim
cards.line: Bochim, meaning "weepers," is a place west of the Jordan, above Gilgal, where Israel wept after the angel of the LORD rebuked them for disobeying.

moments.title: The angel's rebuke
moments.text: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim. He said Israel had not obeyed God's voice, so God would no longer drive out the people of the land.

moments.title: Israel weeps and sacrifices
moments.text: When the angel finished speaking, all the people lifted up their voices and wept. They named the place Bochim and offered sacrifices there to the LORD.

cards.name: Dura
cards.line: Dura was a plain in the province of Babylon where King Nebuchadnezzar set up a huge golden statue and commanded everyone to worship it.

moments.title: The golden statue is set up
moments.text: King Nebuchadnezzar made a golden statue sixty cubits high and six cubits wide. He set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

moments.title: The command to worship
moments.text: Officials from all the provinces stood before the statue on the plain of Dura. A herald said everyone must worship it when the music sounded or be thrown into the blazing fiery furnace, and the people bowed down.

cards.name: El-bethel
cards.line: El-bethel is the name Jacob gave to the place at Luz, also called Bethel, where he built an altar because God had revealed Himself to him.

moments.title: Jacob builds an altar
moments.text: Jacob and his household arrived at Luz, also called Bethel, in Canaan. There Jacob built an altar and named the place El-bethel, because God had revealed Himself to him there as he fled from his brother.

cards.name: Fair Havens
cards.line: Fair Havens was a harbor on the southern coast of Crete, near the town of Lasea, where Paul's ship stopped and Paul warned of danger ahead.

moments.title: Arrival at Fair Havens
moments.text: After a hard trip along the coast of Crete, Paul and the others reached a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.

moments.title: Paul's warning
moments.text: Much time had passed and sailing had become dangerous. Paul warned that the trip would bring disaster and great loss to the ship, the cargo, and their lives.

moments.title: The decision to sail on
moments.text: The centurion listened to the pilot and the ship's owner instead of Paul. Since the harbor was not good for winter, most chose to sail on.

cards.name: Forest of Ephraim
cards.line: The Forest of Ephraim was a wooded region where David's army fought Israel, and where Absalom, David's son, was caught in an oak tree.

moments.title: Battle in the forest
moments.text: David's army marched out to fight Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim. Israel was defeated, and twenty thousand men died that day.

moments.title: The forest devours
moments.text: The battle spread over the whole countryside. That day the forest devoured more people than the sword.

moments.title: Absalom caught in the oak
moments.text: Absalom was riding his mule under the thick branches of a large oak. His head caught fast in the tree, and the mule kept going, leaving him hanging in midair.

cards.name: Galeed
cards.line: Galeed is the name of a mound of stones where Jacob and Laban made a promise of peace, with God as their witness.

moments.title: A mound of witness
moments.text: Jacob told his relatives to gather stones, and they made a mound and ate there. Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed, which means heap of witness.

moments.title: A promise of peace
moments.text: Laban said the mound and the pillar were witnesses that neither man would pass them to harm the other. Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

cards.name: Gate of the Valley
cards.line: The Valley Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's broken wall, where Nehemiah left and returned on his night trip to inspect the ruins before rebuilding began.

moments.title: Out the Valley Gate at night
moments.text: Nehemiah went out through the Valley Gate in the dark with a few men. He inspected the walls that were broken down and the gates that fire had destroyed.

moments.title: Back through the Valley Gate
moments.text: After going up the valley by night and inspecting the wall, Nehemiah headed back and came into the city again through the Valley Gate. The officials did not know where he had gone.

cards.name: Hahiroth
cards.line: Pi-hahiroth was a camping place opposite Baal-zephon and near Migdol on Israel's journey, and it is where they set out to cross the sea.

moments.title: Camping at Pi-hahiroth
moments.text: The people turned back from Etham to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and camped near Migdol. Then they set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea into the wilderness.

cards.name: Horesh
cards.line: Horesh was a place in the Wilderness of Ziph where David hid from King Saul, and where Jonathan encouraged him.

moments.title: Jonathan encourages David
moments.text: David saw that Saul had come out to take his life. Jonathan came to David in Horesh and encouraged him to trust God, telling him not to be afraid because he would be king.

moments.title: A promise before the LORD
moments.text: David and Jonathan made a covenant, a solemn promise, before the LORD. Then Jonathan went home, and David stayed in Horesh.

cards.name: Kedesh-naphtali
cards.line: Kedesh in Naphtali was the city Barak came from, the man Deborah called to march against Sisera, and the place where he gathered his troops.

moments.title: Barak is summoned from Kedesh
moments.text: Deborah summoned Barak from Kedesh in Naphtali. She told him the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded him to march to Mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun.

moments.title: Barak gathers the men
moments.text: Deborah went with Barak to Kedesh, where he summoned Zebulun and Naphtali. Ten thousand men followed him, and Deborah went with him too.

cards.name: Lydda
cards.line: Lydda was a city near Joppa, on the road toward Jerusalem, where Peter healed a paralyzed man and many people turned to the Lord.

moments.title: Peter heals Aeneas
moments.text: Peter visited the saints in Lydda and found Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and in bed for eight years. Peter said Jesus Christ heals him, and Aeneas got up right away.

moments.title: Lydda turns to the Lord
moments.text: All who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw Aeneas, and they turned to the Lord.

cards.name: Merom
cards.line: Merom was a body of water in northern Canaan where a huge alliance of kings gathered to fight Israel and where Joshua won his last great battle.

moments.title: Kings gather at Merom
moments.text: A huge army of kings, with a great number of horses and chariots, joined forces and camped at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.

moments.title: Joshua attacks by surprise
moments.text: The LORD told Joshua not to be afraid and promised to deliver the kings to Israel. Joshua and his army came upon them suddenly by the waters of Merom, and the LORD delivered them into Israel's hand.

cards.name: Moserah
cards.line: Moserah was a stopping place for Israel in the wilderness, near Mount Hor, where Aaron died and his son Eleazar became priest.

moments.title: Aaron dies at Moserah
moments.text: The Israelites traveled to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried. His son Eleazar took his place as priest.

cards.name: Mount of Esau
cards.line: The Mount of Esau is the mountain land of Edom, which God judges in Obadiah and then places under the rule of His kingdom.

moments.title: God judges the wise of Edom
moments.text: The LORD asks if He will not destroy the wise men and men of understanding in the mountains of Esau. Teman's mighty men will be terrified, and everyone in the mountains of Esau will be cut down.

moments.title: Israel will possess the mountains
moments.text: God promises that people from the Negev will possess the mountains of Esau. Edom's land will be taken by the people of Israel.

moments.title: Deliverers will rule Esau's mountains
moments.text: Deliverers will go up Mount Zion to rule over the mountains of Esau. The kingdom will belong to the LORD.

cards.name: Mount Perazim
cards.line: Mount Perazim is a mountain named only in Isaiah, where it recalls a time when the LORD rose up to act, and it warns of coming judgment.

moments.title: David defeats the Philistines
moments.text: Easton's Bible Dictionary says Mount Perazim is the same as Baal-perazim, where David won a victory over the Philistines. Isaiah points back to it, saying the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim.

cards.name: Mount Zalmon
cards.line: Mount Zalmon is a dark, tree-covered hill near Shechem, where Abimelech and his men cut branches to burn the tower of Shechem.

moments.title: Branches cut for fire
moments.text: Abimelech and his men went up Mount Zalmon, and he cut a branch and told them to do the same. They piled the branches against the tower and burned it.

cards.name: Mysia
cards.line: Mysia was a region in northwest Asia Minor, and Paul and his team passed by it on the way to Troas after the Spirit stopped them.

moments.title: Passing by Mysia
moments.text: At the border of Mysia, Paul and his team tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them. So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

cards.name: Neapolis
cards.line: Neapolis, meaning "new city," was a seaport in northern Greece where Paul and his team first landed in Europe to preach the gospel.

moments.title: Landing in Europe
moments.text: After the vision, Paul and his companions believed God had called them to preach in Macedonia. They sailed from Troas by way of Samothrace and came to Neapolis.

cards.name: Pavement
cards.line: The Pavement, called Gabbatha in Hebrew, was the paved place where Pilate sat in judgment and handed Jesus over to be crucified.

moments.title: Pilate sits in judgment
moments.text: Pilate brought Jesus out and sat on the judgment seat at the Stone Pavement. He said to the Jews, "Here is your King!"

moments.title: Jesus handed over
moments.text: The Jews shouted for Jesus to be crucified, and the chief priests said, "We have no king but Caesar." Then Pilate handed Jesus over, and the soldiers took Him away.

cards.name: Perez-uzza
cards.line: Perez-uzza is the place where Uzzah died after touching the ark of God, and David gave it a name that means the breaking out against Uzzah.

moments.title: Uzzah dies at the ark
moments.text: The anger of the LORD burned against Uzzah because he had put his hand on the ark. He struck Uzzah down, and Uzzah died there before God.

moments.title: David names the place
moments.text: David became angry because the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, as it is called to this day.

cards.name: Pharpar
cards.line: Pharpar was a swift river of Damascus, named by Naaman, a man with leprosy, as a better place to wash than the waters of Israel.

moments.title: Naaman names the river
moments.text: Naaman was angry at Elisha's word to wash, and he said the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, were better than all the waters of Israel. Then he left in a rage.

cards.name: Salamis
cards.line: Salamis was a seaport city on the east coast of Cyprus, where Paul and Barnabas first preached the word of God after sailing from the mainland.

moments.title: Arriving to preach
moments.text: Barnabas and Saul, sent by the Holy Spirit, sailed to Cyprus. When they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues, and John was with them as their helper.

cards.name: Three Taverns
cards.line: Three Taverns was a stopping place on the Appian Road near Rome, where Roman believers met Paul on his way to the city.

moments.title: Brothers meet Paul
moments.text: Believers from Rome had heard about Paul and traveled to the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet him. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

cards.name: Vale of Hebron
cards.line: The Valley of Hebron is the place Israel sent Joseph from when he asked him to check on his brothers and the flocks and bring word back.

moments.title: Joseph sent from Hebron
moments.text: Joseph said he was ready. Then Israel asked him to go see how his brothers and the flocks were doing and bring word back, and he sent Joseph off from the Valley of Hebron.

cards.name: Vale of Siddim
cards.line: The Vale of Siddim was a valley, also called the Salt Sea, where five kings fought four kings and lost, leading to Lot's capture.

moments.title: Five kings gather for battle
moments.text: The kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela came as allies to the Valley of Siddim. There they lined up against Chedorlaomer and the three kings with him, four kings against five.

moments.title: Men fall into the tar pits
moments.text: The valley was full of tar pits. As the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some men fell into the pits, and the survivors escaped to the hill country.

cards.name: Valley of Baca
cards.line: The Valley of Baca is a valley named in a psalm, one that pilgrims pass through on their way to God's house in Zion.

moments.title: Pilgrims pass through
moments.text: Those whose hearts are set on pilgrimage pass through the Valley of Baca and make it a place of springs. Even the autumn rain covers it with pools.

cards.name: Valley of Beracah
cards.line: The Valley of Beracah is a valley near Engedi where Judah's people blessed the LORD after He gave them victory over their enemies in Jehoshaphat's day.

moments.title: Blessing the LORD
moments.text: After three days of gathering plunder, the people of Judah met in the valley on the fourth day and blessed the LORD. The place was named the Valley of Beracah because of this.

cards.name: Way of Holiness
cards.line: The Way of Holiness is a highway promised in Isaiah where the redeemed of the LORD will walk safely and return to Zion with joy.

moments.title: A highway for the redeemed
moments.text: Isaiah says there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it, but the redeemed will walk upon it.

cards.name: Zered
cards.line: The Zered is a brook and valley near the Dead Sea, and Israel crossed it thirty-eight years after leaving Kadesh-barnea, when the old generation of fighting men had died.

moments.title: Crossing the Brook of Zered
moments.text: The LORD told Israel to arise and cross over the Brook of Zered, and they crossed it. From Kadesh-barnea to this crossing was thirty-eight years.

moments.title: The old generation is gone
moments.text: By the time Israel crossed the Zered, all the fighting men of that generation had died, as the LORD had sworn. His hand was against them until they had all perished.

cards.name: Rimmon
cards.line: Rimmon was a city in the southern land of Judah, later given to the tribe of Simeon, and it is named in lists of the cities of Israel.

moments.title: A city in Judah's land
moments.text: Rimmon is listed among the cities in the south of Judah's land, together with its villages.

moments.title: A city given to Simeon
moments.text: Rimmon was named among the cities of Simeon. Simeon's land was taken from Judah's portion because Judah's share was too large.

moments.title: A town of Simeon's families
moments.text: Rimmon is listed among the villages of a group of Simeon's families. They kept a family record of their settlements.

cards.name: Bahurim
cards.line: Bahurim was a city east of Jerusalem on the road to the Jordan, where David met curses while fleeing and where two messengers hid in a well.

moments.title: Paltiel turns back
moments.text: Michal's husband Paltiel followed her, weeping all the way to Bahurim. Abner told him to go back, and he returned home.

moments.title: Shimei curses David
moments.text: As David came to Bahurim, Shimei of Saul's family yelled curses and threw stones at him. David would not let Abishai harm him, saying the LORD had told Shimei to curse.

moments.title: Hidden in a well
moments.text: Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed into a well at a man's house in Bahurim. His wife spread a covering over it and scattered grain on top, so Absalom's servants did not find them, and then the two warned David.

cards.name: Edrei
cards.line: Edrei was a royal city of Og, king of Bashan, east of the Jordan, and the place where Israel defeated him as they moved toward the land God promised.

moments.title: Israel defeats King Og
moments.text: Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to fight Israel at Edrei. The LORD told Moses not to fear, and Israel struck Og down and took his land.

cards.name: Beer
cards.line: Beer, meaning "well," is the name of a well near Moab where the LORD gave Israel water, and also of a town in Judah where Jotham fled.

moments.title: The well at Beer
moments.text: Israel came to Beer, the well where the LORD told Moses to gather the people so He could give them water. Israel sang to the well, which the princes and nobles had dug.

moments.title: Jotham runs to a town called Beer
moments.text: After Jotham spoke his warning, he ran away to a place called Beer. He lived there because he feared his brother Abimelech.

cards.name: Bithynia
cards.line: Bithynia was a Roman province in Asia Minor that the Spirit of Jesus kept Paul from entering, and one of the regions where Peter's letter found Christians living in exile.

moments.title: Spirit says no to Paul
moments.text: Paul and his companions came to the border of Mysia and tried to enter Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus would not permit them. They passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.

moments.title: Peter writes to believers
moments.text: Peter addressed his letter to God's chosen people scattered across several regions, and Bithynia was one of them. He reminded them of their living hope and told them their tested faith is more precious than gold.

cards.name: Jahaz
cards.line: Jahaz was a city near the wilderness where Israel defeated King Sihon of the Amorites, and later a place named in warnings against Moab.

moments.title: Sihon fights Israel
moments.text: Sihon would not let Israel pass through his land. He gathered his whole army and came out to fight Israel at Jahaz.

moments.title: The LORD gives victory
moments.text: The LORD delivered Sihon and his army into Israel's hands at Jahaz. Israel then took the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok.

moments.title: Sihon camps at Jahaz
moments.text: Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his land. He gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz, and fought with Israel, and the LORD gave Israel the victory.

moments.title: Cries over Moab
moments.text: The prophets described the sorrow of Moab, saying the cries from Heshbon and Elealeh were heard as far as Jahaz.

cards.name: Mareshah
cards.line: Mareshah was a city in the plain of Judah, strengthened by Rehoboam and found near the battle where Asa beat Zerah's huge army.

moments.title: A city of Judah
moments.text: Mareshah is named with eight other cities, along with their villages, in the land given to the tribe of Judah.

moments.title: Rehoboam strengthens it
moments.text: Rehoboam made Mareshah and other cities in Judah and Benjamin stronger. He put officers, food supplies, shields, and spears in them.

moments.title: Asa wins near Mareshah
moments.text: Zerah the Cushite came with a huge army as far as Mareshah, and Asa lined up for battle in the Valley of Zephathah near the city. Asa cried out to the LORD, and the LORD struck down the Cushites.

moments.title: Eliezer of Mareshah
moments.text: Eliezer, a man from Mareshah, gave God's message against King Jehoshaphat for joining forces with Ahaziah. The LORD wrecked the ships, and they could not sail to Tarshish.

moments.title: A word to Mareshah
moments.text: The LORD spoke to the people living in Mareshah. He said He would again bring a conqueror against them.

cards.name: Tahpanhes
cards.line: Tahpanhes was a city in Egypt where Jewish refugees fled after Jerusalem fell, and where God gave Jeremiah a message about Babylon's coming attack.

moments.title: Refugees reach Egypt
moments.text: The people did not obey the LORD, but went into Egypt anyway. Jeremiah and Baruch went with them, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.

moments.title: Stones at Pharaoh's palace
moments.text: The LORD told Jeremiah to bury large stones in the clay pavement at the entrance to Pharaoh's palace while the Jews watched. God said Nebuchadnezzar would set his throne over those stones and strike Egypt.

moments.title: Word for Jews in Egypt
moments.text: A word from the LORD came to Jeremiah about all the Jews living in Egypt, including those in Tahpanhes. He reminded them that Jerusalem lay in ruins because of idol worship, and asked why they were harming themselves.

moments.title: A call to get ready for war
moments.text: The LORD named Tahpanhes among the Egyptian cities where the coming of Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon was to be announced. The message was to take positions and get ready, because the sword devours those around them.

cards.name: Valley of Salt
cards.line: The Valley of Salt is a valley south of the Dead Sea where Israel and Judah won great battles against Edom, under David and later under Amaziah.

moments.title: David Defeats Edom
moments.text: David made a name for himself when 18,000 Edomites were struck down in the Valley of Salt. He stationed soldiers in Edom, and the LORD made David victorious wherever he went.

moments.title: Abishai Strikes Down Edomites
moments.text: Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. All the Edomites came under David's rule.

moments.title: Amaziah's Victory Over Edom
moments.text: King Amaziah of Judah led his troops to the Valley of Salt and struck down 10,000 Edomites, the men of Seir.

cards.name: Arad
cards.line: Arad was a Canaanite city in the Negev, south of Hebron, whose king attacked Israel in the wilderness and is later listed among the kings of the land.

moments.title: Arad's king attacks Israel
moments.text: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim. He attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.

moments.title: The Kenites live near Arad
moments.text: The descendants of Moses' father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah to the Wilderness of Judah in the Negev. They settled near Arad and lived among the people.

cards.name: En-rogel
cards.line: En-rogel was a spring near Jerusalem that marked a border between Judah and Benjamin, and it was a place of secret messages and a royal feast.

moments.title: A border marker
moments.text: En-rogel is named as a point where the border of Judah ran, and it also appears in the border of Benjamin, near the southern slope of the Jebusites (Jerusalem).

moments.title: Waiting for news
moments.text: Jonathan and Ahimaaz stayed at En-rogel because they dared not be seen entering the city. A servant girl brought them news, and they passed it on to King David.

moments.title: Adonijah's feast
moments.text: Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, next to En-rogel. He invited his royal brothers and the men of Judah who served the king, but not Nathan, Benaiah, or Solomon.

cards.name: Gate of Benjamin
cards.line: The Gate of Benjamin was a gate in Jerusalem where Jeremiah was seized and arrested, and where King Zedekiah sat when Ebed-melech pleaded for Jeremiah's life.

moments.title: Jeremiah seized at the gate
moments.text: Jeremiah tried to leave Jerusalem for the land of Benjamin. At the gate, the captain of the guard accused him of deserting to the Chaldeans, and Jeremiah was arrested and put in prison.

moments.title: Ebed-melech speaks to the king
moments.text: King Zedekiah was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin when Ebed-melech told him Jeremiah had been put in a cistern. The king ordered Jeremiah pulled out before he died.

cards.name: Gibbethon
cards.line: Gibbethon was a city in the land of Dan, given to the Levites, and held by the Philistines when Israel's army camped against it.

moments.title: A city for the Levites
moments.text: Gibbethon is listed among the cities of Dan. It was later given to the Kohathite Levites, along with its pasturelands.

moments.title: Nadab struck down
moments.text: King Nadab and all Israel were surrounding Gibbethon of the Philistines to capture it. Baasha plotted against Nadab and struck him down there, then became king.

moments.title: Omri made king
moments.text: The troops were camped against Gibbethon when they heard that Zimri had killed the king. That day in the camp, all Israel proclaimed Omri, the army commander, king.

cards.name: Habor
cards.line: The Habor was a river in Gozan, in Assyria, where the king of Assyria settled Israelites after he carried them away from their land.

moments.title: Israel exiled to the Habor
moments.text: After three years, the king of Assyria captured Samaria and carried the Israelites away. He settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

moments.title: Israelites settled by the Habor again
moments.text: The king of Assyria exiled the Israelites and settled them in Gozan by the Habor River. This happened because they would not listen to the LORD and broke His covenant.

moments.title: Eastern tribes taken to Habor
moments.text: God moved Pul, the king of Assyria, to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh away from their land. Pul brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan.

cards.name: Halah
cards.line: Halah was a region in Assyria where captive Israelites were settled after Assyria conquered the northern kingdom of Israel, showing the result of Israel's unfaithfulness to God.

moments.title: Israelites settled in Halah
moments.text: After three years of siege, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. He carried the Israelites away and settled them in Halah, in Gozan by the Habor River, and in the cities of the Medes.

moments.title: Eastern tribes taken to Halah
moments.text: Because the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh were unfaithful, God stirred up the king of Assyria to take them into exile. He brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan.

cards.name: Horse Gate
cards.line: The Horse Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, where priests rebuilt the wall and where God promised the land would be holy to the LORD.

moments.title: Priests repair the wall
moments.text: When the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt, the priests made repairs above the Horse Gate. Each priest worked in front of his own house.

moments.title: A promise of a holy city
moments.text: Through Jeremiah, the LORD said the valley and fields out to the corner of the Horse Gate would be holy to the LORD. He said it would never again be uprooted or demolished.

cards.name: Ibleam
cards.line: Ibleam was a city given to the tribe of Manasseh, where Canaanites stayed on, and near where King Ahaziah of Judah was shot while fleeing Jehu.

moments.title: A city given to Manasseh
moments.text: Ibleam was one of the cities assigned to Manasseh, within the lands of Issachar and Asher. It had settlements around it.

moments.title: Canaanites not driven out
moments.text: Manasseh failed to drive out the people of Ibleam and other cities, because the Canaanites were determined to stay. When Israel grew stronger, they made the Canaanites work as forced laborers but never drove them out completely.

moments.title: Ahaziah shot near Ibleam
moments.text: King Ahaziah of Judah fled from Jehu, who shouted for his men to shoot him. They hit him in his chariot on the Ascent of Gur, near Ibleam, and he fled to Megiddo and died there.

cards.name: Zaphon
cards.line: Zaphon was a city in the valley east of the Jordan River, given to the tribe of Gad, and it was where Ephraim confronted Jephthah.

moments.title: A city for Gad
moments.text: Zaphon is listed among the valley cities in the land of Sihon king of Heshbon. This land east of the Jordan became the inheritance of the clans of Gad.

moments.title: Ephraim confronts Jephthah
moments.text: The men of Ephraim crossed the Jordan to Zaphon. They angrily asked Jephthah why he had not called them to fight the Ammonites, and they threatened to burn his house down.

cards.name: Baalah
cards.line: Baalah is the name of a city on Judah's northern border, also called Kiriath-jearim, where David went to bring up the ark of God.

moments.title: A Corner of Judah's Border
moments.text: The border of Judah's land bent around toward Baalah, also called Kiriath-jearim. From Baalah it curled west toward Mount Seir.

moments.title: A Different Baalah in the South
moments.text: A separate Baalah is listed among the cities in the south of Judah, in a list of twenty-nine cities with their villages. It is not the same place as Kiriath-jearim.

moments.title: David Goes for the Ark
moments.text: David and all Israel went up to Baalah of Judah to bring up the ark of God from there. They carried it from the house of Abinadab on a new cart.

cards.name: Bamoth-baal
cards.line: Bamoth-baal was a city in Moab where Balak brought Balaam to see Israel's camp, and later a city given to the tribe of Reuben.

moments.title: Balak brings Balaam up
moments.text: Balak took Balaam up to Bamoth-baal the morning after the sacrifices. From there Balaam could see the outskirts of Israel's camp.

moments.title: A city for Reuben
moments.text: Bamoth-baal is named among the cities of the plateau in the land of Sihon. This land became part of the inheritance of the tribe of Reuben.

cards.name: Bezek
cards.line: Bezek is the name of a city where Judah defeated the Canaanites, and sources suggest a place of the same name where Saul counted Israel's army.

moments.title: Judah wins at Bezek
moments.text: Judah attacked, and the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands. They struck down ten thousand men at Bezek and found Adoni-bezek there.

moments.title: Saul counts the army
moments.text: Saul numbered the people at Bezek. There were 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men of Judah.

cards.name: Hachilah
cards.line: Hachilah is a hill in Judah near Ziph, south of Jeshimon, where David hid from King Saul and chose to spare Saul's life.

moments.title: Saul camps on the hill
moments.text: Saul took three thousand chosen men and camped beside the road at Hachilah. David was in the wilderness and learned that Saul had followed him.

moments.title: David spares Saul
moments.text: David and Abishai went into Saul's camp at night and found him asleep with his spear stuck in the ground by his head. Abishai wanted to strike Saul, but David refused to harm the LORD's anointed.

cards.name: Jeshimon
cards.line: Jeshimon is a word for a dry, empty wilderness, probably near the Dead Sea, and in the Bible it is a landmark near where David hid from Saul.

moments.title: Saul camps at Hachilah
moments.text: The Ziphites tell Saul that David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, opposite Jeshimon. Saul brings three thousand chosen men and camps beside the road there.

moments.title: David spares Saul
moments.text: David and Abishai go into the camp at night and find Saul asleep with his spear in the ground. Abishai wants to strike Saul, but David refuses to harm the king the LORD chose.

cards.name: Joktheel
cards.line: Joktheel was a city in Judah's land, and also the new name King Amaziah gave to Sela after he took it in battle.

moments.title: A city in Judah
moments.text: Joktheel is listed among the cities given to the tribe of Judah. It is named with towns like Mizpeh and Lachish.

moments.title: Sela renamed Joktheel
moments.text: King Amaziah of Judah took Sela in battle and called it Joktheel. It still had that name when this was written.

cards.name: Mahaneh-dan
cards.line: Mahaneh-dan, meaning camp of Dan, was a place between Zorah and Eshtaol where the Spirit began to stir Samson, and it is linked to a Danite camp.

moments.title: The Spirit stirs Samson
moments.text: As Samson grew, the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

moments.title: Danites camp near Kiriath-jearim
moments.text: Six hundred armed Danites set out from Zorah and Eshtaol and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of it is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.

cards.name: Mount Gilead
cards.line: Mount Gilead is the mountain where Gideon's men were when the LORD began shrinking his army, so Israel would know the victory came from Him.

moments.title: The fearful turn back
moments.text: The LORD told Gideon he had too many men, so that Israel would not boast that their own hand had saved them. Gideon announced that anyone fearful could leave Mount Gilead, and twenty-two thousand turned back, leaving ten thousand.

cards.name: New Gate
cards.line: The New Gate was an entrance of the LORD's house in Jerusalem, where officials judged Jeremiah and where Baruch read out Jeremiah's words to the people.

moments.title: Jeremiah on trial
moments.text: Officials sat at the entrance of the New Gate. The priests and prophets wanted Jeremiah put to death, but the officials and people said he had spoken in the LORD's name.

moments.title: Baruch reads the scroll
moments.text: On a day of fasting, Baruch read Jeremiah's words from the scroll to all the people at the opening of the New Gate. Later the officials heard it read too, and they were afraid.

cards.name: Pas-dammim
cards.line: Pas-dammim was a place where Israel and the Philistines fought fierce battles, and where David and Eleazar won a great victory when the troops fled.

moments.title: Victory in the barley field
moments.text: The Philistines gathered at Pas-dammim for battle, and the troops fled from them. Eleazar and David stood in the middle of a barley field and defended it, and the LORD brought about a great victory.

cards.name: Perez-uzzah
cards.line: Perez-uzzah is a place named by David after God struck down Uzzah beside the ark, and its name is given as "the breach of Uzzah."

moments.title: Uzzah dies by the ark
moments.text: God's anger burned against Uzzah for his disrespect, and He struck him down beside the ark of God. Uzzah died there.

moments.title: David names the place
moments.text: David became angry that the LORD had burst forth against Uzzah, so he named the place Perez-uzzah. The writer says it was called that when the account was written.

moments.title: David fears the LORD
moments.text: That day David feared the LORD and asked how the ark of the LORD could ever come to him.

cards.name: Tob
cards.line: Tob was a land east of the Jordan where Jephthah took refuge after his brothers drove him out, and where Gilead's elders later came to call him back.

moments.title: Jephthah flees to Tob
moments.text: Jephthah's brothers drove him out of his father's house. He fled and settled in the land of Tob, where worthless men gathered around him and traveled with him.

moments.title: The elders call Jephthah back
moments.text: When the Ammonites made war on Israel, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah from Tob. They asked him to be their commander, and he agreed to go with them.

cards.name: Valley of Slaughter
cards.line: The Valley of Slaughter is the new name God says will replace Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, a place of child burning, to show coming judgment on Judah.

moments.title: A new name for Topheth
moments.text: God says people built high places at Topheth to burn their sons and daughters, something He never commanded. He says the place will be called the Valley of Slaughter, and they will bury the dead there until there is no more room.

moments.title: Judgment named again
moments.text: God again says Topheth will be called the Valley of Slaughter. He says He will ruin the plans of Judah and Jerusalem there, and they will fall by the sword before their enemies.

moments.title: The jar is shattered
moments.text: God tells Jeremiah to shatter a jar in front of the men with him. It shows that God will shatter the nation and city, and make Jerusalem like Topheth.

cards.name: Zela
cards.line: Zela was a town in the land of Benjamin where Saul and Jonathan were buried in the family tomb of Saul's father Kish.

moments.title: A city of Benjamin
moments.text: Zelah is named in the list of fourteen cities given to the tribe of Benjamin as their inheritance, along with Jerusalem and Gibeah.

moments.title: Saul and Jonathan are buried
moments.text: David had the bones of Saul and Jonathan brought and buried in Zela, in the tomb of Saul's father Kish. After the king's orders were done, God answered the prayers for the land.

cards.name: Zemaraim
cards.line: Zemaraim was a city in the land given to the tribe of Benjamin, listed among the towns of their inheritance in Joshua.

moments.title: A city of Benjamin
moments.text: Zemaraim is named among the twelve cities, with their villages, in the first group of towns given to the clans of the tribe of Benjamin. It sits in the list between Beth-arabah and Bethel.

cards.name: Antipatris
cards.line: Antipatris was a Roman road city that Herod the Great named for his father, and it is where soldiers stopped overnight with Paul on the way to Caesarea.

moments.title: Paul brought by night
moments.text: Soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul to Antipatris by night. The next day the horsemen went on with him to Caesarea, while the soldiers returned to the barracks.

cards.name: Appii Forum
cards.line: Appii Forum was a market town on the Appian Way, 43 miles from Rome, where Roman believers met Paul as he came to the city.

moments.title: Brothers meet Paul
moments.text: Believers from Rome had heard about Paul and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius to meet him. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God.

cards.name: Ariel
cards.line: Ariel is a symbolic name for Jerusalem, the city where David camped, which God warns of trouble and then promises to save from its enemies.

moments.title: Trouble for Ariel
moments.text: God says trouble is coming to Ariel, the city where David camped. He will bring her low with mourning and sadness, and she will be like an altar hearth before Him.

moments.title: Enemies Like a Dream
moments.text: The LORD of Hosts comes with thunder, earthquake, and fire. The many nations that attack Ariel will be like a dream, a vision in the night.

cards.name: Assos
cards.line: Assos was a sea-port city in Mysia where Paul, who had walked there, boarded the ship with his traveling companions on his way toward Jerusalem.

moments.title: Paul meets the ship
moments.text: Paul's traveling companions sailed ahead to Assos to pick him up, since he planned to go there on foot. When he met them at Assos, they took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.

cards.name: Baal-hazor
cards.line: Baal-hazor was a place near Ephraim where Absalom held a sheepshearing feast and had his brother Amnon killed, a dark turning point in David's family.

moments.title: Absalom invites the king's sons
moments.text: Two years after Amnon wronged Tamar, Absalom held a sheepshearing at Baal-hazor and invited the king and his sons. David would not go, but he blessed Absalom.

moments.title: Amnon is struck down
moments.text: Absalom urged David until he sent Amnon and the other sons. Absalom's young men killed Amnon as ordered, and the other sons fled on their mules.

cards.name: Baal-shalishah
cards.line: Baal-shalishah was a city in Israel, and it is where a man came from who brought Elisha twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain.

moments.title: A man brings first-grain bread
moments.text: A man from Baal-shalishah came to the man of God with twenty loaves of barley bread from the first ripe grain. Elisha said to give it to the people, and by the word of the LORD they ate and had some left over.

cards.name: Baale-judah
cards.line: Baale-judah was a city in Judah where the ark of God was kept, and David went there to bring the ark up to Jerusalem.

moments.title: David goes for the ark
moments.text: David gathered thirty thousand chosen men of Israel and set out for Baale of Judah. They went to bring up the ark of God, which is called by the name of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.name: Beth-barah
cards.line: Beth-barah was a landmark by the Jordan River, the point to which Ephraim's men seized the waters to block the fleeing Midianites after Gideon's victory.

moments.title: Ephraim seizes the Jordan
moments.text: Gideon sent messengers to the hill country of Ephraim to call the men down. They captured the waters of the Jordan as far as Beth-barah, ahead of the Midianites.

cards.name: Beth-eked
cards.line: Beth-eked of the Shepherds was a place on Jehu's road to Samaria, where he met relatives of King Ahaziah of Judah, who were killed at its well.

moments.title: Jehu meets Ahaziah's relatives
moments.text: On his way to Samaria, Jehu met some relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah at Beth-eked of the Shepherds. They said they had come to greet the sons of the king and of the queen mother.

moments.title: Forty-two men killed at the well
moments.text: Jehu ordered his men to take the relatives alive. They killed all forty-two men at the well of Beth-eked, and none were spared.

cards.name: Beth-maacah
cards.line: Beth-maacah, also called Abel-beth-maacah, was a strong northern city in Naphtali, called a "mother in Israel," where Joab chased the rebel Sheba.

moments.title: Sheba runs to the city
moments.text: Sheba went through all the tribes of Israel to Abel-beth-maacah, and the Berites gathered and followed him. Joab's troops came and surrounded the city, building a ramp and battering the wall to knock it down.

moments.title: The wise woman speaks
moments.text: A wise woman called from the city and asked Joab to come talk. She said she was one of the peaceful and faithful in Israel, called the city a "mother in Israel," and asked why he would swallow up the LORD's people.

moments.title: A promise about Sheba
moments.text: Joab said he only wanted Sheba, who had rebelled against King David. The woman promised that Sheba's head would be thrown to him over the wall.

cards.name: Bozez
cards.line: Bozez was one of two cliffs beside a pass between Geba and Michmash, the way Jonathan meant to cross to reach a Philistine outpost.

moments.title: Cliff beside Jonathan's pass
moments.text: Jonathan planned to cross a pass to reach the Philistine outpost. Bozez was the name of the cliff on one side, and Seneh was the cliff on the other.

cards.name: Dalmanutha
cards.line: Dalmanutha was a lakeside place near Magdala, on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus landed by boat and the Pharisees tested Him.

moments.title: Jesus comes by boat
moments.text: After sending the crowd away, Jesus got into the boat with His disciples. They went to the district of Dalmanutha.

moments.title: Pharisees demand a sign
moments.text: The Pharisees argued with Jesus and tested Him by asking for a sign from heaven. Jesus sighed deeply and said no sign would be given to this generation, then left them.

cards.name: El-elohe-Israel
cards.line: El-Elohe-Israel is the name Jacob gave to an altar he set up near Shechem on land he bought, and Schaff's Dictionary says it means "strength of God."

moments.title: Jacob buys the land
moments.text: Jacob bought the plot of ground where he had pitched his tent. He paid the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, a hundred pieces of silver.

moments.title: An altar is set up
moments.text: There Jacob set up an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.

cards.name: En-hakkore
cards.line: En-hakkore is a spring in Lehi that God opened for thirsty Samson, and its name, "fountain of the crier," recalls the cry he made to God.

moments.title: Water for thirsty Samson
moments.text: Samson was very thirsty and cried out to the LORD, asking if he must now die of thirst. God opened up the hollow place in Lehi, and water came out, and when Samson drank, his strength returned and he was revived.

moments.title: A spring with a name
moments.text: Samson named the spring En-hakkore because of what happened there. The verse says it remains in Lehi to this day.

cards.name: Enaim
cards.line: Enaim was a city on the road to Timnah, where Tamar sat by the entrance and met Judah in a story that shaped his family.

moments.title: Tamar waits at the entrance
moments.text: Tamar took off her widow's clothes, covered her face with a veil, and sat at the entrance to Enaim. She saw that Shelah had grown up but had not been given to her as a husband.

moments.title: Hirah searches for the woman
moments.text: Hirah took a young goat to get back Judah's items and asked the men at Enaim about the woman by the road. They said no shrine prostitute had been there.

cards.name: Esek
cards.line: Esek was a well in the valley of Gerar that Isaac's servants dug, and its name, meaning quarrel, recalls the argument over the water there.

moments.title: A well named for a quarrel
moments.text: Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh water. The herdsmen of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen and said the water was theirs, so Isaac named the well Esek, because they argued with him.

cards.name: Gibeath-elohim
cards.line: Gibeath-elohim, or Gibeah of God, is a city with a Philistine outpost where Saul met a group of prophets and the Spirit of God came upon him.

moments.title: Saul prophesies with the prophets
moments.text: When Saul and his servant arrive at Gibeah, a group of prophets meets him. The Spirit of God rushes upon Saul, and he prophesies along with them, so people who knew him ask, "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

cards.name: Gibeath-haaraloth
cards.line: Gibeath-haaraloth is a city where Joshua circumcised the sons of Israel at the LORD's command, after the men of war from Egypt had died.

moments.title: Joshua circumcises Israel's sons
moments.text: At the LORD's command, Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the sons of Israel at Gibeath-haaraloth. These were the sons born in the wilderness.

cards.name: Harosheth-hagoyim
cards.line: Harosheth-hagoyim was the city where Sisera, commander of King Jabin's army, lived, and his iron chariots set out from here to fight Israel.

moments.title: Home of Sisera
moments.text: The LORD sold Israel into the hand of Jabin, king of Canaan. His army commander, Sisera, lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

moments.title: The chariots gather
moments.text: When Sisera heard that Barak had gone up Mount Tabor, he called out all nine hundred iron chariots and his men. They went from Harosheth-hagoyim to the River Kishon.

cards.name: Helam
cards.line: Helam was a place east of the Jordan where the Arameans gathered for battle and where David defeated them, which ended their help to the Ammonites.

moments.title: Arameans gather at Helam
moments.text: Hadadezer sent for more Arameans from beyond the Euphrates. They came to Helam with Shobach, the commander of his army, leading them.

moments.title: David fights at Helam
moments.text: When David heard the news, he gathered all Israel and crossed the Jordan to Helam, where the Arameans fought him and then fled. Shobach their commander died there, and the kings under Hadadezer made peace with Israel.

cards.name: Helkath-hazzurim
cards.line: Helkath-hazzurim was a spot in Gibeon named for a deadly fight between twelve men of David and twelve men of Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.

moments.title: The twelve against twelve
moments.text: Twelve men for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth and twelve for David were counted off. Each man grabbed his opponent and thrust his sword into his side, and they all fell together, so the place in Gibeon was called Helkath-hazzurim.

cards.name: Hereth
cards.line: Hereth was a forest in the land of Judah where David went to hide from King Saul after the prophet Gad told him to leave the stronghold.

moments.title: David goes to Hereth
moments.text: The prophet Gad told David not to stay in the stronghold but to go into the land of Judah. So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.

cards.name: Hobah
cards.line: Hobah was a place north of Damascus, the farthest point to which Abram chased the enemy kings after they captured his relative Lot.

moments.title: Abram chases the kings to Hobah
moments.text: After Abram heard that Lot was captured, he set out with his trained men. He defeated Chedorlaomer's army during the night and chased them as far as Hobah, north of Damascus.

cards.name: Jegar-sahadutha
cards.line: Jegar-sahadutha is the name Laban gave to a mound of stones, meaning "heap of testimony," that marked a promise between him and Jacob.

moments.title: A mound of stones
moments.text: Jacob's relatives gathered stones and made a mound, and they ate there by it. Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.

moments.title: A witness between them
moments.text: Laban said the mound was a witness that neither man would go past it to harm the other. Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

cards.name: Karkor
cards.line: Karkor was a place east of the Jordan where the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna were with their army, and where Gideon defeated them.

moments.title: Midian's last army at Karkor
moments.text: Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men. These were all that were left of the armies of the people of the east, after 120,000 swordsmen had already fallen.

cards.name: Mount Zemaraim
cards.line: Mount Zemaraim was a mountain in the hill country of Ephraim, where King Abijah of Judah spoke to Jeroboam and Israel before their great battle.

moments.title: Abijah speaks from the mountain
moments.text: Abijah stood on Mount Zemaraim and called out to Jeroboam and all Israel. He reminded them that the LORD gave the kingship to David's descendants, that Jeroboam had rebelled, and that Judah had not turned away from the LORD.

cards.name: Puteoli
cards.line: Puteoli was a busy port city on the coast of Italy where Paul landed as a prisoner and met believers on his way to Rome.

moments.title: Paul lands in Italy
moments.text: After a south wind came up, Paul and his companions sailed on the second day and arrived at Puteoli.

moments.title: A week with the brothers
moments.text: At Puteoli, Paul found some brothers who invited them to stay a week. After that, they went on to Rome.

cards.name: Ramath-lehi
cards.line: Ramath-lehi is the place Samson named after he struck down a thousand Philistines with a donkey's jawbone, a victory he credited to God's deliverance.

moments.title: Samson names the place
moments.text: After Samson says he has killed a thousand men with a donkey's jawbone, he throws the jawbone away. He names the place Ramath-lehi.

cards.name: Ramathaim-zophim
cards.line: Ramathaim-zophim was a city in the hill country of Ephraim, and it was the hometown of Elkanah, the husband of Hannah, in the story that begins 1 Samuel.

moments.title: Elkanah's hometown
moments.text: 1 Samuel begins by telling us that Elkanah, an Ephraimite, was from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim. His family line is listed back through Jeroham, Elihu, Tohu, and Zuph.

cards.name: Rocks
cards.line: The Rocks of the Wild Goats was a region near En-gedi where Saul went looking for David with three thousand chosen men.

moments.title: Saul Hunts for David
moments.text: Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel. He went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

cards.name: Salim
cards.line: Salim was a town near Aenon, where John the Baptist was baptizing people near plentiful water, and it is named to show where Aenon was.

moments.title: John baptizes near Salim
moments.text: John was baptizing at Aenon near Salim because the water was plentiful there. People kept coming to be baptized.

cards.name: Rock of Escape
cards.line: The Rock of Escape, called Sela-hammahlekoth, was a mountain place in the wilderness where Saul stopped chasing David because of a Philistine attack.

moments.title: Saul closes in on David
moments.text: David went down to the rock in the Wilderness of Maon, and Saul pursued him there. Saul and his men were on one side of the mountain and David and his men on the other, and Saul was closing in to capture them.

moments.title: Saul turns away
moments.text: A messenger told Saul that the Philistines had raided the land, so Saul broke off his pursuit of David. That is why the place is called Sela-hammahlekoth.

cards.name: Seleucia
cards.line: Seleucia was a seaport city near Antioch on the Mediterranean coast, where Barnabas and Saul set sail on the first missionary journey.

moments.title: Sent out by the Spirit
moments.text: After the church fasted and prayed, Barnabas and Saul were sent forth by the Holy Spirit. They went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.

cards.name: Shen
cards.line: Shen was a place near Mizpah, possibly named for a tooth-shaped rock, and Samuel set up the Ebenezer stone between it and Mizpah to remember God's help.

moments.title: The Ebenezer stone
moments.text: After Israel chased the Philistines away, Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer and said, "Thus far the LORD has helped us."

cards.name: Sitnah
cards.line: Sitnah was a well Isaac's servants dug in the valley of Gerar, and its name means strife because people quarreled over it.

moments.title: A second well, a second fight
moments.text: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the herdsmen of Gerar quarreled over this one too. So Isaac named it Sitnah.

cards.name: Ulai
cards.line: The Ulai was a canal or river near the city of Susa, where Daniel stood in a vision and saw a ram and a goat.

moments.title: Daniel's vision by the canal
moments.text: Daniel saw himself in Susa, beside the Ulai Canal. There he saw a two-horned ram standing by the canal, and a goat with one big horn came and struck the ram down.

moments.title: A voice from the Ulai
moments.text: Daniel heard a man's voice calling from between the banks of the Ulai, telling Gabriel to explain the vision. Gabriel said the ram stood for the kings of Media and Persia, and the goat for the king of Greece.

cards.name: Valley of Gerar
cards.line: The Valley of Gerar is a valley where Isaac settled after Abimelech sent him away, and where his servants reopened old wells and dug new ones.

moments.title: Isaac settles in the valley
moments.text: Abimelech told Isaac to leave because he was too powerful. Isaac left and camped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.

moments.title: Old wells reopened
moments.text: Isaac reopened the wells that had been dug in the days of his father Abraham, which the Philistines had stopped up. He gave them the same names his father had given.

moments.title: Quarrels over wells
moments.text: Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found a well of fresh water, but the herdsmen of Gerar said the water was theirs. Isaac named the wells Esek and Sitnah because of the quarrels.

cards.name: Valley of Hamongog
cards.line: The Valley of Hamon-gog is a burial valley in Israel, east of the Sea, where God says Gog and all his hordes will be buried after He defeats them.

moments.title: A burial place for Gog
moments.text: God says He will give Gog a burial place in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the Sea. Gog and all his hordes will be buried there, so it will be called the Valley of Hamon-gog.

moments.title: Cleansing the land
moments.text: God says men will be employed to pass through the land and bury the invaders who remain. Anyone who sees a human bone will set up a pillar next to it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.

cards.name: Valley of Zephathah
cards.line: The Valley of Zephathah, near Mareshah, is where King Asa of Judah faced a huge Cushite army and saw the LORD give Judah the victory.

moments.title: Asa lines up for battle
moments.text: Zerah the Cushite came against Judah with an army of 1,000,000 men and 300 chariots. Asa marched out and lined up his army in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

moments.title: Asa cries out to the LORD
moments.text: Asa prayed that no one but the LORD can help the powerless against the mighty. He asked for help because Judah relied on Him.

moments.title: The LORD defeats the Cushites
moments.text: The LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and Judah, and the Cushites fled.

cards.name: Zephath
cards.line: Zephath was a Canaanite city whose name means "watch-tower," and after Judah and Simeon completely destroyed it, it was renamed Hormah.

moments.title: Judah and Simeon attack Zephath
moments.text: The men of Judah went with their brothers the Simeonites and attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath. They completely destroyed the city, and it was called Hormah.

cards.name: Zophim
cards.line: Zophim was a field on top of Pisgah in Moab, where Balak took Balaam to curse Israel, but God turned the words into a blessing.

moments.title: Seven altars on Pisgah
moments.text: Balak took Balaam to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah. There he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each one.

moments.title: God gives Balaam a message
moments.text: Balaam went off to meet the LORD, and the LORD put a message in his mouth. Balaam told Balak that God does not lie or change His mind, and that he had received a command to bless.

cards.name: Gedor
cards.line: Gedor was the name of a city in Judah's hill country, and the Bible may use it for other places too, including one where Simeonites sought pasture.

moments.title: A city of Judah
moments.text: When the land was divided, Gedor was named with Halhul and Beth-zur among the cities given to the descendants of Judah, along with its villages.

moments.title: Pasture near Gedor
moments.text: In the days of Hezekiah, Simeonite families grew large and traveled to the entrance of Gedor to find pasture for their flocks. They found rich, good land, attacked the Hamites and Meunites living there, devoted them to destruction, and settled in their place.

moments.title: Men from Gedor
moments.text: Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor, are listed among the men who came to David. Gedor here may be a different place from the others.

cards.name: Geruth Chimham
cards.line: Geruth Chimham was a place near Bethlehem where survivors from Judah stayed, afraid of Babylon, on their way to Egypt.

moments.title: Stopping on the way to Egypt
moments.text: Johanan and the commanders led the people who were left to Geruth Chimham, near Bethlehem. They planned to go on to Egypt to escape the Chaldeans, because they were afraid after Gedaliah was killed.

cards.name: Gob
cards.line: Gob was a place where Israel fought the Philistines in David's time, and where two of David's warriors defeated mighty descendants of Rapha.

moments.title: Sibbecai defeats Saph
moments.text: At Gob there was a battle with the Philistines. Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, a descendant of Rapha.

moments.title: Elhanan and Goliath's brother
moments.text: Another battle with the Philistines took place at Gob. Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.

cards.name: Hamath-zobah
cards.line: Hamath-zobah is a place that King Solomon went to and captured, and its exact location is not known today.

moments.title: Solomon captures Hamath-zobah
moments.text: Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and captured it. The verses name it only briefly, and the Bible does not say more about what happened there.

cards.name: Seirah
cards.line: Seirah was a wooded region in the hill country of Ephraim where Ehud fled after killing King Eglon and then gathered Israel to fight Moab.

moments.title: Ehud escapes to Seirah
moments.text: While Eglon's servants waited outside the locked doors, Ehud got away. He passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.

moments.title: Ehud blows the ram's horn
moments.text: On arriving in Seirah, Ehud blew the ram's horn throughout the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites came down with him, and he became their leader.

cards.name: Seneh
cards.line: Seneh was a sharp cliff on one side of a pass near Michmash, where Jonathan set out to face a Philistine outpost trusting the LORD.

moments.title: Cliffs beside the pass
moments.text: Jonathan planned to cross a pass to reach the Philistine outpost, with cliffs on both sides named Bozez and Seneh. Seneh was the southern one, facing Geba.

cards.name: Serpent's Stone
cards.line: The Serpent's Stone was a rocky plateau near the spring En-rogel, where Adonijah held a feast to make himself king, though David had sworn Solomon would reign.

moments.title: Adonijah's feast
moments.text: Adonijah offered sheep, oxen, and fattened calves near the stone of Zoheleth, next to En-rogel. He invited his royal brothers and the men of Judah who served the king, but not Nathan, Benaiah, the mighty men, or Solomon.

cards.name: Zair
cards.line: Zair was a place, probably near Edom, where King Jehoram of Judah went to fight the Edomites after they rebelled against Judah.

moments.title: Jehoram at Zair
moments.text: After Edom rebelled and chose its own king, Jehoram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him, and he rose up and attacked by night, but his troops fled to their homes.
